# Backlog

## ✅ [live-trading][security] Fixed 2026-08-18 — RETL top-up sizing incident: `starting_notional_override` missing from both pending-buy snapshot tuples, plus a silent tolerance-band blind spot in `_reconcile_fill`'s coverage logging
**Real incident, 2026-08-17**: RETL (wl_id=143) missed a real ~$20/2-share post-fill top-up with ZERO trace anywhere — no Slack alert, no `coverage_events` row. Root cause: `signals_db._PENDING_BUY_NODE_KEYS` (~line 3495) was missing `'starting_notional_override'`, a per-node sizing override that `signals_helpers._last_sale_recovery` checks FIRST. Since `pending_buys.node_json` snapshots this tuple's fields at ORDER-PLACEMENT time (a trailing-buy can rest for days before filling), a resting order's snapshot never carried the override, so `_reconcile_fill`'s post-fill top-up calc silently used a wrong, stale fallback target notional. The fill happened to land within `_reconcile_fill`'s ±1-share tolerance band, which additionally had NO logging path at all (`if delta > fill_price: ... elif delta < -fill_price: ...` with no `else`) — a benign-looking near-miss on a wrong target left no evidence either.

**Fix (this session, applying findings CONFIRMED by an already-completed paired review — independent-cold + contextual Opus, with rebuttal exchange)**:
1. Added `'starting_notional_override'` to `_PENDING_BUY_NODE_KEYS` (`signals_db.py` ~line 3495-3498). New regression test `tests/test_pending_buy_snapshot_starting_notional_override.py` verified by both reviewers to genuinely fail red pre-fix / pass green post-fix, reproducing the real RETL numbers.
2. **[HIGH, confirmed]** Fixed a SEPARATE, hand-duplicated 16-field node-snapshot tuple in `signals_blocks.py` (~line 370-374) — used to build the BUY alert's Slack button payload — which had the exact same bug, also missing `starting_notional_override`. Real exposure: `signals_handlers.handle_entry_price` reads this snapshot to size a manually-confirmed market-buy entry's share count (`TrailingExitZScoreBreakout` automation-scoped tickers). Both reviewers confirmed the field addition is safe for Slack's payload size limit (real payloads measured at 432-553 chars vs. the 2000-char limit).
3. **[MEDIUM, confirmed]** Added an `else` branch to `signals_notify._reconcile_fill`'s top-up delta check, logging `coverage_events(scenario_key='top_up', result='within_tolerance', ...)` for any fill landing inside the tolerance band — closing the exact silent-gap shape that let the RETL miss go untraced. Checked `scripts/coverage_registry.py`'s `post_fill_topup` row (`bad_results=['blocked', 'failed_unexpectedly', 'db_update_failed_after_real_order', 'overspent_no_corrective_sell']`) — `within_tolerance` is a benign/expected outcome and correctly does NOT need to be added there; the existing row already handles it (an allowlist of bad outcomes, not a denylist needing every new result added).
4. **[LOW, confirmed]** Fixed a stale docstring on `signals_db.add_paper_pending_buy` (~line 3786) that claimed paper snapshots "keep starting_notional (unlike the real pending_buys node subset)" — already wrong before this session (`_PAPER_PENDING_BUY_NODE_KEYS = _PENDING_BUY_NODE_KEYS` is a direct alias, not a separate subset) and now doubly wrong given fix #1.

**Explicitly deferred (per the paired review, written up as new `docs/backlog_cache.md` items dated 2026-08-18, not built this session)**: the drought-overlay `_pct_override` triplet has the identical missing-tuple-field bug PLUS the real fill path never calls the resolver that would read those keys at all (worse in kind — sits on the SL/arm/trailing-stop trigger-percentage path, not just sizing; latent today, zero live nodes set these columns); pinning `target_notional` into `pending_buys` at placement time (structural fix for the broader frozen-vs-live sizing-basis question); unifying the two node-snapshot tuples behind one shared constant + a subset-assertion test (tier 2, prevents this exact bug shape recurring a third time).

Full suite passed; `scripts/live_sim_harness.py` 7/7 scenarios passed.

## ✅ [live-trading] Fixed 2026-08-17 — the 5 remaining ungated per-position `_post_message` clusters in `signals_notify.py`
Follow-on to the same night's core alert-gating pass (which threaded `node_id=`/`incident=True` through the ~17 UNPROTECTED/reconciliation/placement-failure/market-buy-rejected alerts). A sweep of all 95 `_post_message` call sites had found 5 more clusters with `node`/`pos`/`leg`/`wl_id` right there in scope and no gate at all — noise/consistency, not a safety bug, since an ungated call always sends.

**What was gated (37 sites: 21 `incident=True`, 1 conditionally so, 15 plain `node_id=`).** `incident=True` (the permissive `effectively_dry_run` gate — stays visible on the small `soxl_ira` real-money nodes, whose errors are deliberate early-warning signal) for error/anomaly/failure alerts; plain `node_id=` (the stricter `should_alert_live`/$5k gate) for routine lifecycle notices.
- **add-on leg** — `check_addon_trigger_real` (6: non-margin skip, dry_run_sim synthesis, placement failure, leg order placed, unconfirmed fill, leg filled), `check_addon_leg_reconciliation` (3: abandoned-entry timeout, leg stop filled via reconciliation, orphaned leg), `close_addon_leg_real_if_open` (4: unrecognized account, exit SELL failed, exit placed unconfirmed, leg closed). All keyed `leg.get('wl_id')`/`pos.get('wl_id')` — `addon_legs.wl_id` is `NOT NULL` and copied from the parent position at creation, so the two are the same node by construction (verified by both reviewers).
- **drought-HANDOFF** — `check_drought_handoff` (7), all keyed `wl_id` (= the live `node['id']` the function is called with).
- **`_reconcile_fill` top-up** — 5 sites, keyed `node.get('id')`.
- **`check_gap_resize`** — 6 of 7 sites, keyed `node.get('id')`.
- **auto-detected-fill notices** — `check_own_sell_fills`, `check_sl_order_fills` (2), `check_auto_fills`, plus `_reconcile_buy_fill`'s resolved-node fill notice.

**Deliberately left ungated (4 sites), with the reasoning written at each site.** `check_gap_resize`'s "pending buy has no account on file" alert — it fires *precisely because* the pinned `pending_buys` snapshot has no account, so gating it would have `_post_message` re-resolve the LIVE `watch_list` row and potentially silence an alert whose entire subject is that this resting order's attribution is broken; identical reasoning to `_throttled_entry_abandon_alert`'s existing exemption, and both paired reviewers converged on this exact call site independently. Plus `_reconcile_buy_fill`'s three orphan/ambiguity alerts (no pending row at all / the `wl_id` hint matched nothing / several rows matched) — each fires when node attribution is unreliable by construction, so gating on a guessed node could hide a real unattributed fill; both reviewers judged this well-reasoned rather than a rationalization.

**Paired review (independent-cold + contextual Opus, with rebuttal exchange): no CRITICAL, no HIGH from either.** Neither found a wrong-node bug (both read every enclosing function) nor a newly-silenced alert on any node at or above the $5k `CAPITAL_AT_STAKE_THRESHOLD`. Confirmed findings, all fixed:
1. **`check_auto_fills`' SELL loop had no `log_coverage_event` at all** (cold reviewer; rated the best finding of the set in rebuttal) — the one newly-gated site whose branch logged nothing, so a suppressed real exit fill on a sub-threshold live node would have left only a `trade_log` row, violating `should_alert_live`'s own docstring contract that every caller keeps its coverage logging unconditional. Added, with a **distinct** `result='closed_via_auto_fills'` rather than the siblings' shared `'closed'` (rebuttal point: `compute_status` aggregates by `(mode, result)` and never reads `detail`, so reusing `'closed'` would let this opt-in path count as proof of the always-on ones — the same defect a 2026-08-14 audit already fixed in `check_sl_order_fills`).
2. **`notify_limit_fill` was genuinely ungated** with no function-level gate either — surfaced by the new audit script, missed by both reviewers' first passes, confirmed in rebuttal. Now gated.
3. **`check_addon_leg_reconciliation`'s "cancelled, marked abandoned" message could claim a cancel that was never attempted** (contextual reviewer; cold reviewer called it the best catch independent of gating) — the cancel block only runs when the account is recognized and not effectively dry-run, so a demoted node could reach the message with a real `entry_order_id` still live. Fixed with the same `did_cancel` flag pattern `check_entry_abandon` already uses, and the not-cancelled case now alerts `incident=True`.
4. **Audit-script false positives** — the first version reported 19 ungated candidates, essentially all false (function-level `has_capital_at_stake` gates it couldn't see, plus function-keyed exemptions that would also have excused future ungated calls). Rewritten: structural FN-GATED detection, `(function, message-marker)`-keyed exemptions, widened variable-name set, and `--strict` instead of an unconditional exit 1. Now reports 0 unclassified candidates.
Also recorded (not behaviour changes): the entry-vs-exit `incident` asymmetry both reviewers asked to have written down (an unconfirmed *entry* leaves a filled margin leg with no D3 stop; an unconfirmed *exit* has its order id persisted and a real reconciliation path), and `incident=True` on the add-on leg's protective-stop-filled-while-parent-open notice (a real lockstep divergence, not routine).

**Handed to the separate pinned-anchor workstream, not fixed here** (both reviewers rated MEDIUM, both agreed it is that item's scope): `check_gap_resize` and `_reconcile_fill` place their real orders off the pinned `pending['node']` snapshot while their alerts re-resolve the live row, so a node demoted mid-flight could have alerts suppressed for an order that was nonetheless really submitted. Mitigated today by `coverage_events` firing unconditionally at every one of those sites and the suppressed text still landing in `slack_message_log`. The reviewers noted the fix shape already exists in-file (`check_buy_reminders` gates on `has_capital_at_stake(pending['node'])` — the pinned dict directly) and that `addon_legs` carries its own `account`/`is_dry_run_sim` columns for the same anchoring.

**New**: `scripts/audit_post_message_gating.py` (re-runnable classifier for every `_post_message` site: gated / gated+incident / function-level-gated / deliberate / system-wide / unclassified candidate) and `tests/test_post_message_gate_call_sites.py` (16 tests — behavioural coverage of all 5 clusters driving the real production functions with a recording double, plus two structural backstops so a new ungated per-position alert fails a test instead of silently re-opening this item). Both reviewers independently confirmed the behavioural tests are real, not trivial (removing either kwarg fails them).

**Process notes.** The `incident=` kwarg added by the earlier core pass had broken `tests/conftest.py`'s autouse anti-Slack-leak double (it enumerated `_post_message`'s parameters by name, so `incident=True` raised `TypeError` out of production `except` handlers in 8 fake_broker tests) — found by the cold reviewer, and independently fixed upstream in the main checkout the same evening; the follow-on diff did not itself carry that fix. ## ✅ [live-trading] Fixed 2026-08-17 — `incident=True`'s `effectively_dry_run` gate went dark on a demoted node / stopped account that still held a real position or a real resting order

**Original gap.** `signals_blocks._post_message(incident=True)` suppressed whenever `effectively_dry_run(account, node)` was True — i.e. `node['state'] != 'live'` OR the account's `trading_enabled=False`. Both halves are re-derived from CURRENT config at alert time. So a node demoted to `paper`/`dry_run`, or an account deliberately stopped, while an `is_dry_run_sim=0` position and real resting broker orders remained, would silence exactly that position's UNPROTECTED/reconciliation alerts — at the moment a human had just intervened and most needed visibility. Verified 2026-08-17 against `cache/live/trading_live.db`: not live at the time (all 3 real positions sat on `state='live'` nodes in a `trading_enabled=True` account), latent but real.

**The fix — anchor every incident alert to something PINNED, never to current config.** Three anchors, in precedence order, all resolved inside `_post_message`:
1. `real_order=True` (strongest) — the caller has already proven a real broker order exists (it holds a real `order_id` it is actively querying). Suppression is skipped outright.
2. `pos=` — gate on `bool(pos.get('is_dry_run_sim'))`, the ground truth stamped at ENTRY time. A position that was real when opened does not retroactively become synthetic because someone changed config afterwards. Truthiness rather than `== 0` so a dict missing the key fails OPEN (sends), matching the block's existing fail-open contract. Also carries `or pos.get('origin') == 'paper'` as a pure API guard (unreachable today; kept because `build_reference_table` merges both books into one wl_id-keyed dict and destroys the table-of-origin signal).
3. `node=` — the caller's own in-hand/pinned node dict, used INSTEAD of re-resolving `node_id` from the DB.
16 position-keyed sites pass `pos=` (`_attempt_automated_sell`, `_attempt_automated_exit_sell`, `_verify_resting_before_replace` ×6, `_alert_reconcile_mismatch`, `alert_stale_price_exit_suppressed`, `_place_stop_loss_for_position` ×3, `_place_stop_loss_for_addon_leg` via `parent_pos`); 6 order/placement-keyed sites pass `node=`, 3 of those also `real_order=True`.

**Two upgrades that came from the paired review, not the original scope.**
- *`check_market_buy_rejected` was misclassified.* The original scope (and `_post_message`'s first docstring) claimed these three alerts had "no pinned position to anchor to, so the current node/account genuinely IS the only available truth." False: the loop reads `node = pb['node']` — the frozen `pending_buys.node_json` snapshot — and gates its own "is there a real broker order here" decision on it, then `_post_message` re-resolved the node fresh and could disagree. Loop says "real order, worth polling"; gate says "synthetic, suppress"; gate wins. Unlike the placement-attempt sites (which alert milliseconds after their own attempt, no staleness window), this function polls a resting order across cycles and days. Its partial-fill branch is the worst case: real executed shares at the broker, no stop, no local position row, alerting "tracking PRESERVED... a protective stop may be needed". The cold reviewer noted the codebase already contained the precedent — `_throttled_entry_abandon_alert` was deliberately left UNGATED with a comment saying exactly this — so the diff was internally contradictory. Verified against the live DB: 8 real `pending_buys` rows carrying pinned `state`/`account` (e.g. SOXS wl_id=206, `order_placed=1`, pinned `state='live'`). `real_order=True` rather than `node=` alone, because `effectively_dry_run` ALSO reads the account's live `trading_enabled`, which nothing freezes into `node_json` — a `node=`-only fix would still have gone dark on a stopped account.
- *The alert header contradicted the send decision — attempted, then REVERTED.* Every one of these messages renders `mode_tag(account, node)`, re-derived from CURRENT state, so in precisely the scenario the fix exists for the alert now correctly fires and says `(roth · DRY-RUN)`. A `mode_tag_for_position(pos, node)` helper was built (returning `LIVE · NODE STOPPED`) and applied at 20 sites — then reverted when the full suite disproved its premise: `test_automated_sell_notifies_sl_price_when_trailing_sell_fails_after_sl_cancel` opens a position on a dry-run account via plain `open_position`, which defaults `is_dry_run_sim=0`, so the helper labelled a never-real test position as real money — the mirror-image error (falsely ALARMING rather than falsely reassuring). `is_dry_run_sim` cannot distinguish a real position on a since-demoted node from a never-real position on an always-dry-run account; both are 0, and `sl_order_id`/`broker_stop_price` don't separate them either. The real prerequisite is pinning entry-time account state onto the position row, which nothing records today. Reverted rather than shipped as a guess into a live-trading alert header; tracked as its own `backlog_cache.md` item. Raised by the cold reviewer only — the contextual reviewer did not flag it. Display-only; the suppression half of the fix is landed and correct.

**Residuals from the same backlog entry.** (a) Pinned-account staleness — subsumed: the position-keyed path consults no account at all now, and `mode_tag_for_position` reads `pos['account']`. (b) `alert_stale_price_exit_suppressed` gained a `db.is_snoozed("stale_price_exit_check_skipped", ...)` lever. Deliberately DIVERGES from `_alert_reconcile_mismatch`, which drops its `coverage_events` row while snoozed: there a snooze acknowledges a known FALSE POSITIVE, here it acknowledges something genuinely true (a real position really did go unmonitored that poll). So the row is still written, tagged `result='skipped_snoozed'` and listed in the Grid row's `bad_results`; only the Slack alert is suppressed. The first draft dropped the row entirely, which contradicted the unconditional-logging comment four lines below it in the same function — caught by both reviewers. (c) The three dead `[DRY RUN] would have ...` paths got explanatory comments rather than being made to fire (correct per the 2026-08-08 design). Two of the three comment drafts were themselves wrong and got corrected in rebuttal: the "kept for `scripts/live_sim.py`'s SIM_MODE console output" clause is false in both directions (`_post_message` has NO console branch at all, and `live_sim.py` never drives these functions), and "always False for a dry_run node" is NOT an invariant at the two `check_dry_run_sim_sells` sites, which loop on the POSITION's `is_dry_run_sim` with no node-state check.

**Review.** Paired independent-cold + contextual Opus, with a full rebuttal exchange. No HIGH findings; both reviewers independently confirmed the position-keyed/node-keyed split was correct at every site AND independently flagged the `check_market_buy_rejected` misclassification, the snooze/record contradiction, and that no test pinned the call-site plumbing. Tests: `tests/test_incident_alert_gate.py` (13 tests) drives the REAL `_post_message` (captured before conftest's autouse no-op, Slack transports forced off) and reads the decision off `slack_message_log`, covering both directions plus a lint-style AST backstop asserting every `incident=True` call site carries a pinned anchor — deliberately with no exemption allowlist, since an allowlist is what a future session extends to silence the check rather than fix a real miss. The stale-price tests' capture stub now asserts kwargs (`kw['pos'] is pos`); previously they passed identically with `pos=` deleted.

**Left open (new backlog item).** `_place_stop_loss_for_position` still reads `account = node.get('account')` for the real order-placement call itself, not `pos['account']` — the same staleness class as this fix but on the ORDER-ROUTING path rather than the alert path, so out of scope here and materially higher risk to change.

## ✅ [live-trading][security] Fixed 2026-08-17 — `check_order`'s `replacing_order_id` exemption extended to the `recent_orders` dup-window, corrected after paired review found the first draft too broad
Found 2026-08-16 (`canary_full_lifecycle`/`canary_early_sl` fake_venue scenario build): `schwab_safety.check_order`'s `replacing_order_id` param exempted an atomic-replace target from the resting-order duplicate check (`_has_open_sell_order`, the 2026-07-28 SH fix) but NOT from the separate `recent_orders` 60-second timestamp-fingerprint dedup loop — that loop has no `order_id` field to exclude by at all (`recent_orders` entries are local `(account, ticker, side, quantity, ts)` records, written before the real order exists at the broker). Originally flagged "not confirmed as reachable, not ruled out either."

**Dispatched to a background agent** (worktree-isolated) to investigate reachability first, fix regardless of the outcome. **Confirmed reachable in production**: `signals_handlers.handle_trail_buy_fill_price` (the manual "Filled" Slack-confirmation flow) runs on the Bolt event-handler thread, genuinely outside `POLL_SECS` poll cadence, and calls `_place_stop_loss_for_position` → `schwab_client.place_stop_loss`, recording a `recent_orders` fingerprint. A later arm/exit-side atomic replace of that SAME order within 60s (a normal next-poll arm/exit scan) trips the fingerprint match, and for a real `trading_enabled` account, `_broker_confirms_order`'s fallback CONFIRMS the order as genuinely resting (since it IS the replace's own target) rather than excusing it as a failed retry — so the replace gets wrongly blocked.

**First-draft fix (built by the dispatched agent)**: `_skip_dup_window = is_addon_leg or replacing_order_id is not None` — any caller supplying `replacing_order_id` unconditionally skips the entire `recent_orders` loop, reasoning that `replacing_order_id` is "a direct fact the caller supplies," unlike `is_addon_leg`'s inferred relationship, so no precondition-verification needed.

**Paired independent-cold + contextual Opus review found this too broad, both converging on the same real fix**: the "direct fact, no verification needed" premise was contradicted by this repo's own on-file 2026-08-14 incident (`_verify_resting_before_replace`'s docstring: a human's manual mispriced stop got replaced by the daemon's own logic because nothing verified the resting order actually matched what the algo believed) — `replacing_order_id` is sourced from local DB fields (`pos['sl_order_id']`, `state['exit_order_id']`, `pending['order_id']`) that can be stale, same epistemic category as `is_addon_leg`, not a categorically different "fact." Concrete blast radius: the blanket skip also exempted BUY-side replaces (`check_gap_resize`'s gap-through-trigger swap) and removed the *only* guard covering the window where a SELL's predecessor already filled at the broker but local reconciliation hasn't caught up — a full-position-size SELL could be approved with zero duplicate protection in that gap. Also found: the exemption fired completely silently (no `coverage_event`, unlike every sibling exemption in this function), and a test (`test_replace_with_any_replacing_order_id_still_skips_fingerprint_window`) pinned the bug in place by asserting a bogus/wrong order id still bypassed the guard, with its own force-fill setup disproving the "resting-order guard would catch this" mitigation it cited.

**Corrected fix**: not a blanket skip. `schwab_safety._broker_confirms_order` gained an `exclude_order_id` param (mirroring `_has_open_sell_order`'s own) — for a `trading_enabled` account, the `recent_orders` fingerprint loop stays live (a genuinely separate confirming order still blocks), and `replacing_order_id` is threaded in as `exclude_order_id` so only the replace's own specific target order is excused from counting as broker confirmation. Only for a non-`trading_enabled` (dry_run) account, with no real broker book to check against, does this fall back to a blanket skip (`_skip_dup_window = is_addon_leg or (replacing_order_id is not None and not limits.trading_enabled)`). This also closes the silent-firing gap for free: when the exclusion causes `_broker_confirms_order` to return False, execution falls into the pre-existing `allowed_retry` branch, which already logs a `coverage_event` — no new logging needed.

The pinning test was rewritten (`test_replace_with_wrong_order_id_does_not_bypass_real_duplicate_protection`) to assert the corrected behavior: a replace naming a bogus order id must NOT bypass detection of a genuinely separate real duplicate order still on the broker's book. 3 regression tests total, all passing: the original production collision (still fixed), the negative control (unweakened), and the corrected wrong-id case.

Merged manually from the dispatched agent's worktree into the same working tree as the HANDOFF `is_handoff_exit` fix above (both touch this same `check_order` block) — applied as an equivalent hand-edit rather than a raw git merge, since the worktree branched from a base predating the HANDOFF fix. Full suite: 1202/1202 (main tree, both fixes present). `scripts/live_sim_harness.py`: 7/7. No `coverage_registry.py` Grid row needed — this closes a gap in the existing `dup_order_window_blocked`/`dup_order_retry_after_failure` tracked mechanism, not a new logic branch.

## ✅ [live-trading][security] Fixed 2026-08-17 — HANDOFF's dup-order-window self-collision closed via a new `is_handoff_exit` exemption, mirroring `is_addon_leg`'s verified-not-trusted contract; paired review found and fixed 4 real issues
Found 2026-08-16 (`fake_venue/scenarios_drought_handoff.py`'s NODE B leg): `schwab_safety.check_order`'s dup-order-window guard already exempts a SELL when a node has an open add-on leg (`is_addon_leg`), since a leg's own protective SELL fingerprints identically `(account, ticker, side, quantity)` to the parent core position's own SELL — but had no equivalent exemption for HANDOFF (the drought-overlay handoff mechanism, `signals_notify.check_drought_handoff`). `_reconcile_buy_fill` auto-places a real protective SL for a newly-opened drought position inline; HANDOFF's own Case B fall-through then tries to REPLACE that same SL with a market sell milliseconds later, well inside the 60s `DUPLICATE_ORDER_WINDOW_SECS` — a real, deterministic (not a timing flake) self-collision, deterministically blocked before this fix. System failed safe (position stayed open+protected, human alerted), just not resolved automatically.

**User's decision, explicit**: add a HANDOFF-specific exemption rather than accept the fail-safe-but-manual outcome. **Real-world premise confirmed by the user directly on the Schwab web UI**: two independent resting SELL stop orders on the same symbol/account are both accepted (not merged/rejected) — validates that this is a genuine broker state worth exempting for, not just a local bookkeeping assumption.

**Design** (a dedicated Opus design-recommendation pass first, before implementation): derive `is_handoff_exit = (reason == 'HANDOFF')` at the exact call site inside `_attempt_automated_exit_sell` (no new plumbing needed above it, `reason` already in scope) → thread through `schwab_client.replace_equity_order_with_market`/`place_equity_sell` → `schwab_safety.approve_and_record` → `schwab_safety.check_order`. Critically: the flag is NOT trusted alone in `check_order`'s SELL dup-order-window block — verified against a real open drought position on file (`signals_db.get_drought_overlay_position`) AND (after the review round below) that `replacing_order_id` actually matches THAT position's own resting order (`sl_order_id`, or `trail_state['exit_order_id']` for the hold-time-forced path), mirroring `is_addon_leg`'s own precondition-verification pattern. Confirmed only the `recent_orders`/dup-order-window block needed changing — HANDOFF already uses the atomic replace path (`replacing_order_id=sl_order_id`), so the separate resting-order guard (`_has_open_sell_order`) already excludes it correctly.

**Paired independent-cold + contextual Opus review found 4 real issues, all fixed**:
1. **[HIGH]** The updated unit test (`tests/test_fake_broker_drought_handoff_scenario.py::test_handoff_cancel_race_to_filled_falls_through_to_case_b`) was blind to the exact regression it claimed to guard — proven empirically by the independent-cold reviewer (stubbed `_reconcile_buy_fill` to silently drop the fill, all 3 assertions still passed) because the only "reconciled correctly" evidence was a coverage event logged *before* `_reconcile_buy_fill` ever runs. Fixed: added a positive `trade_log` assertion (real entry price, shares, `exit_reason='HANDOFF'`) that can only pass if the position was genuinely opened and then closed via the real HANDOFF exit path.
2. **[MEDIUM]** The precondition verified "a drought position exists" + "some replace target was supplied" without tying the two together — safe today only by coincidence of the single call site. Fixed: `replacing_order_id` is now compared against the drought position's own actual order id before exempting.
3. **[MEDIUM]** `place_equity_sell`'s `is_handoff_exit` param was dead code — that path never has a `replacing_order_id` (fresh placement, never a replace), so the exemption could never take effect there, silently leaving the narrower "HANDOFF exit when its own SL placement itself already failed" sub-case unfixed. Fixed: removed the dead param from `place_equity_sell`/`_place_equity_order` entirely and documented the remaining sub-case explicitly in both functions' docstrings and the call site — **not fixed, deliberately, to avoid a false sense of completeness**; would need its own precondition design (matching against a failed prior attempt's `recent_orders` fingerprint, not a live resting order).
4. **[MEDIUM/LOW]** New `drought_handoff_precondition_blocked` scenario_key had no Accountability Grid row and was mislabeled `result="blocked"` when it actually falls through to normal (non-exempted) handling, not a real block. Fixed: added a Grid row (`scripts/coverage_registry.py`), relabeled `result="not_exempted"`.

Tests/fake-venue scenario updated to match the fixed (successful) behavior: NODE B's checks flipped from expecting `failed_or_blocked`/`manual_sl_fallback_alert`/an open position to expecting `drought_handoff`='closed', no fallback alert, zero resting SELLs, and (via `verify_proof`'s `handoff_closed_trades` check) a real `trade_log` row. Module docstring updated to describe the fix, not the original finding, as current state.

Full suite: 1202/1202 passed. `scripts/live_sim_harness.py`: 7/7. Targeted addon/dup-order/drought_handoff subset: 144/144. No regression to the existing `is_addon_leg` exemption (new block short-circuits via `not _skip_dup_window` when addon already exempted).

## ✅ [data][action] Fixed 2026-08-17 — `data_manager.py`'s split-guard 1-bar-overlap gap closed via the existing real-split-confirmation helper
Found 2026-08-13 (corroborating point during an unrelated split-artifact-fix paired review), retagged `[data][action]` 2026-08-16, queued behind other work, fixed 2026-08-17. `fetch_live_data_smart`'s Step 3 overlap-guard (`data_manager.py`) computed `consistent = len(overlap) == 1 or (ratios.std() / ratios.mean()) < 0.05` — with exactly one overlapping bar there's no way to compute a std-dev-based consistency check, so it was hardcoded `True` unconditionally, meaning a single corrupted/artifact bar landing in a 1-bar overlap window could itself drive a spurious whole-history rescale of the entire cached series if its price ratio also happened to look like a clean split factor (the `detect_price_discontinuity` magnitude check alone was the only remaining guard in that case). This project already has the right tool for exactly this: `signals_helpers.real_split_confirmed_since(ticker, since)` — the same real-confirmed-split gate (`yf.Ticker(ticker).splits`, three-way True/False/None, fail-closed on `None`/fetch-failure) that `_apply_split_artifact_fix`/`get_real_splits` already use for the same-pull single-bar-artifact case (2026-08-13 fix). **Fixed**: when `len(overlap) == 1`, `consistent` is now `real_split_confirmed_since(ticker, since=overlap[0] - pd.Timedelta(days=1)) is True` instead of a bare `True`; the `len(overlap) >= 2` branch is unchanged (real statistical consistency check still applies there). 2 new regression tests (`tests/test_split_guard_single_bar_overlap.py`): confirms a 1-bar-overlap 20x price ratio does NOT rescale the rest of the cached history without a real confirmed split on file, and DOES rescale when one is confirmed. Full existing suite (`test_data_mutation_log.py` + the new test file): 6 passed. Out of scope for the Review-Gate Persistence Rule — `data_manager.py` is not `active_signals.py`/`signals_*.py`/`schwab_*.py`/a backtest kernel module.

This session's own worktree started behind `main` and was missing the "already implemented" pieces the brief assumed were done (`window_version_suffix`, the guard swap, the phase-function threading) — verified directly (`git log --all -S"window_version_suffix"` across every branch: zero hits) rather than trusted from the brief, then built for real; flagged to peer session "planner" mid-task in case of a worktree/plan mismatch on their end too.

**Design (already decided by the brief, not re-litigated)**: encode the date window into the `backtest_cache` `version` string itself via `window_version_suffix(start_date, end_date)` (`run_optimization_sweep.py` ~line 474, e.g. `v5` → `v5-w2025-06-01_2026-06-01`), instead of a schema/PK migration — `backtest_cache` has no date-window columns, and every real downstream consumer (`_campaign_scope_sql`, `identify_island_candidates`, `identify_full_mesh_candidates`, `db_cache.py`'s `refresh_pivot_cache`/`refresh_dropdown_cache`/`refresh_cliff_grid_cache`, `scripts/top_safe_nodes.py`, `scripts/locate_best_node.py`, `scripts/candidate_summary_report.py::best_node_strategy`) already scopes strictly by `version` alone, confirmed by direct code read of every one of them (not assumed) — so suffixing gives full collision-proof isolation for free, matching the project's existing v4→v5 "distinct version string per incompatible campaign" precedent.

**What was built**: `dispatch_parallel_grid`'s old hard `NotImplementedError` replaced with a `ValueError` assertion — fires only when a windowed call's `config_version` doesn't already carry the required suffix (a caller windowing the DATA without windowing the VERSION, the one real corruption risk left). `start_date=None, end_date=None` threaded through `run_phase1_coarse`/`run_phase2_island`/`run_phase25_cliff_box`/`run_phase3_full`, each passing into its own `dispatch_parallel_grid` call. New `--start-date`/`--end-date` CLI flags (both-or-neither, hard error otherwise), suffixing `config_version` immediately after it's computed, before any consumer sees it. Every one of the ~6 phase-runner call sites inside `main()`'s phase-driving loop threaded through (the `phase_only==3` direct branch, the generation loop's Phase 2 call, Phase 2.5, and both Phase 3 call sites). The B&H precompute loop's `compute_bh_returns(ticker)` call also windowed — CRITICAL, called out explicitly in the brief: a windowed trade set scored against a full-history SPY benchmark would silently reintroduce the exact HIGH bug Phase 1's own review already fixed once, through this separate call site.

**Paired Opus review (independent-cold + contextual, run in parallel against the real diff, full rebuttal exchange — both agents independently converged on the same core findings, then confirmed each other's after seeing the other's list) found 4 real gaps, all fixed same session**:
1. MEDIUM — an out-of-range windowed `compute_bh_returns` call raises `ValueError` (not the missing-CSV `None, None` path), which propagated uncaught out of the B&H precompute loop and aborted the ENTIRE sweep before any phase ran — real risk for the planned 9-window campaign if any window falls outside a ticker's cached span. Fixed: `try/except ValueError` around that one call site, logs and `continue`s (drops the ticker into the same "not in `valid_tickers`" bucket the missing-cache-file path already uses), catching `ValueError` specifically (not bare `except`) so a genuinely broken/corrupt CSV still fails loudly.
2. MEDIUM — the guard was one-directional: `dispatch_parallel_grid`'s check only fires when `start_date`/`end_date` are non-`None`, so running with an already-windowed-looking `--version` (e.g. copy-pasted from a log filename or `sweep_runs` row — exactly what a resume/extend command would naturally do, since the suffixed version is what's user-visible everywhere) but WITHOUT `--start-date`/`--end-date` would silently write full-history results into what looks like a windowed campaign's cache rows, with nothing downstream able to tell them apart. Fixed: a hard `sys.exit(1)` in `main()`, guarded by a regex anchored to `window_version_suffix`'s exact fixed-width format (`-w\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}_\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$`) so an unrelated version string containing "-w" for some other reason doesn't false-positive.
3. LOW/MEDIUM — no date format normalization meant `'2025-6-1'` and `'2025-06-01'` (the identical window to `_window_prep`/`compute_bh_returns`, both of which already parse via `pd.Timestamp`) would silently produce two different version strings and split one campaign's cache across two disjoint, half-populated namespaces with zero error raised. A slash in the date (`'2025/06/01'`) would also propagate into `run_log_path`'s filename construction and crash with `FileNotFoundError` after `init_idempotent_db()` had already run (the contextual reviewer's addition to the cold reviewer's finding) — assessed as the less important half, since it's at least a loud failure; the silent split was the real severity driver. Fixed: dates normalized via `pd.Timestamp(x).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')` inside `window_version_suffix` itself (the one shared source of truth for both the CLI path and `dispatch_parallel_grid`'s guard), which also gives free format validation and normalizes a `datetime.date`/`pd.Timestamp` object caller (e.g. the planned orchestration script) to the same string a CLI caller would produce. Both-or-neither validation also moved into `window_version_suffix` itself (previously only the CLI arg parser checked it), so a programmatic caller gets the same guarantee.
4. LOW — the guard's `required_suffix not in config_version` substring check swapped to `.endswith(required_suffix)` — closes a theoretical false-negative shape (the suffix is fixed-width by construction, so anchoring to the end is free) with zero behavior change for any real case.

Two more findings, confirmed correct but explicitly out of scope for this diff: `scripts/run_sweep_queue.sh`/`scripts/campaign_config.py` have zero windowing plumbing yet — that's the peer "planner" session's orchestration-script job, not this one, flagged for them. `refresh_dropdown_cache()`/`refresh_cliff_grid_cache()` (`main()`'s end) are version-unfiltered, so a real 9-window campaign will accumulate dropdown/cliff-grid-blob clutter over time — not a correctness leak (`CLIFF_GRID_SQL` groups by `version`, confirmed by the contextual reviewer reading `db_cache.py:325,341`), the orchestration script should pass the already-existing `--skip-cache-refresh` per-window and refresh once at the end.

**Validated via the backtest-change-rollout skill (Stages 1-3 this session; Stage 4/full campaign deliberately NOT launched — user's/orchestration-script's call, per the skill's standing convention)**:
- **Stage 1**: extended `scripts/audit_date_window_soxl.py` with a new `--cache-roundtrip` mode — drives SOXL's real live-node params (window=10, z=1.0, arm_sell_pct=30, fixed_sl=2.0, trail_buy_pct=3.0, trail_sell_pct=1.0, max_hold_hours=70, entry_timing=open_check) through the ACTUAL `dispatch_parallel_grid` path (real `ProcessPoolExecutor` + real `backtest_cache` write) under a windowed+suffixed version, then compares the persisted row against a direct uncached `_load_node_inputs`+`run_backtest_dispatch` compute for the identical window. Exact match: trades=37, alpha=171.616786%, compounded=200.473879%, win_rate=16.216216%, all to 1e-6. A second call confirmed a pure cache hit (0 recompute). Also confirmed correct AFTER applying all 4 review fixes (reran, identical result).
- **Stage 2**: ran SOXL through the full Phase1→2→2.5 pipeline for window [2025-06-01, 2026-06-01] via the real CLI (`--start-date --end-date --max-phase 2.5 --tickers SOXL`), with an explicitly-biased grid (stated, not silent): `stop_loss`/`trail_buy_pct` axes restricted to ≤9% (the existing 2026-07-16 robust-alpha precedent — "robust alpha declined consistently above 9% across every ticker checked"), `windows=[10]` (matching SOXL's real live node), `z=[1.0, 1.5]`, `trail_pcts` full 1-7%, `hold_time_caps` full 20-value config.json default. Full grid remains available by rerunning without the bias (`campaign_config.py`'s `COMBINED`/`TRAIL_PCTS`). 13,720 Phase1 tasks + 25,840 new Phase2 tasks (11,340 pre-cached from Phase1 overlap) completed in ~2 minutes at ~200-320 nodes/sec. Phase2.5's 150 tasks were entirely cache hits from Phase2 (a real internal consistency check — Phase2.5's cliff-box search landed inside Phase2's already-computed neighborhood). Checkpoint2 found the window CLIFF (best +79.9%, worst_neighbor -50%), correctly advancing 0 candidates to Phase3 (moot anyway at `--max-phase 2.5`). Confirmed version isolation: `v5-stage2audit-w2025-06-01_2026-06-01` (39,560 SOXL rows, alpha range -69.8% to +130.1%) vs. real `v5` (73,048 SOXL rows, alpha range -144.8% to +1212.1%) — zero row-count or value-range collision. Confirmed `scripts/candidate_summary_report.py::best_node_strategy` reads the windowed version correctly when passed `version=<suffixed string>` — returned `('TrailingBothZScoreBreakout', 28.857093704655146)`, where the spy_bh (28.857%) matches Stage 1's independently-computed windowed SPY benchmark to the decimal.
- **Stage 3**: new `scripts/backtest_cache_storage_forecast.py` (built as a real reusable script, not a one-off — this forecast will need to rerun for every future rolling-window campaign, per the project's "audit work that could plausibly rerun belongs in scripts/" convention). Uses the sqlite `dbstat` virtual table for an exact table+index byte count (not an estimate) and `SELECT MAX(rowid)` for row count (per the skill's guidance — `COUNT(*)` can time out on this table). Current state: ≈9.97M rows, 1.996GB table-only / 3.738GB table+5-indexes (≈375 bytes/row observed, used directly rather than a guessed constant). The real ~9-window SOXL campaign (full grid: z=3, w=2, tp=14, sl=14, hold=20, tpct=7 per the `campaign_config.py` `TrailingBothZScoreBreakout` grid) projects to ~1.48M new Phase1 rows (~0.56GB table+indexes) at a single `fixed_sl` value, scaling linearly with however many `fixed_sl` values the orchestration script ends up sweeping (the project's `FIXED_SLS="1 2 3"` precedent would triple it, ~1.67GB) — Phase2/2.5 add more on top, no closed-form size for those per the skill. `df -h` on `cache/research` reported 870GB free; presented as a raw data point only, flagged per the skill's standing WSL2 caveat as unreliable at face value (a real prior incident: `df` said 826GB free, real available was 113GB) — not treated as the real answer, real available space needs a direct ask to the user before Stage 4.

**Test suite**: 1189 passed, 3 failed — all 3 in subsystems this diff never touches (`test_fake_venue_harness_scenario.py::test_production_access_tripwire_catches_relative_paths`, 2x parametrized `test_entry_abandon_truth_table.py` cases). ## ✅ [live-trading][security] Closed 2026-08-16 — `check_auto_fills`'s buy-side fallback fixed for automated market-buy nodes
Real gap found 2026-08-16 building `fake_venue/scenarios_sl_async_fallback.py`'s Leg 1.5 (see the prior open `backlog_cache.md` entry, now resolved): of the 3 fallback paths `sl_async_fallback`'s Grid row names (`check_auto_fills`, `drain_fill_queue`, `check_gap_resize`), only `drain_fill_queue` actually recovered a timed-out `_sync_confirm_and_protect` fast-confirm poll for a market-buy fill. `check_auto_fills`'s buy-side loop (`signals_notify.py` ~line 4738) gated unconditionally on `pending_buys.order_placed`, which is never set to 1 for any automated market-buy node (`mark_pending_buy_placed_by_wl_id` is only called from `notify_buy_signal`'s trailing-buy branch and the manual "Trailing Buy Order Placed" Slack button, neither of which fires for a market-buy-eligible `TrailingExitZScoreBreakout`-style node) — genuinely dead code for that population. `check_gap_resize` was also confirmed inapplicable (scoped to a still-resting trailing-buy order gapping through its trigger; a market order fills same-tick, nothing resting to resize) and removed from the Grid row's `code_path`.

**Fix**: the buy-side loop now branches on `db._is_trailing_buy(node)` — a trailing-buy row still requires `order_placed` (the real "resting, awaiting fill" GOOD_TILL_CANCEL broker state that genuinely exists for that order type); a market-buy row instead requires only a real `order_id` on file, since a market order has no analogous resting state during regular hours (fills same-tick, genuinely fails/rejects, or — the one exception, a pre-market placement — waits for the open, in which case `get_filled_order` simply keeps returning `None` until then, the same as any other not-yet-filled case this poll already handled safely).

**Test coverage**: `fake_venue/scenarios_sl_async_fallback.py` restructured from a single node/account to two (node_a/`fv_cash`, node_b/`fv_margin`), both `TrailingExitZScoreBreakout` on the same synthetic ticker, so each fallback path's recovery is proven independently rather than one leg's already-reconciled fill masking the other: Leg 1.5 (node_a) proves `check_auto_fills` alone recovers a timed-out market-buy fill end-to-end (position opens, tops up, gets a genuine broker-side protective stop) with zero `drain_fill_queue`/stream involvement — upgraded from a documentary `required=False` Check to a proving `required=True` one; Leg 2 (node_b) proves the pre-existing `drain_fill_queue` stream-path fallback still independently works unchanged. `verify_proof`'s SQL now asserts on 2 rows (one per account), with `async_confirm_events == 0` on node_a's row and `== 1` on node_b's — a genuinely load-bearing negative that makes Leg 1.5 a proof of `check_auto_fills` *alone*, not incidental coverage from the other leg. `tests/test_fake_venue_sl_async_fallback_scenario.py` updated to match (all checks now `required=True`, 2 proof rows expected). Full harness run: 30/30 checks pass.

**Paired Opus review (independent-cold + contextual, per the Review-Gate Persistence Rule)**: both converged — core fix correct, no CRITICAL/HIGH findings, and both independently flagged the SAME MEDIUM finding (convergence taken as sufficient confirmation without a further rebuttal round, given the low cost of acting on it either way): a market-buy `pending_buys` row whose broker order was genuinely rejected/cancelled (not filled) has no termination path — `get_filled_order` never returns non-`None` for it, and `check_entry_abandon` is trailing-buy-only (`skip if not db._is_trailing_buy(node)`), so the row now satisfies this fix's gate forever, polling the broker every cycle with no alert. Pre-existing in shape (the row already lingered pre-fix, just wasn't polled) but the new branch is where a terminal-state check would naturally live — **not fixed here** (a market-buy abandon-timeout is its own design question, out of scope for this fix); reopened as a new backlog item, see `backlog_cache.md`. The contextual review's one real LOW (node-lookup dispatch moved above the ticker-scope gate, so a malformed `node_json` for an OUT-of-scope ticker could raise and take the sell-side exit-fill loop down with it too) was fixed directly: `if ticker not in schwab_safety.AUTOMATION_ENABLED_TICKERS: continue` now runs before `pending['node']` is touched at all. Two other LOW findings (comment overclaiming market-order fill semantics; Grid notes not distinguishing what the `scenario_key` status axis actually measures vs. what the fake_venue proof separately confirms) were also fixed directly (docstring/comment wording, `scripts/coverage_registry.py` notes). The independent-cold review additionally confirmed: no dry_run leakage (`_place_equity_order` short-circuits to `(None, None)` for dry_run, so those rows never carry a real `order_id`), no double-reconciliation risk (`_reconcile_buy_fill` re-reads and clears `pending_buys` by wl_id before opening the position; `check_auto_fills`/`drain_fill_queue` run sequentially on the same poll thread), and confirmed the scenario's two-node/same-ticker construction does NOT (by design, via leg sequencing) accidentally exercise the separate, already-known, structurally-blocked `buy_fill_reconciles_correct_node` disambiguation gap.

**Worktree note**: this fix's development hit a real process snag mid-task — the assigned worktree had branched from a stale `origin/main` (missing the fake_venue harness entirely, added on local `main` after the branch point). An initial attempt to work around this by manually copying the `fake_venue/` directory into the worktree was flagged and stopped by the coordinating session before it compounded; resolved cleanly via `git merge main --ff-only` instead (fast-forward, no conflicts). A `git reset --hard HEAD` used to discard the manual-copy workaround also silently wiped the first pass of the `check_auto_fills` fix itself (uncommitted at the time) — caught via the harness output not matching expectations (Leg 1.5 failing) rather than by inspection, root-caused, and the fix reapplied correctly before proceeding.

Full suite: 1161 passed, 4 skipped, 27 failed — every one of the 27 failures confirmed pre-existing on the merged `main` baseline (reproduced identically via `git stash` with this diff removed), none are regressions from this fix.

## ✅ [test-infra] Root-caused and closed 2026-08-15 (peer session "planner") — `test_a_broker_fetch_failure_cannot_block_the_exit`'s full-suite-only flake
Not reproducible on 2 fresh full-suite runs (0 failures). Root cause: the test uses `inspect.getsource()` to verify `_attempt_automated_sell`/`_attempt_automated_exit_sell` call `_verify_resting_before_replace` inside a `try:`. `inspect.getsource()` internally combines a fresh disk read (`linecache.checkcache`) with the function's IMPORT-TIME `co_firstlineno` — if `signals_notify.py`'s line count shifts above that function while the suite is running (a concurrent git merge/checkout mid-run), `getsource` silently slices the WRONG block, no exception, just wrong source text, causing a false failure even though the real code is correctly wired. Directly demonstrated by replaying the actual +13 line shift that happened for real between commits `484574e` (22:11) and `0c87bf2` (00:16) that night — reproduced the identical failure shape. A standalone 48s run essentially never straddles a mid-run git rewrite; a 10+ minute full-suite run sometimes does, and that night had repeated worktree merges/commits touching `signals_notify.py` in the same window. Ruled out: no raw reassignment of the 3 functions anywhere in `tests/`, no autouse fixture interference, no decorators, worktree copies aren't collected by pytest. Not a code bug — a structural fragility of source-introspection-style tests colliding with long full-suite runs during active git churn. **Not fixed (optional, not done)**: rewriting the test as a behavioral check (call the function, spy on the call) instead of introspecting source text would make it structurally immune to this flake class going forward.

## [testing] Latent, noted 2026-08-15 (peer session "planner") — `tests/test_overlay_paper_trading.py` cross-file synthetic-CSV race (`EmptyDataError`), same class as the already-fixed intra-file race but not covered by that fix
During a full-suite run, one test in this file failed with `pandas.errors.EmptyDataError` — same failure class as the already-fixed intra-file CSV race (`make_synthetic_csv`/`cleanup_csv` sharing a `cache/research/{TICKER}_1h.csv` path, fixed via `--dist=loadscope` 2026-08-11), but this one is CROSS-file: `--dist=loadscope` only pins same-*file* tests to one worker, so two *different* test files sharing the same synthetic ticker string could still race across workers. No fix needed right now — logged so it's tracked rather than rediscovered as a fresh mystery if a future test ever reuses one of those ticker strings.

## [live-trading][security] Open, found 2026-08-16 session-wrap review, user-assessed same day — retry-dedup's single-candidate match could adopt the wrong sibling order id between a core position's SL and its add-on leg's SL
`schwab_client._check_broker_before_retry`/`_find_recent_matching_order` match a retry candidate on ticker+side+quantity+orderType+status only (no per-node/per-leg distinguishing factor). If a core position's stop-loss and its add-on leg's stop-loss (same ticker, same account, same side, same order type) land within the same few-second retry window with matching quantities, a single non-baseline candidate is adopted without disambiguation — could misattribute which order id protects which position/leg. Only the multi-candidate case fails safe (`_AmbiguousBrokerState`); the single-candidate case is the dangerous one, found by the session-wrap contextual review after the retry-dedup fix had already been through 2 review rounds that didn't catch it.

**User's assessment, 2026-08-16**: not urgent to fix the matching logic itself — the downstream live-state-reconciliation check would likely surface a real misattribution as a broker-state mismatch anyway, and an add-on leg's missing "sister" order is itself a tell. **Mitigation shipped same session**: the `'prevented'` coverage_events log now includes `order_type`/`quantity` explicitly in `detail` (schwab_client.py, `_check_broker_before_retry`), so the adopted match's exact shape is inspectable after the fact if a misattribution is ever suspected — no change to the matching logic itself.

**User's secondary idea, a real candidate approach**: the actual problem is that the matching predicate needs a genuine uniqueness guarantee between a core position's SL and its add-on leg's SL, which it doesn't have today. One way to get that: size add-on leg order quantities deliberately off by a fixed amount from the core leg's quantity, so ticker+side+orderType+quantity can never coincide between the two. User's own framing was "just a hack, not something we have to do" — meaning one possible mechanism among others, not the only way to get uniqueness, not a final decision on which mechanism to use. Not scoped: exact offset, which leg it applies to, real position-sizing implications, interaction with `_last_sale_recovery`/existing sizing logic, or whether a different uniqueness mechanism (e.g. threading node_id/leg-type through the order itself, if the Schwab API supports any client-tagged field) would be cleaner. Needs real design work before building.

## [tooling][security] Open, found 2026-08-16 session-wrap review — 6 lower-severity findings from the full-session dual-Opus review, not fixed this session
Full session diff reviewed (independent-cold + contextual, both Opus) after a background-agent-heavy session. 3 mechanical HIGH-adjacent findings fixed same session (see the matching resolved entries in this file / `backlog_resolved_recent.md`: `fast_path_fill_reconciliation`'s `bad_results`/hardcoded-mode fix, `signals_blocks._ticker_block`'s `mode_tag` local-variable shadowing rename). Both reviewers independently deep-dove `fake_venue/isolation.py` and the `tests/conftest.py` autouse fixture and found **no real isolation breach** in either — the highest-risk pieces of the session hold up.

Remaining findings, not fixed, real but lower-severity/deferred:
1. **`signals_db.check_abnormal_drift` doesn't cover add-on legs at all** — `open_position()`/`close_position()` explicitly route `position_source='addon_leg'` to separate `open_addon_leg()`/`close_addon_leg()` functions that never call `check_abnormal_drift`, despite the function's own docstring claiming it's "the one real chokepoint every entry/exit fill passes through." Add-on legs are real fills on exactly the nodes that clear `has_capital_at_stake` (`brokerage`'s $6k addon-enabled nodes) — the single case where liquidity/drift risk is most likely, since an add-on is by definition sizing up. MEDIUM.
2. **The abnormal-drift alert can't fire on `brokerage` at all today** — all 3 real `brokerage` live nodes (ETHU/AGQ/JNUG, `starting_notional=$6,000`) sit below `CAPITAL_AT_STAKE_THRESHOLD` ($10k), so `has_capital_at_stake` gates them out; only `ira`/`roth` $10k+ nodes can trip it. `brokerage` holds the leveraged/1256 tickers whose liquidity was the stated motivation for building the alert. Verified against the live DB, not inferred. MEDIUM.
3. **Tax forecast tool: capital-loss character doesn't cross-net.** `k1_tax.brokerage_tax_forecast()` computes `lt_gain_net`/`st_pool_net` independently, each floored at 0 — real tax mechanics let an excess loss of one character offset gains of the other. Failure scenario: AGQ's 60% LT slice is +$100k while JNUG/ETHU net −$60k; real netted position ≈$40k, but the tool taxes the full $100k LT and reports the ST pool as 0 — an overstatement well outside the tool's own stated "~5-10% expected error." Related: when a gross pool is negative, `*_baseline_remaining` reports MORE remaining baseline than actually exists (conservative direction for the sweep signal, but the printed number is wrong). MEDIUM.
4. **Tax forecast tool: the $240k baseline seed silently resurrects after deletion, and evaporates on year rollover.** `signals_db.ensure_tables()`'s seed guard keys on `(account, tax_year=2026, character)` — if the user ever corrects the baseline by deleting the row (the only correction path, since `add_tax_realized_loss_baseline` is append-only), the next `ensure_tables()` call (runs at daemon startup, in the evening report itself, in the guard-staging script) silently re-inserts $240,000 with no audit trail. Separately: on 2026-2027 rollover, `get_tax_realized_loss_baseline('brokerage', 2027)` returns nothing → both baselines read 0 → `baseline_exhausted=True` on the very first 2027 gain, even though a real carryforward almost certainly exists — an absent baseline and a genuinely-exhausted one render identically. MEDIUM.
5. **Order-retry-dedup's baseline broker-order-history fetch adds a real round-trip to every order placement's happy path**, not just the retry path — `_snapshot_baseline_order_ids()` is called unconditionally before the first attempt (required for correctness — a lazy post-failure snapshot could already contain the landed order — but the cost is real and unflagged in either retry docstring). `schwab_safety.check_order` already fetches real order history moments earlier via `_open_orders`/`_all_orders`; that snapshot could potentially be threaded through instead of re-fetched. Most relevant on the latency-critical `_reconcile_buy_fill → _place_stop_loss_for_position` path, where a position is unprotected until the STOP lands. MEDIUM.
6. **`scripts/evening_status.py`'s new tax-forecast query scopes realized gains to tickers with a currently-`live` brokerage node** (`WHERE account='brokerage' AND state='live'`), not to the account as a whole — if a ticker is demoted to paper (or its node deleted) after realizing gains earlier in the year, those gains vanish from the forecast, understating the reserve. Tax realization is a property of `trade_log`, not current node state. LOW/MEDIUM.

Minor/LOW findings not tracked individually here (see review agent transcripts if needed): `stage_check_order_guard_scenarios.py`'s `_recent_event()` has no time bound (a re-run can report PASS on a scenario that logged nothing new); `drain_fill_queue`'s account-resolution-failure event was hardcoded `mode="dry_run"` (fixed same session, see resolved entry); an unclosed sqlite connection in the new tax-forecast query; `resolve_account_alias_from_number`'s `endswith` suffix match could theoretically misresolve if one account's real Schwab suffix happened to be a suffix of another's (no evidence this occurs today); a naive-timestamp-assumed-UTC edge case in `_parse_broker_timestamp`; a `ZeroDivisionError` risk in the abnormal-drift computation if `signal_price` is ever exactly 0, raised after the DB commit (would leave the caller believing the open/close failed while the DB says otherwise).

## [live-trading][coverage] Open, scoped 2026-08-16 — coverage_events write-attribution (`source` column), fixed enum taxonomy, real-execution-first rollout
Raised while investigating the STAGE_GUARD_TEST/node-breaker-state incidents tonight — no way to tell, after the fact, whether a `coverage_events` row came from the real daemon, a specific fixture/staging script, or a test, without forensic timestamp/log correlation each time. Precedent already in this codebase: `sweep_runs` has `git_commit`/`kernel_dirty` for the identical reason (write-time provenance, not reconstructed after the fact).

**Design, refined 2026-08-16 (user-answered)**:
1. **Fixed enum, not freeform** — an enforced taxonomy (e.g. `'daemon'`, `'fixture:stage_check_order_guard_scenarios'`, `'fixture:test_fake_broker_entry_scenario'`, ...), not caller-typed strings.
2. **Piecemeal rollout, not a blanket default-then-move-on migration** — prioritize by highest-value targets: call sites touching `check_order`/order placement/fills first (real trade execution), lower-priority call sites can wait. User's rationale: punting broadly means "tomorrow we'll need to dig in on something else and we won't have this lineage."
3. **Backfill for existing rows: best-effort only**, not a rigorous forensic requirement — "we'll get cleaner over time." Don't over-invest reconstructing every historical row; reuse the same timestamp/log-correlation approach already used tonight to attribute the 42 `STAGE_GUARD_TEST` rows and any other identifiable existing rows, converging on the same taxonomy so old and new data are comparable.
4. **Relationship to `mode`: not fully orthogonal** — a validity constraint, not overlap. A `source='fixture:...'` row should probably never be able to co-occur with `mode='live'` (a fixture producing a real trade would be structurally wrong) — worth a check/assertion at write time, not just two independent free fields.

Scope to `coverage_events` first (the immediate pain point); extend to other tables (e.g. `trade_log`?) as they come up rather than a big-bang migration. Not started — logged for whenever it's greenlit, per the user's explicit call tonight not to start new schema-migration scope mid-session-wrap.

**Scope expanded 2026-08-15 (user's call)**: the previously-standalone "closed-trade reconciliation" item (audit `trade_log` against real broker order history after a position closes — full design was in `docs/design.md`'s 2026-08-15 (later still) entry, ending in an unresolved OPEN DECISIONS list: when it runs, what it reconciles against, backfill scope, where it lives, alert policy) is not being built as its own item — its scope now lives inside this data-lineage/attribution work instead. Standalone `docs/backlog_cache.md` entry removed; resolve reconciliation's open design questions as part of this effort when it's picked up, not separately.

Started from the "expand paper trading" item; concluded paper trading itself is a component-level (kernel-fidelity) tool that structurally can't catch the system-level bugs (node/account interactivity, order-lifecycle/response-handling) actually biting this project lately — those need the real code path. Key architecture calls: reuse real `check_order` unchanged (no parallel `fake_venue_safety`), ≥2 fake accounts (permanently venue-tied, not an EMS/routing abstraction), separate process (fake_broker's client patch is process-global), separate physical DB file via `TRADING_DB_PATH`+`SCHWAB_STATE_DIR` (not shared-table tagging), seeded state to manufacture the Grid's structurally-blocked `buy_fill_reconciles_correct_node` row on demand, real market data but a historical-replay mode for the price feed so it's not bound to real trading days.

**Real limitation, should be stated wherever this gets built**: the harness cannot validate Schwab's actual internal correctness (margin math, order-matching edge cases) — only that OUR response-handling code reacts correctly to a *plausible* fake response shape. **Phase 1 BUILT, 2026-08-16 — build writeup: `docs/design.md`'s 2026-08-16 (build) entry.** New `fake_venue/` package + `scripts/fake_venue_harness.py` + `tests/test_fake_venue_harness_scenario.py`, zero production-code changes. `buy_fill_reconciles_correct_node` reproduced end to end and proven by a read-only query against the harness's own `coverage_events`; the emitter drives the real `_handle_activity_message`/`_parse_activity_message` with a raw envelope transcribed from a real captured message. ## [portfolio] Open — idea raised 2026-08-14, substantially expanded 2026-08-16 — portfolio-level rebalancing across a 3-bucket structure (safe / risky / algo); real design work, not ready to build, partly blocked on data
Original question (2026-08-14): if one strategy/ticker (e.g. AGQ) performs well, should capital be deliberately rotated out of an existing holding like TQQQ into it, rather than TQQQ being a static allocation. Distinct from the existing "TQQQ cleared for IRA trading" item (that's about adding a new TQQQ node/candidacy; this is about rebalancing an existing position based on relative performance).

**Portfolio structure, updated framing (2026-08-16)**: 3 buckets, replacing an older safe/risky/play-money split — (1) **Safe**: SPY/SSO/QLD, sized to guarantee a reasonable retirement on its own. (2) **Risky**: TQQQ/UPRO, moonshot upside that doesn't jeopardize the retirement goal if it goes to zero. (3) **Algo trades** (this system) — user explicitly moved ALL the old "play money" allocation into algo trading, since manual discretionary stock-picking hasn't worked out for them personally. This is why algo capital keeps growing — a deliberate reallocation away from a bucket that wasn't working, not just this project's own success.

**Open question, genuinely unscoped**: portfolio-level rebalancing vs. individual-bucket rebalancing — never designed. User's own framing: deprioritizing solving this precisely because bucket 1 alone already secures the actual goal (retirement) — buckets 2/3 are pure upside attempts, so getting the rebalancing mechanism "right" matters less than it would if retirement depended on it. Don't over-invest design effort proportional to the stakes here.

**Ties into the still-unbuilt hedging/skim idea** (this file's 2026-08-04 "skim-and-reserve insurance policy" entry — decided-in-principle, SPY reserve + manual redeploy, never built): the real open question is whether take-profit + redistribution across the 3 buckets is the actual mechanism, not the old single-SPY-reserve framing. Needs reconciling with the new 3-bucket structure, not a separate design.

**Real blocker, user's own words: "I actually think this needs to be simulated — not easy to do"**: wants to simulate TQQQ (and other volatile candidates) against REAL HOURLY bars, not daily — this project's own established finding (`feedback_daily_bar_understates_real_risk` memory, KORU's -64.1% daily-bar artifact) means a daily-bar sim would give a false read on real volatility comfort. Requires purchasing additional historical hourly data not currently on file — user has this on their own todo list, possibly this weekend, not something to route around.

**Interim practice, not a zero-fallback gap**: user currently rebalances across the 3 buckets manually, by hand, on a quarterly cadence, given currently diminished capital — this is a real, acknowledged, deliberately-deferred open design question, not something with no fallback in the meantime.

**Net**: needs (1) genuine design discussion on the rebalancing mechanism scoped proportionally to "upside only, not survival-critical," (2) reconciliation with the still-unbuilt skim/hedging design, (3) is blocked on the user's own hourly-data purchase before any TQQQ volatility sim can run for real. Not ready to build — ready to scope once the data question resolves.
