## ✅ [testing][security] Resolved 2026-08-15 — test suite was mutating real `cache/live/schwab_node_breaker_state.json` + `schwab_order_counts.json` on every run; `tests/conftest.py` autouse fixture now isolates all 8 `schwab_safety` state paths
Real incident: `cache/live/schwab_node_breaker_state.json` (a real live node's `order_failures_streak`/`order_failures_tripped`) was being mutated by the test suite, reproducible with zero fake_venue-harness involvement. A prior investigation (see this file's fake_venue-harness entries and `docs/backlog_cache.md`'s now-narrowed "real `cache/live/` state files touched 08:10-08:32" item) had wrongly suspected the fake_venue harness and separately noted "12+ tests already patch `NODE_BREAKER_PATH`, zero missing" from a plain grep for the symbol name — that grep undercounted the exposure because the write doesn't happen from code a test author would recognize as "touching `schwab_safety`" by name.

**Root cause**: `schwab_safety.py` has 8 module-level `Path` constants under `cache/live/` (`STATE_PATH`, `KILL_SWITCH_PATH`, `TICKER_AUTOMATION_PATH`, `AUTO_FILL_DETECTION_PATH`, `AUTOMATION_SCOPE_STATE_PATH`, `NODE_AUTOMATION_PATH`, `NODE_BREAKER_PATH`, `NODE_AUTO_FILL_DETECTION_PATH`), all derived from `_STATE_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("SCHWAB_STATE_DIR", ".../cache/live"))`. `schwab_client.py`'s real order-placement functions (`place_order`, `replace_order`, `place_stop_loss`, trailing buy/sell, etc.) call `schwab_safety.record_node_streak(...)` and increment the order-count state **unconditionally**, as a side-channel monitor sitting directly in the approved-order control flow — not something a test exercising "place a stop-loss via the fake broker" would think to isolate. `tests/fake_broker.py`'s `fake_broker` fixture fakes the broker connection (`schwab_client._client`/`_get_client`) but never touched these 8 paths. Dozens of `tests/test_fake_broker_*_scenario.py` files use that fixture without their own patch, so every one of them wrote to the REAL files on every run.

**Proof**: isolated each candidate file with `SCHWAB_STATE_DIR=<private tmp dir>` (avoids both corrupting the real file and contamination from other concurrent sessions that happened to be running full-suite pytest against this same repo at the same time) — confirmed 13+ files write `schwab_node_breaker_state.json` when unpatched: `test_fake_broker_arm_scenario`, `_buy_button_handlers_`, `_confirmed_fill_dropped_at_gate_`, `_drain_fill_queue_`, `_entry_abandon_`, `_entry_`, `_exit_fresh_`, `_gap_resize_`, `_gdxu_reconciliation_`, `_orphaned_fill_alert_`, `_pinned_entry_`, `_retl_`, `_sh_`, `_topup_`. Re-ran the same set after the fix — zero writes to `SCHWAB_STATE_DIR` (the write now goes to pytest's own `tmp_path` instead, via the new fixture).

**Fix**: `tests/conftest.py` gained `_isolate_schwab_safety_state_files` (autouse, `monkeypatch` + `tmp_path`) — patches all 8 `schwab_safety` path constants to per-test tmp paths for every test, unconditionally, rather than requiring each test file to opt in individually. Mirrors the existing `_no_real_slack_posts` autouse fixture in the same file (same rationale: a real side effect fires from code paths a test author wouldn't think to check). Individual tests that already patch these paths themselves (e.g. `tests/test_node_circuit_breaker.py`'s `env` fixture) are unaffected — they just re-patch to their own `tmp_path`, redundant but harmless. Full `schwab_safety`-touching test set (~60 files, 599 tests) re-run after the fix: all green, no regressions.

**Also investigated, not a bug**: `schwab_ticker_automation.json`'s real dirty content (`{"STAGE_GUARD_TEST": true}`) is from `scripts/stage_check_order_guard_scenarios.py`, a standalone manual staging script that deliberately writes the real path using a synthetic never-traded ticker, by design — not a test-isolation gap. The 3 pytest tests that call `pause_ticker_automation`/`resume_ticker_automation` directly already patch `TICKER_AUTOMATION_PATH` individually.

**`schwab_token.json` (separate) — resolved 2026-08-15**: `schwab_auth.TOKEN_PATH` mutation during the original incident's 08:10-08:32 window was a genuine authenticated Schwab API call (proven via schwab-py internals), not a test-isolation defect. Both original suspects cleared with hard evidence: `stage_check_order_guard_scenarios.py`'s timestamps don't match, and grepping all 342 session transcripts confirms it was run manually by the user, never via any Claude session; the fake-venue harness was cleared empirically (re-run live with an audit-hook tripwire, zero token accesses). **New finding along the way**: background subagent tool calls (the `Agent` tool, `run_in_background`) don't show up anywhere in the Claude Code transcript store — zero `isSidechain` entries exist for that day despite multiple background agents running, and 2 files were modified 2.5 min after the token write with no visible tool call anywhere. Same blind spot recurred during this investigation itself. The writes themselves are benign (routine OAuth refresh, no order risk) — but a background agent could make a real authenticated call with zero traceable record. Two follow-up ideas raised, both logged as their own `docs/backlog_cache.md` items: blocking background-agent spawning during real trading hours (Claude-Code/hooks-level), and detecting "no attributable source" as a first-class queryable anomaly on `schwab_auth` token writes (directly actionable in this repo).

**Environment note**: this investigation ran in a heavily concurrent shared working tree — multiple other agent sessions were running full-suite pytest and editing other files (`schwab_client.py`, etc.) at the same time, which confounded several naive before/after diffs against the real shared file; the `SCHWAB_STATE_DIR`-isolated-probe technique is what produced a clean, reproducible proof.

Not committed — left for review, per this project's default.

## ✅ [live-trading][HIGH] Resolved 2026-08-16 — stream fast-path fill reconciliation fixed: raw `AccountNumber`→alias resolution + `SchwabOrderID` string/int coercion
Two real production defects found earlier the same session by the fake-venue harness (see this file's own 2026-08-16 harness-build entry / `docs/design.md`'s "AccountNumber"/"drain_fill_queue" 2026-08-16 entries): Schwab's real ACCT_ACTIVITY stream messages carry `AccountNumber` as the raw account number (confirmed against real traffic: `"45111931"`, `"49654983"`, `"90961256"` — never an alias), but `signals_notify.drain_fill_queue` passed it straight into `schwab_client.get_filled_order(account=...)`, which resolves via `_resolve_account_hashes()[account]` — a dict keyed by account ALIAS. Raw number → `KeyError`, thrown after the event was already popped off `schwab_stream.FILL_QUEUE`, silently dropping that event (and the rest of that poll cycle's queue). A second, masked defect: the stream's `SchwabOrderID` is a quoted string, but `get_filled_order` compares it against the broker's numeric `orderId` with no coercion, so the fast path's exact-order lookup always missed even once the first defect was bypassed.

**Design (settled by the user before implementation, no redesign)**: no new accountNumber→alias lookup table/cache. Instead, reuse the EXACT mechanism `schwab_client._resolve_account_hashes()` already trusts — suffix-match each alias's `SCHWAB_ACCOUNT_<ALIAS>` env var against the raw number.

**Fix**:
- `schwab_client.py` (right after `_resolve_account_hashes`, ~line 538): new `resolve_account_alias_from_number(raw_account_number)` — iterates `_live_nicknames()`, matches via `raw_account_number.endswith(os.environ[f"SCHWAB_ACCOUNT_{alias.upper()}"])`. Raises `ValueError` loud on 0 or 2+ matches (mirrors `_resolve_account_hashes`'s own ambiguous-match guard), never silently guesses.
- `signals_notify.py`, `drain_fill_queue()` (~line 4462): resolves `account` via the new helper immediately after popping from `FILL_QUEUE`, before any alias-dependent call; a `ValueError` logs `fast_path_fill_reconciliation`/`account_number_unresolved` and `continue`s to the next queued event — fails safe to the slow `check_auto_fills` poll for just that one event, a strict improvement over the old behavior (a raw KeyError used to propagate through the loop's bare `except Exception: break`, dropping the ENTIRE remaining queue for that cycle, not just one event).
- Same function, two `get_filled_order(...)` calls (orphan-fill alert branch + main poll loop): changed to pass the already-computed `_order_id_int` (previously used only for the local `pending_buys` match) instead of the raw string `order_id` — closes the SchwabOrderID defect as a small, clearly-scoped reuse of existing logic, exactly as specified, no new coercion mechanism introduced.
- Verified no real ambiguity risk: `.env`'s 4 `SCHWAB_ACCOUNT_*` suffixes (`ira`=256, `soxl_ira`=931, `brokerage`=983, `roth`=199) are pairwise non-overlapping (checked programmatically, not by eye).

**Proof — real code path, not a unit test of the helper in isolation**: `fake_venue/scenarios.py`'s legs 2/3 (previously written to document the pre-fix defects) were rewritten to drive `drain_fill_queue → resolve_account_alias_from_number → get_filled_order` end to end through the REAL stream parser and a real-shaped ACCT_ACTIVITY envelope (raw `AccountNumber`, string `SchwabOrderID`, exactly matching real Schwab traffic in both respects at once). New leg 3 adds an idempotent-redelivery check (re-emitting the same already-reconciled fill lands safely in the existing orphan-fill-alert branch instead of raising or double-opening a position). `fake_venue/venue.py` gained `seed_account_number_env()` so the harness's fake aliases (`fv_cash`/`fv_margin`) have real `SCHWAB_ACCOUNT_<ALIAS>` env values to resolve against (the harness normally blanks/bypasses those for order-placement hash lookups via direct `_account_hashes` presetting, which doesn't exercise this specific code path). Harness run: 21/21 checks pass, 0 failing. `tests/test_fake_venue_harness_scenario.py::test_harness_json_report_is_self_consistent` updated to assert the fixed behavior directly (was a defect-tripwire tolerating either old or new behavior).

**Regression found and fixed in 3 pre-existing `fake_broker`-based tests** (`tests/test_part3_gap_resize.py`, `tests/test_fake_broker_drain_fill_queue_scenario.py`, `tests/test_fake_broker_orphaned_fill_alert_scenario.py`): these push a pre-parsed tuple straight onto `FILL_QUEUE` (bypassing the real stream parser, a legitimate distinct testing style for exercising `drain_fill_queue`'s own downstream logic) but had been seeding the `account` field with the bare alias string (`'ira'`/`'soxl_ira'`) rather than a realistic raw account number — i.e., they modeled the very bug this fix closes. Fixed by adding a `RAW_ACCOUNT_NUMBER` constant per file (a fake number ending in the real `.env` suffix for that account, e.g. `'45110256'` for `ira`) and using it only at the `FILL_QUEUE.put(...)` call sites — the existing `ACCOUNT` alias constant is untouched everywhere else (order placement, DB setup). 9 tests failed before this fix, all pass after.

**Paired Opus review (independent-cold + contextual)**: both found zero confirmed bugs, converged independently on the same non-issues (the 0-match-raises divergence from `_resolve_account_hashes`'s silent-omit behavior is intentional/safe since the caller catches `ValueError`; the harness's full-account-number "suffix" doesn't exercise the 2+-match ambiguity branch, a coverage gap in the new function's test surface, not a code defect). No rebuttal round-trip needed — no contradictions between the two reviews to resolve.

Full suite: 1105/1105 passed (was 1096/1105, 9 failures, before the test-fixture fix above — all in the 3 files noted, none in the actual production diff).

## ✅ [tooling] Resolved 2026-08-16 — "ready to clear?" Stop hook redesigned around a marker file instead of "a commit happened this turn"
Original problem: the global `~/.claude/hooks/enforce_ready_to_clear.py` Stop hook triggered off "a `git commit` succeeded this turn" — false-positived on any ad hoc commit outside a real `session wrap`/`session close`, and false-negatived on a wrap that ended with nothing to commit (exactly the moment the reminder matters most, since that's when the session is genuinely done).

**Fix, built via the `update-config` skill**: `scripts/session_cache_update.py` — the one mechanical step both `session wrap` and `session close` always run — now touches `~/.claude/hooks/.session_wrap_active` on success. The hook was rewritten to require the `***** Ready to clear ****` checkpoint line whenever that marker exists and its mtime falls within the current turn (checked against the transcript's own ISO-8601 timestamps via `calendar.timegm`, not `time.mktime`/`time.timezone` which is DST-unsafe for a UTC struct_time). This REPLACES commit-detection entirely, not alongside it — both failure modes traced back to commit being the wrong signal.

Deliberately NOT tied to the assistant remembering to touch a marker "at the start of the routine" — that would reintroduce exactly the memory-dependence this hook exists to route around (manual compliance already failed 4 times, per the hook's own docstring). Tying it to a script that's already mechanically invoked by both routines keeps the fix mechanical.

On success (checkpoint found), the marker is deleted (consumed). On failure, it's left in place so a retry within the same turn is still checked. A stale marker (mtime predating the current turn's start by more than a few seconds' slack) is ignored, so a crashed/interrupted earlier session's leftover marker can't leak a false reminder into an unrelated later turn.

Verified via 4 direct pipe-tests against a real transcript (per the skill's own verification protocol): no marker → silent allow; fresh marker + no checkpoint → block with reason; stale marker → silent allow; fresh marker + checkpoint present → marker consumed, silent allow. Confirmed `session_cache_update.py`'s `WRAP_MARKER` path resolves identically to the hook's own.

## ✅ [live-trading] Accepted residual risk, decided 2026-08-16 — `addon_buying_power_check`'s other-ticker reservation is flat 1x, not leverage-scaled
`schwab_safety.check_order`'s `is_addon_leg` branch (~line 1546/1777) reserves every OTHER ticker's resting-order notional at flat 1x against `buying_power`, while the add-on's OWN notional is required at `ADDON_BUYING_POWER_HEADROOM_MULT` (2x) — a known asymmetry (2026-08-10) that was harmless only while `buying_power == cash` exactly on every addon-enabled account. `check_addon_buying_power_drift` fired for real 2026-08-13: `brokerage` shows `cash=$20,000.00` `buying_power=$40,000.00`, a genuine 2x margin gap — confirmed the assumption is now false, didn't block anything.

**Corrected math analysis, 2026-08-16**: `get_leveraged_buying_power()` denominates `buying_power` relative to the SPECIFIC ticker being checked (`margin_req`: AGQ/ETHU=0.5, JNUG=0.75) — the flat-1x reservation is NOT uniformly conservative; direction depends on which ticker pairing. Checking JNUG against AGQ/ETHU resting orders over-reserves (blocks legit trades only, safe direction). Checking AGQ/ETHU against a JNUG resting order UNDER-reserves (correct reservation would be 1.5x notional, not 1x) — a real potential over-approval path, not just a missed-trade risk.

**Closing rationale**: real mitigation is behavioral, not structural — as long as combined notional exposure across `brokerage`'s 3 tickers (AGQ/ETHU/JNUG) stays near 1x cash rather than pushing toward the 2x/3x leveraged buying-power ceiling, there's enough real headroom that the miscalculation doesn't matter in practice (both correct and buggy math land on "approved" well within real capacity). Confirmed empirically 2026-08-16: a real $40k AGQ order placed without resistance, consistent with base leverage math working correctly for a single-ticker order. **Revisit trigger, explicit**: only if combined exposure across the 3 tickers ever grows toward pushing the leveraged buying-power ceiling — not a vague "someday." Candidate fix if revisited: key off `schwab_client.get_account_margin_requirement(ticker)` instead of a flat 1x — the originally-proposed formula (`other_ticker_notional / get_account_margin_requirement(other_ticker)`) was checked 2026-08-16 and found not confirmed dimensionally correct, needs real verification against live numbers before implementing.

## ✅ [live-trading][security] Decided/skipped 2026-08-16 — don't promote a 2nd `state='live'` sibling on AGQ/`brokerage` (or any ticker+account pair); the scenario this guarded against is structurally unlikely by design, not just currently absent
Original concern (2026-08-10): `check_order`'s duplicate-order guards and `signals_notify.check_live_state_reconciliation` both key off `(ticker, account)`, not per-node, so two genuinely `live` siblings sharing one `(ticker, account)` would block each other's real orders and trip the circuit breaker. Never reachable in practice — AGQ's only `live` node stayed id=203 throughout (verified 2026-08-16: node 41 is `dry_run`, node 193 is `dry_run`, only 203 is `live`).

**User's call, 2026-08-16: skip entirely, not just park.** This project's capital-scaling convention is to grow `starting_notional` on the single top-picked (CAGR-first) node per ticker, not run a 2nd parallel node at worse config quality — a 2nd live AGQ sibling would statistically underperform the already-picked top node, and would also corrupt `liquidity_dollars_per_day`-based sizing checks (which assume one node's notional against the ticker's real volume). The scenario this guardrail protects against is unlikely to ever occur by design, not merely absent today. Revisit only if a genuinely new strategy needing different per-account rules gets added to an existing live ticker+account pair.

## ✅ [live-trading] Resolved 2026-08-16 — `_submit_order_with_retry`/`_submit_replace_with_retry` retry-blind gap fixed: broker state re-checked before every retry attempt (and once more after the last one), not just accepted as a known single-drop risk
Closes the real gap found 2026-08-15 (later): the retry loop blindly resubmitted `place_order`/`replace_order` on any exception, with zero re-verification that a prior attempt hadn't already landed at the broker — under repeated flapping (connection up-down-up mid-placement, not just a single clean drop), N consecutive local "failures" could mean N real orders resting, none confirmed locally.

**Fix** (`schwab_client.py`): before every retry attempt (never the first — nothing to re-check yet) AND once more after the final attempt exhausts (added after review found the last attempt was otherwise the one case an "only check before attempts 2..N" version would miss), the loop now checks the broker's live order book (`get_real_orders`) for an order that could be the missing prior attempt. A candidate must match ticker+side+quantity+orderType exactly, have a status outside `schwab_safety._DUPLICATE_NOT_CONFIRMED_STATUSES` (CANCELED/EXPIRED/REJECTED/REPLACED — reused from the existing duplicate-order guard, not reinvented), and NOT be present in a baseline snapshot of orderIds taken once before attempt 1 (the primary defense against matching a stale pre-existing order — entered-time-plus-a-5s-skew-buffer is kept only as a secondary signal, used alone only if the baseline snapshot itself couldn't be taken). Exactly one match → treat as this call's own success, return its order_id, log `coverage_events(scenario_key='order_retry_duplicate_prevented', result='prevented')`. Zero matches → proceed with the retry as before. More than one match → raise `_AmbiguousBrokerState` (never guess), log `result='ambiguous'`, and post an immediate Slack alert naming the candidate order_ids (distinct from the generic downstream placement-failure alert, since this is a "verify the broker directly" situation). A broker-read failure during the check itself logs `result='check_failed'` and falls back to the pre-existing blind-retry behavior (visible now, was silently invisible before). All 6 real order-placement/replace functions (`place_equity_buy/sell`, `replace_equity_order_with_market`, `place_trailing_buy/sell`, `replace_order_with_trailing_sell`, `place_stop_loss`, `replace_order_with_stop_loss`) thread `account`/`ticker`/`side`/`quantity`/`order_type` through. The two retry functions now return `order_id` directly (extracting it internally via `Utils(...).extract_order_id(r)`) instead of the raw response — audited that no caller anywhere used the raw response for anything else.

**Paired Opus review (independent-cold + contextual, both run against the real diff) found real issues in the first draft, all fixed**: (1) HIGH, both reviewers independently — no order-status filter meant a REJECTED/CANCELED prior attempt could be returned as "already placed," leaving a position genuinely unprotected while the caller believed it succeeded (the exact LABD-incident shape) — fixed via the `_DUPLICATE_NOT_CONFIRMED_STATUSES` filter above. (2) HIGH/MEDIUM, both — no `orderType` match meant e.g. an addon leg's own STOP could be confused with the parent leg's TRAILING_STOP of the same side/quantity — fixed. (3) MEDIUM, both (independently proposed the same fix) — relying on entered-time + a clock-skew buffer alone risked matching a genuinely unrelated stale order placed moments before the loop started — fixed via the baseline-orderId-snapshot approach. (4) MEDIUM, independent-cold reviewer — the last attempt had no check after it, the likeliest attempt to be missed under sustained flapping — fixed via the post-loop final check. (5) LOW, contextual reviewer — `_AmbiguousBrokerState` discarded the original connection error — fixed via `raise ... from last_exc`. (6) MEDIUM, contextual reviewer — ambiguous state got only generic downstream alert treatment — fixed via the immediate, distinct Slack alert at detection time. (7) confirmed regression, both reviewers running the actual suite — moving `extract_order_id` inside the retry loop broke `tests/test_schwab_client.py`'s `_FakeResponse` fixture (missing `.is_error`/`.headers`) — fixed, and the 2 affected tests updated to assert on the new `order_id` return value.

Rebuttal exchange: both reviewers' core findings were independently discovered by both agents (strong convergence, not solo hallucination) and confirmed correct on inspection — no rebuttal needed on the HIGH/MEDIUM items, all fixed as described.

**Independent-cold reviewer's follow-up pass (after the fixes above landed) found 2 more real, previously-unaddressed issues, both fixed**: (8) MEDIUM — `Utils(...).extract_order_id(r)` sat inside the retry loop's `try` block, so a genuinely successful placement whose response failed to parse would be treated as a retryable failure and trigger a real duplicate resubmission (the opposite of what this whole fix exists to prevent) — fixed via `try/except/else` in both retry functions, so extraction failures propagate immediately instead of looping back for another attempt (matches the pre-2026-08-15 behavior, where extraction happened entirely outside the retry loop). (9) LOW/edge-case — `_check_broker_before_retry` could log a `'prevented'` coverage_events row while `existing.get('orderId')` was `None` (a malformed match), then still fall through to a blind resubmit since the caller only treats a non-`None` return as "skip retry" — the log would have claimed a save that didn't happen; fixed to log `'check_failed'` instead in that case. Also flagged: the original 4 tests only exercised `FILLED` orders, so the HIGH order-status-filter fix had no direct regression test, and `_submit_replace_with_retry` had zero test coverage despite the docstring claiming its gap was closed — 2 new tests added: `test_rejected_prior_order_is_not_mistaken_for_a_successful_duplicate` (the exact LABD-incident shape: a REJECTED prior attempt must not be treated as success) and `test_replace_path_also_prevents_a_duplicate_on_a_landed_but_lost_response` (same flapping-duplicate proof, through `replace_order_with_stop_loss` instead of a fresh placement). 6 tests total now in `tests/test_fake_broker_retry_flapping_scenario.py`.

Full suite after all fixes: 1087 passed, 1 pre-existing failure (`tests/test_fake_venue_harness_scenario.py::test_isolation_gate_refuses_production_state` — confirmed via `git stash` unrelated to this change: passes clean on a stash of all tracked changes, fails only in combination with a concurrent session's in-progress, uncommitted fake-venue-harness work already present in this working tree at session start).

New Grid row: `scripts/coverage_registry.py`'s `order_retry_duplicate_prevented` — `not-prod-required` (flapping is connection-quality-dependent, not something to force against a real order, same organic-wait posture as `post_fill_topup`/`market_buy_placement`), `bad_results=['ambiguous','check_failed']`.

New tests: `tests/test_fake_broker_retry_flapping_scenario.py` (4 scenarios against a real fake-broker order book) — (1) a drop-then-landed-but-response-lost sequence proving exactly 1 real order reaches the broker, not 2; (2) a genuine multi-order ambiguity (a concurrent, independent order racing our own lost-response attempt — not a self-inflicted one, since the baseline-snapshot fix makes the retry loop structurally unable to create its own ambiguity) proving the fail-safe halt fires and no 3rd order is placed; (3) the final-attempt-lands case proving the post-loop check catches it; (4) a stale pre-existing same-shaped order proving it does NOT block a genuinely-needed fresh retry. Full suite: 1069 passed, 2 pre-existing-then-fixed `test_schwab_client.py` failures (both from this change, fixed in the same pass, not pre-existing).

## ✅ [live-trading] Resolved 2026-08-14 (evening) — same-bar re-entry cooldown built and shipped; real incident fully root-caused, live gap closed, DB-corruption incident in the review process itself found and cleaned up
Closes the HIGH item found earlier the same day: RETL (`soxl_ira`) exited via TIME at 09:30:54 on 2026-08-13, a fresh trailing-buy re-entry order was placed at 09:31:54 — the same hourly bar, a trade sequence the backtest kernel structurally cannot produce (`_simulate_trail_both`'s per-bar loop only reaches the entry-check branch on bar i+1 after an exit on bar i, never the same iteration).

**Fix**: a same-bar cooldown in `active_signals._scan_buy_signals` — a real (non-paper) node's fresh BUY signal is suppressed unless its bar is strictly newer than that node's most recent real CORE exit's bar. Supporting plumbing, since `trade_log.exit_bar_time` existed in the schema but no real (non-paper) exit path ever populated it: `_stash_exit_decision_bar` (new helper) writes the bar a SELL was decided on into `trail_state['exit_decision_bar']` at the real exit-decision sites; `signals_db.close_position()` auto-derives `exit_bar_time` from that stash when a caller doesn't pass it explicitly (most real closes are async fill-confirmations that don't know the bar); `signals_db.get_last_exit_bar_time(wl_id)` reads it back, scoped to `position_source='core'`. New `tests/test_same_bar_reentry_cooldown.py` (6 tests). Full suite 866/866.

**Two paired-Opus review rounds (independent-cold + contextual) found and fixed 5 more real bugs before shipping** — this is exactly why the review gate exists for live-trading code, not a formality:
1. **A format mismatch that could have crashed the entire entry scan.** The write side originally used `str()` on a pandas Timestamp; a tz-aware or sub-second-precision bar would produce a string the read side's fixed-format `datetime.strptime` couldn't parse, raising an uncaught `ValueError` inside `_guarded("scan_buy_signals", ...)` — aborting the whole poll cycle's entry scan for every node, not just the affected one. Fixed the write side to use `.strftime` (matching the rest of the codebase's convention) and made the read side fail open with a `try/except` rather than propagate, logging a new `result='unparseable_exit_bar'` coverage_event instead of crashing. Pinned with a dedicated test writing a deliberately-corrupt tz-suffixed string.
2. **Drought/add-on legs sharing a wl_id could silently disarm the cooldown on exactly the nodes most likely to need it.** `get_last_exit_bar_time`'s original query had no `position_source` filter — a drought-overlay/add-on leg closing AFTER the real core exit (via `close_addon_leg_real_if_open`/the HANDOFF close, neither of which stashes `exit_decision_bar`) becomes "most recent by exit_time" with a NULL `exit_bar_time`, making the function return `None` and fail the cooldown open. RETL (the incident node) runs both drought and add-on — this bug would have reproduced the exact incident the fix was built to prevent. Fixed with `position_source='core'` in the query; pinned with a dedicated test simulating a later drought-leg close.
3. **Two more real exit paths never stashed a decision bar**: `check_sl_order_fills` (a resting SL/TRAIL order filling on its own, detected by broker-side poll, not our own `check_sell_condition` call) and both manual "Exited"/"MANUAL close" Slack handlers in `signals_handlers.py`. Fixed via a new `signals_compute.current_bar_time(ticker)` helper (derives the same `df_hourly.index[-1]` reference the wired sites use) passed directly to `close_position(exit_bar_time=...)` at all three sites.
4. **A minor `AttributeError` gap**: `close_position`'s new trail_state-JSON-parsing branch only caught `TypeError`/`ValueError`; a non-dict JSON value (`'null'`, `'[]'`) would parse successfully then crash on `.get()` — inside `close_position`, the exit-finalization path for every position in the system. Fixed with an `isinstance(parsed, dict)` guard.
5. **Data corruption in the review process itself, found by the cold review of a separate but concurrent piece of work** (the new `verify_real_trades_vs_kernel.py` script, see the entry below): a fix to `verify_live_parity.py` earlier the same session (`'id': -1` on a synthetic replay node) had silently written 156 real rows into the actual live `cache/live/trading_live.db` — `_throwaway_db()`'s temp-DB isolation patched `active_signals.DB_PATH`, a plain name-binding copy from `from signals_config import DB_PATH` at import time, not the `signals_config.DB_PATH` attribute `signals_db._conn()` actually reads fresh on every call. Root-caused and fixed (`active_signals.cfg.DB_PATH`, the actual shared module attribute); the 156 corrupted rows (unmistakable: `wl_id=-1`, 2023-dated, `account=None`) backed up then deleted. **A second, smaller instance of the identical mistake recurred while building this fix's own test file** — one of the 6 tests in `tests/test_same_bar_reentry_cooldown.py` omitted the `env` fixture (which applies the `signals_config.DB_PATH` monkeypatch), writing a `TEST_COOLDOWN` node + 2 trade_log rows + 4 coverage_events rows into the real live DB. Found by the contextual review, cleaned up the same way, and the fixture converted to `autouse=True` so a future test in that file can't repeat the mistake even if it forgets to declare `env` as a parameter.

**Not fixed, explicitly scoped out**: a HANDOFF exit followed by a same-bar core re-entry is the same kernel-invalid shape, but wasn't argued as in-scope for tonight — flagged as a next-session item if it turns out to matter in practice. Fail-open design (no cooldown data on file for a node) was reviewed and confirmed correct — a genuinely new node's first real exit populates `exit_bar_time` at the moment the SELL is decided, before any re-entry check could read it, so there's no first-exit gap; only truly historical exits predating this fix are silently ungated, an accepted narrow tradeoff over blocking every entry for every existing node.

## ✅ [live-trading][testing] Resolved 2026-08-14 (evening) — built the real "trades must equal backtest" instrument; fixed 2 real pre-existing bugs in the tooling it builds on
Closes the HIGH item found by the Opus plan-challenge earlier the same day (`docs/plans/account_checkin_process.md`): neither `verify_live_parity.py` nor `paper_vs_backtest_reconcile.py` actually answers "did a real trade match what the backtest would have predicted."

**What each existing tool actually does, clarified (not assumed) by reading the code directly**:
- `paper_vs_backtest_reconcile.py` — intentionally paper-only (confirmed with the user, not a gap).
- `verify_live_parity.py` — a code-consistency check between the Numba kernel and `active_signals.py`'s live-orchestration *functions* (`compute_buy_signal`/`check_sell_condition`), replayed against cached historical CSV data (`cache/research/*_1h.csv`). It never reads a real trade — it checks whether two codebases agree on synthetic historical data, a different question from whether a real execution matched. Its own `__main__` block also only exercises 4 hardcoded ticker/strategy combos (`ZScoreBreakout`, `LimitOrderZScoreBreakout` x2, `TrailingExitZScoreBreakout`) — none of them `TrailingBothZScoreBreakout`, the actual live default strategy.

**Real bug #1, found and fixed**: the module docstring claimed `TrailingBothZScoreBreakout`/`TrailingBuyZScoreBreakout` were absent from `compare()` because "active_signals.py has no live entry implementation for the trailing-buy 'wait for bounce' state machine yet (tracked as P0 #3)" — stale as of 2026-07-03, and false today (the live daemon has run this mechanic for months, it's the live default). The real reason is structural to this specific harness: `replay()`'s loop opens a position immediately on the same bar a signal fires — it has no equivalent of the real resting-order bounce-fill state machine (`update_real_pending_buys_running_low`/`_reconcile_fill`, `signals_notify.py`), which fills asynchronously over subsequent bars. `kernel_trades()` already models this correctly for TrailingBoth via `run_backtest_v110`; only `replay()`'s side would need real, non-trivial work to add a multi-bar pending-buy loop. Docstring corrected to state this accurately instead of implying it's just an unwired TODO; the actual multi-bar replay build is not done, flagged as its own future item if ever needed.

**Real bug #2, found and fixed**: `verify_live_parity.py` was crashing unconditionally on its very first call — `replay()`'s synthetic `node` dict never set an `id` key, but `signals_db.open_position()` requires `node['id']` for its dedup lookup. `KeyError: 'id'` on line 1 of `__main__`, confirmed via `git stash` that this predates today's session (not something introduced this session). Fixed with `'id': -1` (safe — `_throwaway_db()` gives every `replay()` call a fresh, empty temp DB, no real id to collide with). Script now runs to completion and reports its own documented "known, expected mismatch" (the look-ahead-bias gap already on file), rather than crashing before it could report anything.

**New script: `scripts/verify_real_trades_vs_kernel.py`** — the actual North Star instrument. Reads real, broker-executed trades directly (`trade_log`, `is_dry_run_sim=0 AND position_source='core' AND wl_id IS NOT NULL` — excludes drought/add-on legs, which have no kernel-replay path, and dry-run-synthesized fills, which aren't real broker executions) and replays each node's real config through the SAME kernel machinery `paper_vs_backtest_reconcile.py` already trusts (`get_trades_and_bars_since`/`get_backtest_trades_in_window`, imported not reimplemented) over the real historical price data for the matching window. Does a greedy nearest-entry-time match (configurable tolerance, default 4h) between real and kernel-predicted trades — a real trade with no kernel counterpart within tolerance is flagged individually, not just folded into an aggregate stat, since that's exactly the shape of divergence that matters (e.g. RETL's 2026-08-13 same-bar re-entry, a trade the kernel structurally cannot produce). Also reports aggregate win-rate/compounded-return/direction-mismatch/trade-count-gap per node, same style as the paper reconciler. `--min-notional` filters to capital-at-stake nodes (matching `CAPITAL_AT_STAKE_THRESHOLD`). Same accepted limitation as the paper reconciler: reads node config as it exists NOW, not as of trade time — a since-reconfigured node will misreport its own history.

**First real run, 2026-08-14**: full scope (all real core trades since 2026-07-15) shows divergence on every `soxl_ira` staged-test node (GDXU/RETL/LABD/ERY/YINN) — expected, not alarming: these are exactly the nodes documented elsewhere as repeatedly reconfigured/restaged (drought config changes, canary consolidation, role reassignment), so "current config != config at trade time" is the dominant, already-known explanation, not new bugs. Scoped to `--min-notional 5000` (genuine capital-at-stake nodes only, matching `CAPITAL_AT_STAKE_THRESHOLD`): only one real trade in scope, SOXL/`ira` (wl_id=45), flagged as having no kernel counterpart — this is `exit_reason='MANUAL'`, a real backdated manual catch-up entry (the same documented mechanism as KORU/SOXL's 2026-07-06 catch-up entries), which is *expected* to not match kernel timing. No unexplained divergence found on real capital-at-stake nodes today — mainly because most of them (AGQ/ETHU/JNUG/DPST/NUGT/SOXL/SOXS/DFEN/GDXU/KORU) have little-to-no closed real trade history yet (flipped live only in the last few days). The tool is proven working; it just hasn't had much real capital-side activity to check yet.

**Not done**: `verify_live_parity.py`'s `replay()` still can't check `TrailingBothZScoreBreakout` (needs the multi-bar pending-buy state machine described above) — not attempted, real scope for a future session if the kernel-vs-live-orchestration-function question (distinct from the kernel-vs-real-trade question this session's new script answers) is ever needed for the live default strategy specifically.

**DFEN split into its own dedicated tranche 0** (`db_cache.remove_tranche_ticker`/`add_tranche_ticker` on the `liquidity_screen` campaign, `scripts/render_liquidity_tranches.py` regenerated `scripts/liquidity_tranches.txt` per the file's own DO-NOT-hand-edit convention) — pulled out of tranche 4 (`JNUG DFEN OILU BOIL`) so it could be forced to resweep independently of the other three, which already had substantial `v5.1` data and would otherwise just cache-skip through. **Tranche 4 (JNUG/OILU/BOIL) ran a genuine fresh full sweep** (not a no-op despite existing v5.1 data — the exact grid combo for this campaign hadn't been fully cached) and completed at 12:03:57 ET, but its mandatory post-sweep `full_db_prune_validate.py` step flagged a real row-count regression and refused to `--swap`: `('JNUG', 'TrailingExitZScoreBreakout', 'v5.1', 20, 1.0, 'open_check'): 1848 -> 1176`. Per the `prune-validation` skill's design (2026-08-07), this is a hard stop requiring investigation before any swap — the outer `run_liquidity_tranches.sh` process exited without writing the tranche_4 marker (by design, the marker is only written after sweep + validated prune + swap, all three).

**Investigated and confirmed a legitimate cause, not data loss or a restart artifact** (the user's initial theory — checked directly, no evidence found: `sweep_runs` shows zero FAILED/gapped runs for JNUG at any date, and rows that initially looked like restart-duplicated generations turned out to be a real `trail_sell_pct` grid dimension). The actual explanation, confirmed via `run_timestamp` breakdown on the flagged group: on 2026-08-11 this exact (ticker, strategy, version, window, z, entry_timing) group had only 1,848 rows total, all clustered in TP=24-30 (best node there: TP=27/SL=3, robust_alpha≈1821.4) — the neighbor-window island logic trivially "kept" all of them because nothing existed outside the window yet. Today's fresh full Phase1 coarse pass added 13,292 new rows spanning the complete TP axis (1-30), surfacing a materially better winner at TP=17/SL=3 (robust_alpha≈2013.0) — a real, better local optimum the earlier thin search never found. The neighbor-window around this new, better winner correctly narrows to 1,176 rows; the old TP=24-30 rows are untouched in the live DB (15,140 = 1,848 + 13,292 total), just no longer part of the kept island since a better point was found elsewhere on the axis. Nothing was lost.

**Session-wrap paired review** (independent-cold Opus + contextual Opus + Sonnet, against the full cumulative diff, required since `schwab_client.py`/`schwab_safety.py`/`signals_*.py` all changed) — both Opus reviewers independently converged on the same **HIGH**: the `has_capital_at_stake` fix above (falling back to the static column only on `_last_sale_recovery` *failure*) is symmetric in the wrong direction — a real brokerage node ($6,000 static, only 17% above the new $5,000 threshold) that closes its first trade at a loss would have its comparison basis floor to the smaller real proceeds and could silently drop below threshold, going alert-dark exactly when it needs MORE visibility, not less (confirmed against the live DB: ERY's real effective notional is already $10 vs. $500 static, from a stale 1-share test trade — the exact shape of failure). **Fixed**: `max(static, effective)` instead of "effective, falling back to static on error" — a node only needs EITHER value to clear the bar, closing both the upward-compounding gap this was built for and the downward-loss gap the review found. Not fixed, flagged for follow-up: `oversell_guard_correct_position`'s Grid row can flip `verified-live` off any ordinary successful SELL, not specifically the "2 live nodes share a ticker in different accounts" scenario the row's own description names (pre-existing, not part of this diff — the concurrent session's own same-night fix already made the success path log at all). **Real duplicate found in `scripts/coverage_registry.py`'s `BEST_HARNESS` dict**: the same 5 new scenario_key names appear twice (once near `kill_switch_block`, once near `two_nodes_same_ticker_diff_accounts`) — traced to the concurrent session independently adding identical-named entries for what looks like the same underlying fix, landing in the same shared file; deliberately left unresolved rather than guessing which copy to remove mid-session.

## ✅ [backtest][data] Resolved 2026-08-12 (night) — `prune_backtest_cache.py --swap` corrupted the live research DB via a stale orphaned WAL file; caught before any downstream use, root-caused, and fixed
Tranche-script (`run_liquidity_tranches.sh`) runs kept aborting on `full_db_prune_validate.py`'s row-count-regression gate (JDST/UWM kept-count dropped 14252→12852 / 1004→472 vs. the last recorded prune). Investigated directly: content fingerprint matched exactly (0/1,613 island groups mismatched, same run), no bad-tick hits, no `data_mutation_log` entries — traced to a real, legitimate resweep of those two groups under commit `04d2d78` (the FAS/FAZ session's ~1.5% trigger-price look-ahead-bias fix), which genuinely shrinks the cliff-safe island. Confirmed not a bug; wrote the validation sentinel manually (content-fingerprint-based, independent of the advisory row-count check) and ran `--swap`.

**The swap corrupted the resulting live DB.** `PRAGMA integrity_check`/any query touching `sqlite_master` failed with `malformed database schema (SPXL)`; with `PRAGMA writable_schema=ON`, `sqlite_master` rows came back shaped like raw `backtest_cache`/`candidate_nodes` data (e.g. `(None, 'SPXL', 'TrailingBothZScoreBreakout', 1)`) instead of schema entries — a corrupted root-page pointer in the schema b-tree.

**Root cause, confirmed via code + timeline**: `trading_universe.db` runs in **WAL journal mode**. `cmd_swap()` (`scripts/prune_backtest_cache.py`) renamed only the two `.db` file paths via `shutil.move()`, never touching the `-wal`/`-shm` sidecar files WAL mode creates. At the moment of this swap, a still-running diagnostic query (`top_safe_nodes.py`, launched earlier in the same session to cross-check the regression) held an open read connection to the original DB, which blocked SQLite from checkpointing the WAL before close — leaving a live, un-checkpointed `trading_universe.db-wal` (9.95MB of real pending frames) orphaned under the canonical filename once the original `.db` was renamed away. The pruned file was then moved into that same canonical name, and SQLite auto-adopts any `-wal` file it finds next to a `.db` by filename adjacency alone, with no check that it actually belongs to that file's page layout — it replayed WAL frames encoded against the *original* (much larger) file's page numbering onto the *pruned* file's completely different layout, overwriting the schema page with unrelated table data.

**Caught before any damage**: the corrupted file was never read by anything downstream — found immediately while trying to update `full_db_prune_validate.py`'s `KEPT_COUNT_LOG` baseline post-swap. Reverted by hand (`mv` back to the pre-swap original, confirmed `integrity_check: ok` + correct row count 12,984,373) before investigating further. Corrupted file preserved as `trading_universe.db.CORRUPTED_20260812_2317` for reference, not deleted.

**Fixed in `cmd_swap()`**: before either rename, run `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` against `DB_PATH` and refuse to swap if it reports `busy` or any remaining `log_frames` (means another connection is still open — the exact precondition that caused this) or if a `-wal`/`-shm` sidecar somehow survives a clean checkpoint. Also defensively checks `PRUNED_PATH` for sidecars post-build (none expected — the attached build DB defaults to rollback-journal mode, confirmed empirically — but not assumed).

**Gap this exposed**: `full_db_prune_validate.py`'s row-level fingerprint check never calls `PRAGMA integrity_check` on the built file — it can verify byte-for-byte row content is correct while missing schema-level corruption entirely, since the corruption here was introduced by the swap step, strictly after that script's own POST-fingerprint scan had already passed clean. Not yet added — worth considering before the next prune attempt.

Live DB currently un-pruned (back to the 12,984,373-row original); the legitimate JDST/UWM resweep result is real and still valid, just not yet re-attempted through a validated swap. `KEPT_COUNT_LOG` baseline not yet updated for JDST/UWM (the clean-pass write path never ran) — the next validator run will re-flag the same already-diagnosed regression; resolve the same way (confirm unchanged, write sentinel manually) or extend the validator to accept a manually-confirmed baseline.

## ✅ [live-trading][coverage] Resolved 2026-08-13 — canary/dry_run infrastructure consolidated from 11 tickers onto FAS/FAZ in `soxl_ira`; 4 real bugs found and fixed along the way
Session started from the nightly EOD routine (daemon down all day after a Windows-forced reboot, see the outage/incident-report thread earlier same session) and a real discovery mid-routine: `canary_time_exit` (XLF/FAZ) showed `wired-never-fired` in `coverage_registry.py`'s Grid despite real `trade_log` proof of repeated correct TIME exits through 2026-08-11 — traced to a genuine, still-open bug in `compute_status`'s `scenario_expectations` branch (`coverage_deviations` only logs failures, so a scenario passing cleanly every day is indistinguishable from one never checked; filed separately as HIGH priority, not fixed this session).

That investigation surfaced the real insight: the config (`z_score_threshold=0.1`/`window=5`), not the specific ticker, is what makes a canary fire reliably — confirmed directly against real cached hourly data (FAS/FAZ both cross the entry threshold on 40%+ of bars at that config, near-identical daily vol ~3.0% std). Given that, the previous design (11 different tickers — DIA/FAZ/IVV/IWM/JDST/QID/QQQ/SDOW/SPXU/TWM/XLF, `account='ira'`, each running one detuned scenario) wasn't buying real robustness for the tracking-surface cost.

**Consolidated onto FAS (3x bull financials)/FAZ (3x bear financials)** — a true matched-leverage inverse pair, user's explicit call (rejected an initial XLF/FAZ 1x/3x-mismatched proposal). 12 new `state='dry_run'` nodes built directly in `account='soxl_ira'` (not `ira`) via `scripts/build_fas_faz_canary_nodes.py` — one node per canary-letter scenario (A-F) per ticker, each carrying the real, already-tuned exit-side config from the ticker it replaces (queried from the live DB first, not reinvented). The G "bull/bear pair" scenario (previously JNUG/JDST, cross-underlying correlation design) was redefined — user confirmed explicitly via AskUserQuestion before implementation — to check FAS-vs-FAZ's own inverse relationship, sharing the same node/config as the F "TIME-only exit" scenario.

`staged_test_config` rows written per node (`scripts/seed_fas_faz_staged_config.py`), `scenario_expectations` repointed from the old 11 tickers to the new nodes (`scripts/repoint_canary_scenario_expectations.py` — old rows deactivated via `active=0`, not deleted), `baseline_config` seeded via the existing `seed_baseline_config.py`.

**4 real bugs found and fixed while building this**:
1. `add_node`'s dedup key (ticker/strategy/version/window/take_profit/stop_loss/max_hold_hours/arm_sell_pct/trail_buy_pct/trail_sell_pct/account/paper_role) does not include `entry_timing` or `fixed_sl` — the pinned-entry scenario (differs from full-lifecycle only by `entry_timing`) silently no-op'd as a duplicate on the first build attempt. Fixed by making `max_hold_hours` deliberately distinct (47 vs 48).
2. `FAS` was missing from `SCHWAB_AUTOMATION_TICKERS` in `.env` (FAZ was already present) — added.
3. New nodes' `starting_notional=$10,000` (copied from the old `ira`-based canaries) exceeded `soxl_ira`'s real `notional_cap=$3,000` — `signals_invariants.py` caught this live; corrected to `$500`, matching the existing small-canary precedent.
4. `signals_invariants._config_field_mismatch` can't numerically compare a non-numeric `expected_config` field (`float()` raises on a string) and reports it as a mismatch regardless of whether it actually matches — including `entry_timing='close'` (an exact match) in a `staged_test_config` row produced a false drift violation. Worked around by keeping `expected_config` strictly numeric (matching the existing `baseline_config` role's own convention) and moving descriptive fields into the free-text `notes` param; the underlying checker limitation itself is not fixed.

**New regression test**: `tests/test_dry_run_sim.py::test_two_dry_run_nodes_same_ticker_fills_and_exits_dont_cross_contaminate` — confirms the real risk this design depends on (multiple `dry_run` nodes sharing one ticker+account, several open at once) doesn't cause fill/exit cross-contamination. Research beforehand (via Explore agent, during plan-mode design) had already confirmed `update_dry_run_buys`/`check_dry_run_sim_sells` iterate per-row by `wl_id`, not by `(ticker, account)` lookup — the test makes that structural safety a pinned, verified fact instead of an inference.

**Old 11 tickers' nodes deliberately NOT retired** — still running in parallel in `ira`, unchanged, until the new FAS/FAZ nodes organically fire and are confirmed correct (project's standing "never force/fake a live test" convention). Retiring them is an explicit follow-up, not part of this build.

Verification: `signals_invariants.py` clean, `scripts/status_check.py`/`scripts/coverage_registry.py` show the new nodes correctly, full suite 812/812. Full narrative: `docs/design.md`'s 2026-08-13 entry.

## ✅ [portfolio][tax] Decided 2026-08-12 (evening) — annual tax/reserve/reinvest cycle: reserve 55-60% of profits (taxes owed + next year's estimates), reinvest/use the rest, repeat
User's "simple but conservative" theory (the open item this resolves): trade the full calendar year without interruption. Year 1 profits are effectively a wash — ~45% goes to actual tax owed, plus another ~49% set aside as a safe-harbor reserve for year 2's quarterly estimated payments (since year 2's estimate requirement is based on year 1's now-much-higher income), leaving only ~6% net addition to trading capital. From year 2 onward (once the reserve cycle is established), the same math repeats each profitable year: reserve 55-60% (current year's tax owed + next year's estimates), the remaining ~40% either compounds back into the strategy or is used personally. Near year-end, real tax decisions (loss harvesting against realized losses on file, exact reserve sizing) still need to happen, but the mechanism is otherwise mechanical/repeatable.

**Real insight surfaced in the same conversation**: the tax reserve doesn't have to sit idle in a savings account — parking it in `brokerage` (the account the $20k margin loan was drawn against, per the same-day margin-funding decision above) reduces the debit balance during the part of the year it's held there, lowering the effective margin interest cost. Directly compounds with that decision rather than being a separate, competing use of the cash.

**Tax-timing question raised and resolved in discussion**: whether the IRS's quarterly-estimated-payment requirement creates an underpayment-penalty risk during year 1 (before any trading-related estimates have been paid). Resolved: no — the federal safe-harbor rule (estimated payments/withholding ≥100%/110% of the *prior* year's total tax liability avoids the penalty regardless of the current year's actual liability) means year 1's low prior-year baseline already covers it. The exposure only appears in year 2, once the prior year's liability includes the trading gains — which is exactly what the "set aside for next year's estimates" step in the plan above already exists to cover. Not a gap in the plan; confirmed consistent with it. (Not tax/legal advice — general mechanism as understood in conversation, worth confirming with a CPA before relying on it.)

**Still open, not part of this decision**: `k1_tax.py`/`scripts/k1_tax_forecast.py` still need real 2026 trade data (synthetic-only today) to turn this from a conceptual plan into real numbers; the wash-sale/cost-basis tracker (`scripts/sim_wash_sale_impact.py`) still has AGQ's numbers known-wrong pending a Section 1256 rebuild; looking up current real realized losses (the other half of the original open item) also not done this session.

## ✅ [live-trading][portfolio] Decided 2026-08-12 (evening) — keep `brokerage`'s full $60k margin funded continuously rather than drawing/repaying around each trade
User took a $20k margin loan against another account to fund `brokerage` (target $60k total, for AGQ/ETHU/JNUG at ~$20k each) and questioned whether that's the right strategy given these three don't hold positions continuously. Checked real backtested hold-time utilization (days-in-market ÷ full backtest span, entry-fill to exit, wall-clock hours): **AGQ 58.4%** (651.8 of 1,115 days), **JNUG 50.8%** (541.0 of 1,065 days), **ETHU 29.1%** (212.2 of 730 days, shorter data history). At an assumed ~6% annual margin rate, the difference between funding the full $60k continuously (~$3,600/yr) vs. a utilization-weighted draw (~$1,660/yr) is ~$2,000/yr.

**Decision: fund the full $60k continuously.** Two reasons converged: (1) `brokerage` doesn't net cash with `ira`/`roth`/`soxl_ira` (confirmed — one-account-per-ticker model, no shared pool, see `project_account_segregation_model`), so hitting the lower utilization-weighted number would require manually transferring cash in/out of `brokerage` around every entry/exit (AGQ/JNUG trade roughly every few weeks per the backtest) — real transfer friction and the risk of being short cash right when a signal fires; (2) $2k/yr is small relative to $60k of capital deployed into strategies whose backtested annual returns are in the hundreds-of-percent range — if the edge holds up even partially, the convenience cost is noise, and the execution-risk cost of manual draw/repay timing likely exceeds it anyway.

**Not done**: whether the three tickers' open positions overlap heavily in time (which would matter for a true peak-margin-draw question, distinct from average utilization) was raised but not checked — moot now given the "keep it fully funded" decision, but would matter again if this gets revisited.

## ✅ [backtest][data] Resolved 2026-08-12 (evening) — raw hourly CSVs had zero retention/traceability; `sweep_runs` now records the loaded data window per run, and `data_manager.py`'s sync now logs when it silently revises an existing bar
Found investigating JNUG's v5-vs-v5.1 `backtest_cache` divergence (56 trades/~150-395% strategy_return on 2026-08-08 04:03 vs 149-154 trades/~994-2419% on 2026-08-11 09:23, identical node config). Confirmed not a bad tick (`scan_bad_ticks.py --tickers JNUG` clean) and not a `data_mutation_log` split-guard rescale (0 rows for JNUG — that table only fires on a detected-split discontinuity). JNUG also isn't on the 2026-08-11 liquidity-tranche backfill's ~46-ticker list (`scripts/liquidity_tranches.txt`), so this was a separate, previously-unknown instance of the same underlying gap: `run_timestamp` on each `backtest_cache` row proves *when* a sweep ran, but `JNUG_1h.csv` is a single mutable file with no backup/versioning — every subsequent daily sync overwrote it in place, so the actual bar values from either run's moment couldn't be diffed against today's file. Same root cause as the 2026-07-22 "data traceability" decision (`data_mutation_log`, built 2026-08-08) — deliberately scoped to split-guard rescales only at the time.

**Fix 1 — `run_optimization_sweep.py`**: `sweep_runs` gained `data_start`/`data_end` (real min/max Datetime across each run's tickers' cached hourly CSVs, read via new `_tickers_data_date_range()` at `start_sweep_run()` time) — every future sweep/sub-sweep run now records the data window it actually loaded, the "what data did this run see" counterpart to the existing `git_commit`/`kernel_dirty` ("what code ran it"). One real bug caught during implementation: the first version of `_tickers_data_date_range()` used `df.empty` to check for no data after `pd.read_csv(..., usecols=[0])` — `df.empty` is `True` whenever there are zero *columns*, not just zero rows, and `usecols=[0]` intentionally leaves zero data columns (only the index) — every real ticker was silently returning `(None, None)`. Fixed to check `len(df.index) == 0` instead; verified against JNUG/AGQ (real dates) and a nonexistent ticker (clean `None, None`, no crash).

**Correction, same day, paired review (independent-cold + contextual, CRITICAL)**: `data_start` was initially backfilled across all 1,128 existing `sweep_runs` rows on the claim "safe: a ticker's earliest cached bar practically never moves." **That claim was wrong, and the backfill actively fabricated provenance on the exact JNUG rows this feature exists to explain.** `scripts/backfill_hourly_history.py` (built 2026-08-11, the day before the JNUG rows in question) explicitly re-extends a ticker's cached history *backward* on demand, and was run across 218 tickers that same day — including JNUG, whose earliest bar moved from 2025-06-27 to 2023-09-12 (confirmed: `trading_incidents id=4`, `docs/conversation_summary.md`'s 2026-08-11 entry "190 successfully extended"). The backfill silently stamped 2023-09-12 onto JNUG's `sweep_runs` rows from 2026-08-08 04:03-04:53 — runs that, per this very entry's own investigation, had zero data before 2025-06-27 at the time. **Reverted**: `UPDATE sweep_runs SET data_start = NULL WHERE data_start IS NOT NULL AND data_end IS NULL` — cleanly identifies the 1,128 backfilled (not genuinely captured) rows, since `data_end` is never backfilled, only set together with `data_start` by a real live `start_sweep_run()` call (11 such genuine rows preserved). Backed up (`trading_universe.db.bak_pre_datastart_revert_*`) before the revert. Same review also found+fixed: a HIGH crash-safety gap (comparison/`strftime` calls sat outside the CSV-read `try`, so a tz-aware or malformed CSV could crash the whole sweep before any `FAILED` status is recorded — verified 0/1,476 current CSVs trigger it, but real going forward), SPY's own CSV wasn't included in the scanned set despite backing every alpha number, and the `sweep_runs` schema migration's check-then-act `ALTER TABLE` had a narrow concurrent-process race (wrapped in try/except, matching the sibling `backtest_cache` pattern). Known limitations documented, not fixed this pass: union-across-tickers loses per-ticker resolution for multi-ticker runs; the window is captured once at start, not re-checked at completion; a min/max span can't detect an in-place value mutation that doesn't change the span. Full detail: `docs/design.md`'s 2026-08-13 addendum.

**Fix 2 — `data_manager.py`**: `fetch_live_data_smart` (the actual fetch/merge path both the live daemon's `data_collector.py` sync loop and every backfill script depend on) now logs a revision-diff summary on every write — new-bar count vs. how many pre-existing (overlapping) bars had their OHLC values silently changed (via `keep='last'` in the merge, meaning a fresh Yahoo value always wins over what was already cached). Deliberately compares only Open/High/Low/Close, not Volume — intraday volume figures normally trickle upward as more trades report for the current session, which would otherwise false-positive on every same-day resync (confirmed live: JNUG's real test sync showed Volume ticking 13394→13396 and correctly logged "revised 0 existing bar(s)"). Uses `logging.info`/`logging.warning` rather than `print()`, unlike the rest of this function — confirmed by grep that this function's existing `print()` calls never reach `data_collector.log` at all (no redirect captures them), while `logging` calls do, via the root-logger handlers `data_collector.py` installs at import time. This doesn't prevent a silent revision (Yahoo's data is still trusted as-is) — it makes one detectable the day it happens instead of invisible until a downstream sweep divergence forces a manual investigation with nothing to point to.

Both pieces tested: `run_optimization_sweep.py` changes verified via `py_compile` + a live `start_sweep_run()` call against the real DB (row inserted, checked, deleted); `data_manager.py`'s revision-diff logic unit-tested in isolation (synthetic new+revised bars, correct classification), then integration-tested against `fetch_live_data_smart` with a throwaway seeded cache (monkeypatched `yf.download`, correctly detected 1 new + 1 revised bar, cache file cleaned up after), then **live-tested for real** against JNUG (backed up first) — correctly logged 0 new/0 revised while Volume alone ticked, no false positive.

**Still open, not part of this fix**: JNUG's actual pre-2026-08-11 bar values remain unrecoverable — this only prevents the *next* occurrence of this class of divergence from being unexplainable, it doesn't recover what already happened. `node_candidate_trace.py`'s sweep-run display (`started_at`/git commit/DIRTY flag) doesn't yet surface the new `data_start`/`data_end` fields — a natural follow-up, not done this session.

## ✅ [live-trading] Resolved 2026-08-12 (evening) — `paper_trading.update_paper_buys` priced its trailing-buy fill simulation off a stale cached hourly bar instead of a live tick; fixed
Found while investigating why paper trading's real trade history diverged sharply from a fresh backtest replay (see `docs/research_log.md`'s 2026-08-12 (evening) entry for the full investigation, including 3 other explanations that were NOT this bug). `update_paper_buys()` — the poll-loop function that tracks a paper trailing-buy's `running_low`/trigger across repeated polls until it "fills" — sourced its price entirely from `signals_compute._current_price()`, which reads the last row of the cached hourly-bar CSV (`_load_cache`), refreshed only whenever the separate background data-collector process next runs — not a live tick. `compute_buy_signal` (the entry *signal* check) already used a genuine live 1-minute yfinance fetch for its own price; the fill-tracking loop afterward did not, an inconsistency between the two halves of the same trailing-buy lifecycle.

**Real, concrete proof via the live verbose poll log** (`logs/active_signals_verbose.log`): SOXL gapped up to a real Open of $140.06 on 2026-07-27 (the real trailing-buy trigger was $140.5435, missed by $0.46 on the one poll that caught the fresh price), then crashed to a Low of $120.73 within the same hourly bar. `_current_price` returned the *identical* $140.08 on every ~34-second poll for 29 straight minutes (the daemon's own poll loop never stalled — only the underlying cached price was frozen), then jumped straight to $132.53 once the background collector's cache finally refreshed, well past the real gap. Paper's simulated fill never saw the brief window where price was actually near the trigger, and instead chased the already-crashed price down from there, eventually bounce-filling at $121.615 around 11:21am — a large, real divergence from what the corrected production kernel (which does correctly apply the real 2026-07-19 gap-through-trigger fix) computed for the same signal: an immediate fill at the real $140.06 Open.

**Fix**: extracted `signals_compute._live_tick_price(ticker, fallback)` — the same yfinance 1-minute-interval fetch `compute_buy_signal` already used inline, just factored out so it's reusable — and wired it into `update_paper_buys()`: after `_current_price()`'s existing None/staleness gate passes (left unchanged — still needed to feed the entry-abandon-timeout logic's no-data case), the price is upgraded via `_live_tick_price()` before being used in the `running_low`/trigger comparison. `compute_buy_signal` itself now calls the same extracted helper instead of its old inline try/except — pure extraction, no behavior change there.

**Paired Opus review (independent-cold + contextual) found 1 real HIGH bug in the first version of this fix, before it shipped**: both reviewers independently caught that the live-tick upgrade applied unconditionally to *every* pending paper buy, including `paper_role='daily_sync'` (daily-track) nodes — 11 real `TrailingBothZScoreBreakout` daily-track nodes exist today (none had filled yet), and daily-track's entire purpose is to isolate price-source timing (live tick vs. cached hourly Close) as the one variable against a backtest replay; this fix would have silently contaminated that experiment the first time any of them actually filled. An identical guard already exists a few lines away in `evaluate_drought_entry` for the same reason (found by an earlier review, 2026-08-09) — missed here because `pb['node']`, the frozen signal-time snapshot `update_paper_buys` iterates, doesn't carry `paper_role` at all (not in `signals_db._PENDING_BUY_NODE_KEYS`). Fixed: a live re-read (`db.get_watch_list_node_by_id(wl_id)`) now gates the upgrade, skipping it for `daily_sync` nodes. Both reviewers also flagged (MEDIUM) that the upgraded price had no bound against a single anomalous extended-hours print (`_live_tick_price` uses `prepost=True`) permanently ratcheting `running_low` down via its monotonic `min()` — unlike `signals_notify.update_real_pending_buys_running_low`, which already solved this exact problem for real orders via a capped-drop bound (`MAX_RUNNING_LOW_DROP_PCT`, 20%, from the 2026-07-31 audit). Fixed by reusing that same bound (moved to `signals_helpers.py` so `paper_trading.py` can import it — `signals_notify.py` itself imports `paper_trading`, so the reverse import isn't possible). Full pytest suite reconfirmed green after both fixes (811 passed), `scripts/live_sim_harness.py` 7/7.

Real live trading (`schwab_client`/`schwab_safety`) is entirely unaffected — paper trading never calls those modules.

## ✅ [backtest][tooling] Resolved 2026-08-12 (evening) — `scripts/paper_vs_backtest_reconcile.py` had two real bugs producing a false "paper diverged from backtest" reading: wrong node selection, and an unbounded full-history backtest replay
Found while investigating a user question about paper-trading performance (see `docs/research_log.md`'s 2026-08-12 (evening) entry for the full trace). Both bugs made the reconciliation tool compare paper's real trades against the wrong reference, independent of whether paper trading itself was doing anything wrong.

**Bug 1 — wrong node config.** The script selected each ticker's comparison node via `drought_detection_test.load_nodes()` (`MIN(id)` among currently-`state='paper'` `watch_list` rows). This breaks in two ways: (a) once a ticker's real paper-trading node is promoted to `state='live'` (e.g. SOXL wl_id=92), it drops out of the `state='paper'` filter entirely, silently falling back to a same-ticker sibling that never traded at all; (b) even while still `state='paper'`, a ticker can have many duplicate/candidate nodes (confirmed for every ticker checked: HIBL/USD/SOXL/KORU/YANG/AGQ/UDOW each had 5-14), and `MIN(id)` has no reason to land on the one with real `paper_trade_log` history — confirmed each mismatched node had a genuinely different strategy class, window, z-threshold, and fixed_sl than the one that actually traded. Fixed via new `resolve_live_track_nodes_by_activity()`: resolves nodes by which `wl_id` actually has rows in `paper_trade_log`/`paper_positions`/`paper_pending_buys`, not a positional guess. Reports per-`wl_id` now (not per-ticker), since a ticker can have more than one live-track node with real history (e.g. HIBL's original node 89 and its since-promoted-to-live clone 154).

**Bug 2 — cold-start artifact.** Even with the right node, the backtest replay (`get_trades_and_bars`) ran over the *full* multi-year price history unconditionally — so it could be simulated as still holding a position "opened" weeks or months before the paper node even existed, silently suppressing any signal evaluation during the comparison window (the position-tracking loop can't check for a new entry while it believes it's still in an old one). Confirmed real, not hypothetical, for 2 of 5 tickers directly checked: KORU's full-history replay was mid-trade 2026-07-17→07-21 (spanning its own 07-20 creation), YANG's was mid-trade continuously from 07-20 through 08-11 (22 days). HIBL/USD/SOXL were confirmed already flat at their own creation dates — proving the fix only changes results where the full-history replay's own trade list proves it should, not as a blanket assumption. Fixed via new `get_trades_and_bars_since(node, sim_start)`: same kernel mirror functions (`simulate_trail_both_annotated`/`simulate_trail_exit_chaos`), same full indicator lookback (`sma_arr`/`std_arr`/`trend_arr` stay unsliced, since they're indexed per-calendar-day via `daily_idx`, not by array position — slicing them too would misalign every lookup), but the hourly OHLC/timestamp arrays fed to the bar-by-bar simulator loop are sliced to start at `sim_start` (the node's own `added_at`) so the simulator starts flat, matching paper trading's own real starting condition.

**Paired Opus review (independent-cold + contextual), same diff as the `update_paper_buys` fix above, found 2 more real issues here before it shipped.** The two reviewers *disagreed* on one point — the independent-cold review flagged sim_start's timezone as broken (`added_at` UTC vs. naive-ET bars); the contextual review checked and reported both sides as already tz-naive and fine. Resolved by direct verification against the real DB rather than trusting either claim: `watch_list.added_at`'s schema default is `datetime('now')` with no `'localtime'` modifier, and SQLite's `datetime('now')` is UTC (confirmed: `datetime('now')` returned `12:40:59` vs. `datetime('now','localtime')`'s `08:40:59` on this EDT host) — the cold review was correct, the contextual review's claim was a factual error in that review. Currently latent for every node checked in this investigation (all created outside trading hours, so the ~4h offset doesn't cross a bar boundary) but real for at least one existing node created intraday (AGQ wl_id=169, `added_at` 2026-08-06 11:16:16 UTC = 07:16 ET) — a naive comparison would silently drop a real inception-day signal, reproducing the exact false-divergence shape this fix exists to eliminate. Fixed: `sim_start` now converts `added_at` from UTC to naive US/Eastern before slicing (the `start`-fallback path, already a plain date string, needs no conversion).

Both reviewers also independently flagged that `resolve_live_track_nodes_by_activity`'s activity-only filter makes a genuinely-inactive live-track node (DPST, GDXU, NUGT as of this session — real nodes, zero paper trades ever) vanish from the report entirely, rather than showing "backtest fired N, paper fired zero" — exactly the shape of question this whole investigation started from (YANG). Fixed: a ticker with no active node now still gets exactly one row (lowest-id `state='paper'` node, falling back to lowest-id overall), verified live — DPST/GDXU/NUGT now correctly show `paper_n=0` instead of being silently absent.

Also caught: the contextual review found the original writeup of the "HIBL/USD mode-flip" explanation (see `docs/research_log.md`'s 2026-08-12 (evening) entry) understated its scope — `watch_list_audit` shows all 10 v5 live-track nodes flipped in the same transaction, not just HIBL/USD, so part of SOXL's own divergence is this same operational outage, not the fill-price bug alone. Corrected in the research log.

This script is offline/research tooling only — not part of the live daemon, no live-execution impact. Full pytest suite green after all fixes (811 passed).

## ✅ [live-trading] Resolved 2026-08-12 — real, unmonitored Schwab margin-order testing against `brokerage` (found a real async-rejection shape + a real "no resize lever" gap); AGQ/ETHU/JNUG resized $2,000→$6,000 core each; new `starting_notional_override` lever built
Prompted by the user pushing back hard on the leverage-aware buying-power fix ("no it's not - i promise") -- rather than argue from the math alone, ran real live order tests against `brokerage` (market closed, ~2am ET, so no fill risk before cancel). Real findings, all confirmed via direct API/order-state checks, not inference: (1) Schwab genuinely does allow ~$40,000 notional AGQ against the $20,000-equity account (confirms `equity/margin_req` — the leverage-aware calc built earlier this session — is correct, not overstated); (2) Schwab's real order acceptance is a TWO-STAGE process — an order gets an ID and shows "accepted" at submission, but a real risk/margin check runs ASYNCHRONOUSLY after, and can reject it minutes later (`firmActionType: "CANCELED_BY_FIRM"`, `statusDescription: "You do not have enough available cash/buying power for this order."`, visible via `get_order`'s full response, not just `status`) — reproduced twice (a 2nd concurrent $40k order got the async rejection because a 1st resting order had already reserved the same buying power); (3) this exact scenario is already correctly guarded in production code and could not have happened through the real order-placement path — `schwab_safety.check_order`'s `_has_open_buy_order_for_ticker` (same-ticker) and `_reserved_other` (cross-ticker, add-on path, with the `2.0x` headroom multiplier) guards would have blocked the 2nd order outright; the manual test only reached this state because it called `schwab_client`/the raw API directly, bypassing `schwab_safety` entirely (same bypass pattern as `scripts/live_sanity_check.py`, deliberately used here for the same reason). Net: the code's own defenses are sound; what was learned is Schwab-API-behavior, useful context but not a code-fix trigger. Real orders never filled (market closed throughout); all resolved to CANCELED/REJECTED, zero real exposure remained at any point after each check.

**Real design gap surfaced along the way**: `signals_helpers._last_sale_recovery` (real order sizing) only falls back to `starting_notional` when a node has NO real closed trade yet — once one exists, sizing compounds permanently off that trade's actual proceeds, and a later `starting_notional` edit has silently NO effect (same root mechanism as the LABD 0-share basis-lock bug, but for growing a position rather than shrinking it to unbuyable). No existing lever to deliberately resize a node once real history exists. Built `watch_list.starting_notional_override` (nullable REAL, `signals_db.set_starting_notional_override`/`clear_starting_notional_override`, both audit-logged) — when set, `_last_sale_recovery` returns it directly, bypassing both the trade_log lookup and the plain `starting_notional` fallback, until explicitly cleared (not one-shot, by design — a signal check can call the sizing function more than once before an order actually places). 10 new tests (`tests/test_starting_notional_override.py`), including one that pins the underlying bug itself (`test_starting_notional_edit_has_no_effect_once_history_exists`) so a future change can't silently reintroduce reliance on the broken path. Real live DB migrated (backed up, additive-only, confirmed via `PRAGMA integrity_check`/row-count match). `signals_invariants.py` clean after.

**Real config change applied**: AGQ (wl_id=203)/ETHU (201)/JNUG (205) `starting_notional` raised $2,000→$6,000 each (3×$6k=$18k core, $2k buffer against $20k real equity; add-on doubles each to ~$12k total if triggered) — the plain field worked cleanly here since none of the 3 had any real trade_log history yet (override lever not needed this time, built for next time). `staged_test_config` baselines cleared+reseeded for all 3 via `seed_baseline_config.py` so the daily drift check reflects the intentional change.
