## ✅ [live-trading][security] Resolved 2026-08-11 (late) — hardcoded `schwab_safety.ACCOUNTS`/`schwab_client.NICKNAMES` replaced by a DB-backed `accounts` table ("Option 1.5"); overloaded `account_type` split; 3 tax-advantaged substring guesses replaced with an explicit column
Real trigger: user funded two new real Schwab accounts this session (`brokerage` $20k genuine Reg-T margin, `roth` $60k confirmed real limited-margin) and linked them via OAuth. Renaming/adding an account previously meant a manual find-and-replace sweep across two independent, hand-synced hardcoded Python structures (`schwab_safety.ACCOUNTS` dict, ~30 read sites; `schwab_client.NICKNAMES` list) with nothing enforcing they stayed in sync — plus two known, already-documented real bugs: (1) tax-advantaged-account detection was a substring guess (`any(kw in account.lower() for kw in ("ira","roth","sep"))`, in 3 places) whose own comments admitted it would "fail open on a future name like 'hsa'/'401k'", silently disabling the K-1/UBTI compliance guard; (2) `account_type` was overloaded, answering two unrelated questions (same-day cash-settlement eligibility vs. real margin-borrowing capability) — already known wrong for `soxl_ira`.

**Design, "Option 1.5"**: an independent Opus consultation recommended (and the user confirmed after a real back-and-forth about timing/risk) keeping the existing 5 alias strings (`brokerage`/`sep`/`roth`/`ira`/`soxl_ira`) as the DB primary key rather than a surrogate-ID migration — zero data migration on the 7+ tables that already store `account` as free text (`watch_list`/`open_positions`/`trade_log`/`paper_positions`/`paper_trade_log`/`addon_legs`/`paper_addon_legs`, later confirmed to actually be **11** tables via a live `PRAGMA table_info` sweep, adding `coverage_snoozes`/`skim_reserve_pool`/`skim_reserve_log`/`trading_incidents`), zero risk to the 5 currently-open real positions (`ira` x2, `soxl_ira` x3). New `accounts` table: `alias` (PK), `schwab_name` (informational only, e.g. `'ROTH-A-1'`, never read by logic), `enabled`, `notional_cap`, `daily_order_cap`, `trading_enabled`, `cash_settlement_type` (replaces the settlement half of the old `account_type`), `margin_capable` (new, replaces the borrowing-eligibility half), `margin_floor`, `is_tax_advantaged` (NOT NULL, no default), `retired_at` (an alias is retired, never renamed/reused). A new invariant (`signals_invariants.check_all_account_values_are_known_aliases`) replaces the FK enforcement the plain-TEXT `account` columns don't have — split into live-state tables (checked against non-retired aliases only) vs. historical/log tables (checked against every alias ever, retired included, so retiring an account doesn't make the check permanently red).

**Critical scope decision, explicit user sign-off required mid-design**: today's real add-on-margin-eligibility gate (`account_type != "margin"`) already passes for `ira`/`soxl_ira` (8 real live `soxl_ira` `addon_enabled` nodes exist right now) despite neither genuinely being able to borrow — user explicitly chose "preserve current behavior exactly" (`margin_capable=True` for brokerage/roth/ira/soxl_ira, `False` only for sep) over "match real-world capability" (brokerage-only, would've required pausing 8 real live nodes first) or "redesign the whole gate to be cash-aware" (explicitly rejected — reopens the already-known-hard skim-reserve-cash-ambiguity and concurrent-reservation problems, stays a separate deferred backlog item).

**`roth`'s real account_type was itself corrected `"cash"`→`"margin"` earlier the same session** (a small, standalone fix, done before any of the table work, reflecting the genuine real-world change to limited-margin) — this is NOT a side effect of the refactor, but its seed-data comments briefly implied "preserving" the old value, which two Opus reviews (both a pre-implementation plan review and a post-implementation paired cold+contextual review) caught as self-contradictory/misleading and had corrected to state plainly.

**Process**: two rounds of pre-implementation Opus plan review (caught the `margin_capable=False for roth` seed error before it shipped, the missing `.items()/.keys()/__contains__` dict-method overrides, the 7→11 table-count error, a `monkeypatch.setitem` test hazard) followed by implementation, then the required paired post-implementation review (independent-cold + contextual, per this project's standing convention) which found 1 HIGH (the roth-comment self-contradiction above, resolved) + 3 MEDIUM (a non-atomic `clear()`-then-repopulate race in the lazy `ACCOUNTS` cache across the daemon's two real threads — fixed via a lock around the whole check-and-reload decision, not just the reload body; the new invariant going permanently red once any alias is ever retired — fixed via the live-vs-historical table split above; a `RuntimeError` that could escape a `.get()`-shaped call site that assumes `.get()` never raises — checked and found already-safe at the one call site inside real order-placement flow, `record_node_streak`'s existing blanket `except Exception: pass`) + 2 LOW (leaked sqlite connections in the lazy-load path, a dead unused `id` column — both fixed).

**Real live DB migration**: the actual `cache/live/trading_live.db` was migrated for real this session (not just tested against a throwaway copy) after the full test suite surfaced that several tests read `schwab_safety.ACCOUNTS` directly against the real default `DB_PATH` with no test fixture at all — confirmed the daemon wasn't running, backed up first, applied `ensure_tables()`, verified purely additive (table count 26→27, zero row-count deltas on any pre-existing table, `PRAGMA integrity_check` clean). 26 of 764 test failures surfaced this way, every one traced to the single root cause of tests hardcoding `'roth'` as "the cash-typed/non-margin-capable example account" (true before this session, false after roth's real account-type change) — fixed by switching those specific tests to `'sep'` (the one account still genuinely cash-typed/non-margin-capable), confirmed by the contextual review as legitimate fixes to stale test assumptions, not tests weakened to paper over a regression.

**Verification**: 764/764 full suite, `scripts/live_sim_harness.py` 7/7, `signals_invariants.py` (including both new/modified checks) zero violations against the real live DB, both post-fix.

**Not done, deliberately out of scope**: renaming any existing alias, a surrogate-ID migration of the 7+ tables, the cash-aware add-on-margin redesign (stays a separate, already-tracked deferred item). See the still-open "GDXU/DFEN/KORU need to move to a new Roth account" entry below — this work unblocks that node migration (the account now exists correctly in the DB) but doesn't perform it.

## [backtest][live-trading] Research idea, raised 2026-08-11 (later still) — quarterly resweep cadence + dual-window (max-year/1yr) CAGR + candidate rotation, more fully specified than the older monthly-rescreen item in backlog_cache.md
User's framing: rerun the full sweep every quarter, report BOTH long-term (full cached history -- NOT a fixed "3yr", the real per-ticker span varies: ETHU ~2.0y, most others ~2.91y, newer ones like FNGU ~1.47y, whatever `calendar_days()` finds as that ticker's own min-to-max cached span) and near-term (1yr trailing) CAGR side by side per candidate (long/max window tests durable edge/consistency across regimes; short window tests current/near-term behavior, but is inherently noisier -- confirmed live this session: ETHU's "hot" 1.11yr window rode almost entirely on 5 concentrated trades), then consider rotating live watchlist tickers based on what the fresh sweep finds. Corrected same session: earlier framing said "1yr vs 3yr" -- should be "1yr vs max-available-year" throughout, since the long side isn't a fixed duration.

Design refined same session into a two-stage funnel, both stages real independent grid searches (not the cheap derived-CAGR shortcut originally considered): (1) run the full multi-phase sweep on just the 1yr trailing window first -- genuinely faster per-combo since fewer bars to simulate per backtest, not just a smaller param grid; (2) only run the full, expensive max-year sweep for candidates that clear a LOOSE 1yr bar (not "top N," just "not clearly broken") -- most of the universe gets eliminated cheaply before ever paying for the expensive pass. Real objection raised and resolved in conversation: a strategy that's genuinely strong long-term but temporarily cold in the last year would get filtered out before the max-year pass ever sees it (survivorship bias toward currently-hot strategies) -- resolved by the cadence itself: since this reruns every quarter, a missed cyclical-but-sound candidate just skips one cycle and re-qualifies once its trailing year shows strength again. Nothing is permanently lost, only delayed until it's actually showing recent life -- a real, load-bearing property of doing this on a recurring cadence rather than once.

Explicitly deferred, not built 2026-08-11 (later still, 2): user asked directly whether to codify this now. Real blocker before any build: unknown whether `run_optimization_sweep.py`/`backtester.py` already support restricting a backtest to a date window, or whether this needs new kernel-level plumbing -- not investigated yet. This also touches the backtest kernel/sweep engine, which per this project's own convention goes through the `backtest-change-rollout` skill's staged process (single-node verify -> biased single-ticker -> full campaign), not an ad hoc build. A concurrent session was also active on live-trading files at the time this was raised, adding coordination risk to starting a second significant change. Start fresh in a dedicated session: first confirm date-windowing capability, then scope the funnel mechanism, then run the staged rollout.

**Blocker resolved 2026-08-12/13**: confirmed by direct code check -- neither `backtester.py`'s `run_backtest*`/`run_backtest_dispatch` functions nor `run_optimization_sweep.py`'s `_load_node_inputs` take a start/end date parameter; `_load_node_inputs` reads each ticker's full CSV unconditionally (no slicing anywhere in the sweep engine today). So date-windowing genuinely doesn't exist yet -- not a false alarm. But the slicing technique needed is already built and live-verified, from an unrelated fix earlier the same session: `scripts/paper_vs_backtest_reconcile.py`'s `get_trades_and_bars_since(node, sim_start)` slices the per-bar OHLC/timestamp arrays to a start date while leaving `sma_arr`/`std_arr`/`trend_arr` unsliced (indexed per-calendar-day via `daily_idx`, not by array position -- slicing those too would misalign every lookup), confirmed correct against real KORU/YANG divergence. So the remaining work is threading that already-proven pattern into `_load_node_inputs`/`dispatch_parallel_grid`, not inventing new kernel logic from scratch. Still needs the staged `backtest-change-rollout` process once picked up (touches the sweep engine); not started.

**Short-window duration reconsidered and confirmed at 1yr, 2026-08-13**: user floated a shorter 2-quarter (~6mo) window instead of 1yr trailing, reasoning it reacts to regime change faster and aligns naturally with the quarterly cadence itself. Tested against real trade counts (real live-node configs, all 10 real tickers, current cached data): 2-quarter trade counts range 10-41 (AGQ 36, DFEN 17, DPST 10, ETHU 12, GDXU 41, JNUG 38, KORU 16, NUGT 24, SOXL 31, SOXS 32) vs 1yr's 18-54 (same order: 47/30/18/30/54/49/24/33/50/53). 4 of 10 tickers (DPST/ETHU/KORU/DFEN) are too thin at 2Q (10-17 trades) to trust a rotation decision off, roughly doubling to a trustworthy range at 1yr. **Decision: 1yr confirmed as the short window, uniform across all tickers** — consistency across the watchlist outweighs an optimized-per-ticker window, and 1yr is the one duration that doesn't leave any real ticker marginal.

Directly motivated by tonight's investigation, which is really several symptoms of the same underlying gap (nothing periodically re-touches a ticker once it's live): (1) ETHU/NUGT's `strategy_cagr_pct` going stale as their cached CSV window grew (same trades, growing `years` denominator, no automatic re-flag); (2) GDXU/DFEN/KORU's real `ira` live nodes (2026-08-11 promotion batch, $30k total) all running `z_score_threshold=2.0` when their linked candidates specify 1.0/1.5/1.5 -- invisible to BOTH existing safety nets (`staged_test_config`'s `FIELDS` list never tracked window/z at all, now fixed but not yet reseeded/scanned; `node_candidate_trace.py` only confirms a link exists, never diffs live params against the linked candidate -- also not yet fixed). Confirmed materially real for GDXU specifically via a fresh ad hoc island check (current full data, `+/-2` neighbor on arm_pct/stop_loss): the live z=2.0 config's exact params had ZERO rows in `backtest_cache` ever (never swept at all, at any window), and once actually backtested this session came back CLIFF and alpha-NEGATIVE vs SPY (center alpha -28.1%, worst neighbor -54.2%) -- while the correctly-linked candidate (z=1.0, same everything else) is robustly SAFE (worst neighbor alpha +129.2%, CAGR 47-106% across its whole neighborhood). A quarterly rotation review would need real params-diff tooling as a prerequisite, not just fresh CAGR numbers.

Not started -- explicitly "something to explore," not to build tonight (session has a concurrent editor active on live-trading files, per user's caution). Supersedes/subsumes the older 2026-07-25 monthly-rescreen idea in backlog_cache.md with a more concrete cadence and mechanism; that entry's "v6" strategy-variant half is unrelated and still separately open.

## [live-trading][coverage] Idea, raised 2026-08-11 — 4-tier test-confidence reframe (fake-venue/dry-run/paper/live), a nightly job to auto-manage staged-test node lifecycle against it, and a dry-run-only "can't-trade" ticker pool to cut live-test wash-sale exposure
Prompted directly by the LABD basis-lock finding above (a staged live-test node that had already proven its scenario 2026-08-07 kept running hot, hit a real sizing bug, and nobody noticed until a routine morning check). User's framing: each test tier answers a genuinely different question, not just "more or less real" — **fake-venue** (`fake_broker` pytest scenarios) proves the code mutation/branch is correct, zero timing/market risk; **dry-run** proves the decision logic fires against real signal timing without a real order reaching the broker; **paper trading** proves execution-timing/fill realism (bounce-fill, running_low, gaps) with no real money; **live** proves whatever the first three structurally can't (real broker rejection behavior, real fill mechanics, true settlement/margin behavior). A mechanism is "done" once whichever tier(s) it actually needs have fired — close to what `scripts/coverage_registry.py`'s `status`/`offline_proof_for()` already compute per-row, just not yet turned into an active lifecycle manager.

**Proposed staged build (not started)**:
- **Step 1 (read-only, safest to build first)**: nightly report cross-referencing `coverage_registry.py` against every `staged_test_config` row — flags (a) nodes whose target Grid row is already proven (safe to pause from active live duty, same judgment status_check.py's 🧹 STALE flag already makes ad hoc for ERY/RETL/SH) and (b) Grid rows still unproven with nothing staged for them. Would have caught LABD automatically instead of by accident. **A staged config is a reusable regression fixture, never revert/delete on "proven" — pause (state flip) while keeping the detune on file, per the live-test-node-setup skill's regression-pass mode** (corrected 2026-08-11 after the STALE banner's own wording said "revert/remove," which the user flagged as wrong: what if a full regression needs to re-run this exact staged config later?).
- **Step 2 (auto-retire, gated)**: once Step 1's judgment holds up over some nights, let it actually flip a proven node `live→paper` — but Slack-notify only above a real notional threshold (mirroring the existing `has_capital_at_stake` $10k convention); silent-log-only for small-notional staged/paper nodes, since routine intraday noise below that bar is already suppressed by the 2026-08-08 capital-at-stake redesign and shouldn't be reintroduced by this feature.
- **Step 3 (auto-restage)**: deferred — deciding what a freed-up node's next target should be needs a real priority model (which mechanisms are even compatible with which ticker/strategy). Not scoped yet.
- Nightly cadence first (per user's explicit call); move to weekly only once nightly is proven out.

**Wash-sale-reduction idea, corrected twice in discussion (final form)**: use the already-disqualified `underlier_count < 20` ticker pool (GLL/KOLD/UGL/UVXY/TBT/TMF/TMV/BULZ/FNGU/FNGD/SPCL/QPUX — 12 tickers, `tickers.k1_status`/`underlier_count`/`underlier_note`, built 2026-08-09) as **dry-run-only** test vehicles for future staged mechanism tests, instead of real candidate tickers (LABD/RETL/ERY/SH today). First proposed as a live-test pool (wrong — these are explicitly "we're not supposed to trade these," so a real staged order on them would just be trading a disqualified instrument), then paper (also corrected — user's actual ask was dry_run). dry_run never places a real broker order (no real shares, no real tax lot), so it's genuinely wash-sale-inert regardless of ticker — matches the tier framework's own definition of what dry_run is for ("forcible execution path" testing without real capital). Real candidate tickers (LABD-shape) would then be reserved for whatever specifically needs the live tier, shrinking the live-test surface that currently carries real wash-sale exposure. **Paper trading explicitly excluded from this substitution** — user's correction: paper trading's whole value is checking real execution divergence against the real backtest for tickers actually traded (the daily-track reconcile mechanism), so it must stay on real candidate tickers, not the disqualified pool. Only dry_run (decision-logic/forcible-execution-path proving, never a real fill either way) moves to the disqualified pool. Not started: confirming which of the 12 have workable liquidity/backtest history to actually serve as dry-run test vehicles, and how dry-run nodes on structurally-disqualified tickers should be flagged so they're never mistaken for real candidates.

## ✅ [live-trading][security] Resolved 2026-08-11 — LABD retired after a real `_last_sale_recovery` basis-lock; the "buried scenario prose in a baseline_config row" gap that let it hide fixed, swept for other instances (none found); STALE-banner wording corrected from "revert/remove" to "pause, keep as regression fixture"
Morning state check (`daily-routine-check`) found LABD (wl_id=152, `soxl_ira`) stuck: a pending buy from 2026-08-10 09:30 (`order_placed=False`) that would never resolve, because the automated buy path had declined at 0 shares (`coverage_events` `automated_buy_execution`/`shares_too_small`, 2026-08-10 13:30:23). Root cause: `signals_helpers._last_sale_recovery(node)` sizes the next buy off `exit_price * shares` from the node's last real closed trade and never falls back to `starting_notional` once any real trade has closed — LABD's last close was a 1-share test fill (~$7.66-7.69, `trade_log` id=69, 2026-08-07), so every subsequent signal sized `target_notional≈$7.66` against a ~$7.75 price, permanently flooring to 0 shares with no organic recovery path (a 0-share node can never close a bigger trade to grow the basis back up). LABD's staged-test purpose (Scenario 1 of the 4-scenario exit test matrix — SL-sell, not armed) had already gone verified-live 2026-08-07, so retiring was simpler than inventing a basis-reset mechanism: cleared the stuck `pending_buys` row (`signals_db.clear_pending_buy_by_wl_id`), flipped `state` `live→paper` (`signals_db.set_node_state`), documented the retirement + finding in `staged_test_config.notes`.

**Gap that let it hide, fixed**: LABD's real test purpose was recorded as free-text prose ("SCENARIO CONTEXT...") inside a `scenario_role='baseline_config'` row instead of getting its own mapped `scenario_role` — `scripts/audit_live_test_candidates.py`'s existing STALE-detection (`_scenario_relevance`/`SCENARIO_ROLE_TO_GRID_IDS`) deliberately excludes `baseline_config` (it's meant to be the generic per-node drift-check row, not a test scenario), so the check structurally couldn't see LABD was done. Fixed: `_print_staged_config` now flags any `baseline_config` row whose notes contain "SCENARIO CONTEXT" via a new `_looks_like_buried_scenario` heuristic, printing a distinct warning (can't compute a real STALE verdict without a mapped `scenario_role`, so it just surfaces the mismatch itself). Verified firing against LABD's row; 7/7 existing tests in `test_audit_live_test_candidates.py` still pass.

**Swept all 40 `staged_test_config` rows for the same pattern**: LABD was the only one. Everything else is either a properly-mapped `scenario_role` (`time_exit_via_trail`: SH, `time_exit_via_sl`: RETL, `gap_resize_and_topup`: ERY — all three now correctly get real STALE tracking) or the plain generic drift-check boilerplate with no embedded scenario prose (33 nodes). Real finding from the sweep: **SH and RETL both now correctly flag 🧹 STALE** — `time_exit_trigger` is verified-live 7x (last 2026-08-07), so both nodes' detuned configs have already delivered their proof. Left running as-is per user's explicit call (RETL has a real 80-share position open, TIME-exit expected to fire ~2026-08-11 midday; user wants to let it fire naturally before touching anything) — not paused this session.

**STALE-banner wording corrected**: the banner previously said "revert/remove this staged_test_config row" — user pushed back ("stop saying revert — what if we want to run a full regression?"). A staged detune is a reusable regression fixture (see the live-test-node-setup skill's regression-pass mode across staged nodes after a batch of trading-code changes), not disposable scaffolding — the right action once proven is pausing from active live duty (state flip, exactly what was done for LABD) while keeping the config values on file, never reverting/deleting them. Banner text updated to say this explicitly.

**Root cause**: no persisted FK between `watch_list` and `candidate_nodes` (a separate SQLite DB, `cache/research/trading_universe.db`) ever existed. `portfolio_account_status.py`'s `candidate_node_id` export is a live, best-effort recompute (exact param-tuple match) — silently breaks on any post-promotion tweak, and `candidate_nodes.pick`/`comment` (columns that exist specifically to record a decision) were NULL on every row, never used. Multiple real agent mistakes this session traced directly to trusting this fragile matching: a false "these are duplicate nodes" claim on SOXL/AGQ paper test nodes (missed the `skim_enabled` axis — turned out to be deliberate combinatorial drought×addon×skim test scaffolding, not a bug); comparing the wrong DB column (`arm_sell_pct` instead of `take_profit`) for `TrailingExitZScoreBreakout` tickers, producing false "NO MATCH" results for YANG/NUGT/UDOW that were actually clean; comparing HIBL against the highest-`robust_alpha` candidate row instead of the user's actual documented pick. Node 154 (`soxl_ira`) genuinely diverges from candidate 113 (fixed_sl 1.0 vs 3.0, arm 10.0 vs 13.0, trail_buy_pct 1.0 vs 2.0, max_hold 56 vs 77) — still needs the link recorded and/or a resync, user's call pending. Confirmed flat (no open position/pending buy) before the change; audit-logged via `watch_list_audit`.

**Real bug found and fixed, same follow-up session, unrelated to the above**: 2 tests flagged 2026-08-10 as "flaky from real `datetime.now()` dependencies" were actually failing from a real file race — `pytest.ini`'s `-n auto` had no `--dist` scope, so pytest-xdist's default `--dist=load` could schedule two tests from the *same file* (sharing a fixed ticker and the same physical `cache/research/{ticker}_1h.csv` path via `make_synthetic_csv`/`cleanup_csv`) onto different worker processes concurrently, racing on that file (`EmptyDataError`, wrong data). Reproduced reliably: 6-12 failures across 3/3 full-file runs under bare `-n auto`. Fixed via `--dist=loadscope` in `pytest.ini` (keeps all tests in one file on one worker) — verified 45/45 passing across 3 repeated runs, and 757/757 on the full suite with no meaningful timing regression (~4:26 vs. the prior ~5min baseline). The original datetime-based diagnosis was wrong; no clock-injection changes were made or needed.

Real `.env`/2 uncommitted pre-session files (`scripts/sim_wash_sale_impact.py`, `scripts/sim_real_portfolio_rebalance.py`) were left untouched — predate this session, never investigated. A new untracked `scripts/backfill_hourly_history.py` also appeared mid-session, not created by the agent — left untouched, unclear provenance.

**Scope note (user's explicit framing, several times this session)**: candidate SELECTION is the user's job, not the agent's — this tooling exists to record and verify the user's decision, never to pick or infer one. Also: "candidate selection" is distinct from "sweep campaign" — the user pushed back specifically when an earlier framing conflated per-list tracking with per-sweep provenance, landing on the sweep-campaign framing above as the more correct foundation ("because now there's no ambiguity").

**Session-wrap paired review (independent-cold + contextual, run in parallel) found real gaps in the fix as first shipped — 5 confirmed by BOTH reviews independently (strong signal), all fixed same session**:
- **[HIGH, both]** The cold-start bookmark floor (`paper_trading.py`'s `reconcile_daily_track_nodes`) compared `watch_list.added_at` (stored UTC — the column's own `datetime('now')` default) directly against ET-naive cached bar timestamps with zero conversion. Cold review verified this **empirically against real SOXL data**: for a node created 13:06 ET, the floor landed on `15:30` instead of the correct `12:30`, silently dropping the `14:30` bar — exactly the bar the 15:25-15:40 signal window evaluates. Compounded by a related off-by-one both reviews separately flagged: the floor used "last bar at-or-before creation" (bar START vs. `added_at`) instead of "last bar fully CLOSED before creation," which could exclude a bar that started before creation but closed after — a real, catchable signal. **Fixed**: new `paper_trading._added_at_floor_bar` converts `added_at` to `America/New_York` via `zoneinfo` before comparing, and floors on bar CLOSE (`bar_start + 1h`) not bar START. New regression test uses a real `add_node()`-generated `added_at` (not a hand-written string) specifically because the hand-written version in every existing test masked this exact bug — confirmed the 10 currently-live real `v5` daily-track nodes were unaffected by luck (`added_at` at 03:16 ET, both readings floor to the same prior-day bar) but any node created during market hours going forward would have hit it.
- **[MEDIUM-HIGH real-money, both]** `set_drought_config`'s `sl_override`/`arm_override`/`trail_override` params defaulted to `None` and were written unconditionally — a follow-up call to adjust just `confirm_days`/`vol_gate` would silently NULL any previously-set override back to "use the node's own core risk params" with zero record it happened. No harm tonight (all three were NULL on every node touched), but this helper is built to be reused. **Fixed**: sentinel default (module-level `_DROUGHT_OVERRIDE_UNSET`, deliberately NOT named `_UNSET` — that name was already taken by the existing `set_skim_state`'s own sentinel at a later line in the same file, and the first attempt at this fix silently rebound the shared name, breaking both functions' identity checks in a way that only surfaced as a cryptic `sqlite3.InterfaceError` — found immediately by the new tests, not shipped).
- **[MEDIUM, both]** Neither `set_drought_config` nor `set_candidate_link` logged to `watch_list_audit`, despite both being real config mutations on live nodes (contrast every other watch_list mutator, which does). Tonight's real drought-enable on wl_id 92/208/209 left no audit trace. **Fixed**: both now call `_log_audit`; the 3 already-applied pre-fix calls backfilled with an explicit "(backfilled...)" note so the historical record isn't silently missing.
- **[MEDIUM/HIGH, both]** `set_candidate_link` wrote an unvalidated `candidate_node_id` with no check it exists or actually matches the node's ticker/strategy — cold review noted `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` is never issued so even the declared `REFERENCES` clause is inert, and a typo'd id would produce a stored, confidently-wrong link that LOOKS more authoritative than the guess it replaced (the exact failure this table exists to eliminate). **Fixed**: now opens `signals_config.RESEARCH_DB_PATH` and validates both wl_id existence and ticker/strategy match before writing, raising `ValueError` otherwise — a deliberate, one-time exception to this module's usual no-live-cross-DB-join rule, justified since the function is called rarely (promotion time) and its whole point is trustworthiness. Tonight's 13 already-written links re-verified against this new check — all pass (they'd already been manually field-verified before writing).
- **[LOW, both]** `role` wasn't case/whitespace-normalized (`'Core'` vs `'core'` could create two rows under `UNIQUE(wl_id, role)`) — fixed via `.strip().lower()`. `note` was blanked on any re-link that didn't repeat it (`COALESCE(excluded.note, ...)` now preserves it).
- **[HIGH scope finding, contextual only, documentation fix]**: `candidate_nodes` has no drought/add-on/skim columns at all — a `role='drought'` link records "the candidate whose CORE params this node's drought config sits on top of," not a separately-validated drought-specific candidate. `confirm_days`/`vol_gate` have zero recorded provenance anywhere. The table's own comment overstated this ("core config vs. drought vs. add-on config" implying each role is independently sourced); corrected to state the real, current limitation explicitly rather than implying more precision than exists. Not a code fix — a real gap in what this table can currently express, left open (same category as the sweep-provenance gap above).
- **[LOW, cold only, not fixed — accepted]**: pre-fix false `entry_miss_unexplained` rows from the first (buggy) catch-up run remain in `daily_track_reconciliation_log` (4 per real node, 3 per overlay-test node) — the fix prevents new false rows, doesn't retroactively clean old ones. Left as historical record per the project's deviation-as-ticket convention, now self-explanatory given this entry.

Full suite after all fixes: `tests/test_candidate_link.py` (17 tests, all new/rewritten this session) + `tests/test_daily_track_paper.py` (37, incl. 2 new regression tests) all green; `test_overlay_paper_trading.py`/`test_paper_trading.py`'s 2 failures under combined parallel runs confirmed pre-existing (both pass serially, same real-`datetime.now()`-dependent class already tracked in `docs/backlog_cache.md`, unrelated to this diff). `signals_invariants.py` clean, `live_sim_harness.py` 7/7.

## ✅ [live-trading][security] Resolved 2026-08-10 — `node_id` threaded through schwab_client's order-placement chain, closing the ticker+account ambiguity bug shape (found live for AGQ/brokerage, same shape as the JNUG/ira collision fixed earlier the same day)
Found while investigating an unrelated question ("why so many tickers on brokerage") — `watch_list` has three nodes sharing `ticker='AGQ', account='brokerage'` (corrected 2026-08-10 by the contextual review below — originally reported as two): id=41 (`dry_run`, legacy v3.26), a `dry_run` rehearsal canary (id=193, `v5-canary-drought-marketbuy`, staged 2026-08-06 for the drought/add-on real-order-execution build), and the new `live` promotion node (id=203, $231, added 2026-08-10's ira-activation checklist pass). `schwab_safety.check_order`'s own code comment already flagged this as a KNOWN LIMITATION: `_node_id` was re-derived via `get_watch_list_node(ticker, account)`, which returns `None` on an ambiguous match — making `node_automation_enabled(None)` silently default to `True` for exactly this pairing, and `get_open_position_for_account(ticker, account)` (used by both the BUY existing-position guard and the SELL oversell guard) resolve to whichever node's position has the latest `entry_time`, regardless of which node actually placed the order. Harmless today only because `brokerage.trading_enabled=False`; would have become live-reachable the moment that account activates.

**Real fix, not a relocation** (unlike JNUG's fix earlier the same day, which moved the colliding canary to a different account) — the user explicitly asked for the wl_id-threading plumbing this project's own comments had flagged as "a separate follow-up, not done" since at least the 2026-07-25/26 wl_id refactor. Added `node_id: int | None = None` to all 8 of `schwab_client.py`'s order-placement/replace functions (`place_equity_buy/sell`, `place_trailing_buy/sell`, `place_stop_loss`, `replace_equity_order_with_market`, `replace_order_with_trailing_sell`, `replace_order_with_stop_loss`) and the 2 internal helpers they share (`_place_equity_order`, `_place_trailing_order`), threaded through `schwab_safety.approve_and_record` into `check_order`. When `node_id` is given, `check_order` uses it directly instead of the ambiguous ticker+account lookup, and `_local_pos`/`_presell_pos` resolve via the already-existing `get_open_position_by_wl_id(node_id)` instead of `get_open_position_for_account(ticker, account)`. Backward-compatible: `node_id` defaults to `None`, falling back to the old ambiguous-on-collision behavior for any caller that doesn't pass it (none remain in production code — all 16 real call sites across `signals_notify.py` already had the relevant node/position dict in scope, e.g. `node['id']`/`pos.get('wl_id')`/`leg.get('wl_id')`, just not threaded through).

**Proof, not just a green suite**: two clean full-suite runs (728/728) from a concurrent session confirmed nothing broke, but neither exercised the actual collision scenario (no existing test constructs two nodes sharing ticker+account and passes node_id through). Added two regression tests: `tests/test_schwab_safety.py::test_node_id_resolves_ambiguous_sibling_same_account` (in-process, mirrors the existing `test_node_level_automation_pause_no_op_for_ambiguous_sibling_same_account` test that documents the old known-limitation behavior) and `tests/test_fake_broker_check_order_guards_scenario.py::test_node_id_disambiguates_same_ticker_account_siblings` (fake-venue: two real siblings, pausing one's automation blocks only that node's real order at the fake broker, the other's real order still reaches the book).

Landed in the same commit as a concurrent session's unrelated `get_full_position_state`/coverage_check.py work (both sessions editing the same working tree with no branch/worktree isolation — coordinated via a direct message exchange between sessions before either committed, confirmed no file-level overlap and a clean combined diff). AGQ's three `brokerage` nodes were deliberately left in place, not relocated — the fix is now correct at the code level, so no operational workaround is needed.

**Session-wrap paired review (independent-cold + contextual, run in parallel per the standing convention) found real gaps in the fix as first shipped, all confirmed and fixed same session**:
- **[HIGH, independent-cold]** The BUY existing-position guard could fail OPEN: `get_open_position_by_wl_id(node_id)` alone misses a position whose `wl_id` doesn't match the ordering node's id — a legacy/unbackfilled `wl_id IS NULL` row (`signals_db.open_position()`'s own docstring documents these can exist) or a node recreated under a new id while its position stayed open under the old one. Either would have let a second real BUY through against real, untracked capital — the exact double-buy gap the 2026-08-02 existing-position guard exists to close. Verified live: zero such rows exist in `trading_live.db` today, so no current exposure, but the code path is real. **Fixed**: new `signals_db.get_orphaned_open_position_for_account(ticker, account)` (scoped strictly to `wl_id IS NULL` rows — never falls back to a sibling's real wl_id-tagged row, which would reintroduce the exact misattribution bug this fix exists to close) is now checked whenever the primary `get_open_position_by_wl_id` lookup comes up empty, on both the BUY (`_local_pos`) and SELL (`_presell_pos`) sides — the SELL mirror was failing CLOSED (blocking a genuine exit) rather than open, same root cause.
- **[MEDIUM, independent-cold]** `node_id` was trusted from the caller with no verification it actually belonged to the `(ticker, account)` being ordered — the old ticker+account derivation guaranteed this by construction; a bare `node_id` didn't. **Fixed**: `check_order` now verifies via `get_watch_list_node_by_id(node_id)` and falls back to the old ambiguous derivation (rather than raising) on a mismatch, logging `node_id_ticker_account_mismatch` so it's visible rather than silent — a real-money order-placement gate shouldn't gain a new way to unexpectedly block a legitimate order over a caller-side bug.
- **[MEDIUM, contextual]** `schwab_safety.record_node_streak` (the node-level circuit breaker) was still being called from all 24 of `schwab_client.py`'s call sites via the old ambiguous `(ticker, account)` derivation, even though `record_node_streak` already accepts `node_id` and every call site already has it in scope locally. For AGQ/`brokerage`, the derivation would return `None` and the function silently no-ops — meaning node 203's protective SL placement failing 3x consecutively would never trip the circuit breaker once that account goes live, defeating the exact case the breaker was widened to cover 2026-07-29. **Fixed**: all 24 call sites now pass `node_id=node_id`.
- **[MEDIUM, contextual, confirmed real but NOT fixed this session — documented, deliberately deferred]**: `check_order`'s duplicate-order guards (`_has_open_order`/`_has_open_buy_order_for_ticker`, the `(account, ticker, side, quantity)` duplicate-fingerprint window) and `signals_notify.check_live_state_reconciliation` (broker-level share-count reconciliation) both still assume `(ticker, account)` uniqueness — neither can be fixed by `node_id` threading alone, since Schwab's own order book and account-balance API have no concept of this project's per-node identity. Two genuinely `state='live'` siblings sharing one `(ticker, account)` would still block each other's real orders (duplicate-guard false-positive) and permanently trip the circuit breaker via reconciliation mismatches (broker total vs. one node's local belief). **Not reachable today** — AGQ's only `live` node is id=203; ids 41/193 are `dry_run`, which `_effectively_dry_run` keeps off the broker and whose synthesized positions are `is_dry_run_sim` (skipped by `check_live_state_reconciliation`). Real constraint going forward: **don't promote a second AGQ/`brokerage` sibling to `state='live'` without addressing this** — see `docs/backlog_cache.md`'s new open item.
- **[LOW, both]** Both original regression tests only exercised the node-automation-pause path, not the higher-consequence BUY existing-position guard or the new orphaned-position fallback. **Fixed**: added `tests/test_fake_broker_check_order_guards_scenario.py::test_existing_position_guard_scoped_to_node_not_ticker_account` (fake-venue: sibling A's real position doesn't block sibling B's genuine first entry, while A's own duplicate BUY is still correctly blocked) and `tests/test_schwab_safety.py::test_node_id_scoped_buy_guard_still_catches_orphaned_wl_id_null_position` (the orphaned-row fallback itself). Also tightened the original ambiguous-sibling test's precondition (assert the ambiguity actually exists on that DB state) per a LOW finding.
- **[LOW, independent-cold, not fixed — accepted]**: `replace_order_with_stop_loss` gained `node_id` but has no production caller (test-only) — harmless dead parameter, consistent with the rest of that function's pre-existing "reusable infra, not yet wired" status. `_log_pre_action_state_verification` could log a false `mismatch` in a genuine two-live-sibling state (detection-only, never blocks) — same underlying constraint as the deferred item above, not worth a separate fix.

Full suite green after all fixes (see session-wrap entry). `scripts/coverage_registry.py`'s `node_level_automation_pause` row notes updated to point at this fix instead of the stale known-limitation text.

## ✅ [live-trading][coverage] Resolved 2026-08-10 — `post_fill_topup`/`drought_entry_placement` got real live proof from today's soxl_ira executions; found+fixed a 3rd recurrence of the "missing a real state" coverage_check.py bug; built `signals_helpers.get_full_position_state` (local+broker ground-truth diff), paired review caught 3 real false-positive bugs before it shipped
Prompted by two real fills in `soxl_ira` today: **RETL** (wl_id=143, drought-overlay entry, 09:32 ET) and **ERY** (wl_id=153, the staged `post_fill_topup` test, 10:28 ET).

**Real coverage-grid wins, traced to exact `coverage_events` rows**: RETL's drought entry fired `drought_entry_placement` (2x live total, first `signalled` 2026-08-07, now confirmed to actual fill), then `_reconcile_fill` placed a genuine top-up (`top_up` `result='placed'`, 2 shares @ $9.9150, position topped up 78→80 shares) — the first-ever real `'placed'` top-up event in `coverage_events`, closing the real-money risk that's been open since the 2026-07-24 daily-order-cap incident. Both Grid rows flip to `verified-live`. Same day, ERY's staged test independently fired `top_up`'s *other* branch, `overspent_no_corrective_sell` (overspend=$11) — traced the math and confirmed this is correct, not a bug: ERY's `_last_sale_recovery` sizing basis came from a stale 1-share prior test trade (exit_price=$10.495) rather than the $500 staged target, so the 2-share fill ($21.04) exceeded that tiny basis. No real money was misallocated either way — ERY bought exactly the 2 shares staged, `overspent_no_corrective_sell` is a documented notify-only branch by design. `CLAUDE.md`'s `post_fill_topup` checklist bullet flipped ⏳→✅; `scripts/coverage_registry.py`'s notes for both rows updated to point at this real evidence instead of the stale "no live proof yet" text. **Follow-up left open**: SH's node (id 135, `soxl_ira`) still has `trail_buy_pct` widened 1%→5% from the now-resolved organic-wait — needs reverting to 1%, not done this session (a live-node config mutation, left for explicit confirmation).

**While checking the Grid, found a real false "unexplained deviation"**: SDOW (canary, `ira`, dry_run) — its `canary_overnight_carry` scenario reported `no pending_buys row and no closed trade found`, but SDOW's real trailing-buy had actually filled today (`open_positions` id=85, still open, not yet exited). `scripts/coverage_check.py::_check_trade_lifecycle`'s `expect_pending_carryover` branch only checked `pending_buys` (resting) and `trade_log` (closed) — never `open_positions` (filled, not yet exited), the third of three real states. **This is the 3rd independent recurrence of the identical bug shape on this exact scenario/ticker**: (1) 2026-08-04/05, `get_pending_buys_for_ticker_on_date`'s exact-date match instead of `<=`; (2) 2026-08-04/05, `audit_one`/`status_check.py` never checked `pending_buys` at all; (3) today. There's a long-standing open backlog item (`docs/backlog_cache.md`'s 2026-08-04 "broader diagnosis") proposing a shared canonical state function as the real fix instead of point-fixing each recurrence.

**Fixed the immediate gap**: new `signals_db.get_open_positions_for_ticker_on_date` (sibling of the existing `get_closed_trades_for_ticker_on_date`/`get_pending_buys_for_ticker_on_date`), wired into `coverage_check.py` as a new middle branch (pending → open → closed). Confirmed live: rerunning `coverage_check.py --date 2026-08-10` now reports SDOW's real activity instead of a false deviation.

**Built the broader ask**: the user then asked "we should also check both sides for open positions — Schwab and local — order state, cash, open positions?" Confirmed the existing local-only canonical function (`signals_db.get_real_position_state(wl_id)`, built 2026-08-05) never diffs against the broker — `audit_one` fetches broker facts separately and only prints them for a human to eyeball. Built `signals_helpers.get_full_position_state(wl_id)`: merges `get_real_position_state` with a fresh broker read (`schwab_client.get_real_position`/`get_real_orders`/`get_account_balance`, moving the latter two out of a private `scripts/audit_live_test_candidates.py` helper into public `schwab_client` functions so a core module can reuse them), best-effort on broker fetch failure, computing a `mismatches` list.

**Paired Opus review (independent-cold + contextual) of the full diff, run in parallel, converged strongly on the same 3 severe bugs** — all fixed before shipping:
- **HIGH**: gating mismatches on `node['state']=='live'` alone is wrong — `roth`/`brokerage` carry real `state='live'` nodes at `trading_enabled=False` (GDXU/KORU/DFEN, ETHU/AGQ), which fill via `signals_notify.update_dry_run_buys`' synthesis path and never touch the broker at all; the gate would have produced a permanent false "broker holds 0" mismatch for those. Fixed: gate on `effectively_dry_run(account, node)` (the module's own existing shared definition), not `state` alone.
- **HIGH**: add-on legs live in a separate table (`addon_legs`) from `open_positions` — 9 real `soxl_ira` nodes carry `addon_enabled=1` today, so a healthy core+leg position would have false-flagged as a share-count mismatch. Fixed: `holding` branch now adds any open add-on leg's shares before comparing against the broker total.
- **MEDIUM-HIGH**: `pending_buys.order_placed=0` is the normal window between a BUY signal firing and the order actually being placed (confirmed live on LABD id=152 at review time) — not evidence of anything wrong. Fixed: only asserts a mismatch when `order_placed` is true, and only against BUY-instruction resting orders (a leftover protective SELL no longer masks a genuinely missing entry order, nor falsely satisfies one).

Also fixed from the same two reviews: the docstring's claim that `add_node`'s UNIQUE constraint "already prevents two live nodes from sharing one (ticker, account)" was flatly false (both reviewers independently caught this) — replaced with the accurate `effectively_dry_run`-based justification; `get_open_positions_for_ticker_on_date`'s date filter was `=` not `<=`, which would recreate the SDOW false-deviation bug on day 2 of a multi-day-open position (fixed to `<=`, matching the pending sibling's own 2026-08-04 fix for the identical reasoning); mismatch branching moved off the merged `status` string onto the real local fields directly (`real_position`/`pending_buy`), since `status` collapses to `'holding_paper'`/paper-`'pending_entry'` when only paper state exists, which would have skipped real-orphan detection for a live node that also happens to carry a paper position; `filter_resting_orders`' hand-picked 5-status allowlist (inherited verbatim from the moved private helper) was replaced with `schwab_safety._OPEN_ORDER_STATUSES_EXCLUDED`, the same blocklist-of-terminal-statuses `schwab_safety`/`signals_notify` already use to define "still open at the broker" — one definition, not two that can drift apart.

**Deliberately NOT done**: `get_full_position_state`'s `holding` branch does not check for a missing protective order (resting SL/trailing-sell) — `signals_notify.check_live_state_reconciliation` already does that, with retry/outage handling and Slack alerting this function doesn't replicate; the contextual review's own scope note flagged reimplementing it here, more weakly, as the exact "two independently-drifting implementations" problem `get_real_position_state` was built to close in the first place. Not wired into any automated/nightly path — `coverage_check.py`'s fix is the only piece that runs unattended; `get_full_position_state` is new library code for `status_check.py`-style manual/on-demand tooling going forward, deliberately not swept across the whole watchlist yet (would be ~270+ broker API calls for ~90 mostly-paper nodes).

15 new/updated tests (`tests/test_get_full_position_state.py`, `tests/test_coverage_check.py`), each a direct regression for one of the review findings, not just the happy path. Full suite green throughout.

Pulled the real verdicts from the most recent full report (`output/candidate_full_review_20260809_192051.xlsx`, run 2026-08-09 19:20) for both tickers' every candidate-selection type:

| ticker | node_id | candidate_type | strategy_cagr_pct | worst_neighbor_pct | drought_ie_verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GDXU | 119 | best safe node (robust_alpha default) | 252.8 | +14.0 (SAFE) | NO_REAL_SELECTION |

## ✅ [live-trading] Resolved 2026-08-10 — all 5 follow-ups from the add-on buying-power reservation fix closed; item 1 resolved via a new monitoring job (user's call), not a math fix
Items 2-5 fixed directly (stale comments corrected, `coverage_registry.py` rows added/fixed for `addon_buying_power_check`/`addon_second_ticker_buy_allowed`, the failing test rewritten as 3 real cases: allowed-when-sufficient, blocked-when-insufficient, blocked-unpriced). Item 1 (reservation-headroom asymmetry) was deliberately NOT fixed as a math change — user's explicit direction: add a daily daemon job (`signals_notify.check_addon_buying_power_drift`) that monitors whether `buying_power == cash` still holds for every account hosting a live `addon_enabled` node, alerting unconditionally if it diverges, rather than scaling `_reserved_other`. `ADDON_BUYING_POWER_HEADROOM_MULT` still only applies to the add-on's own notional, confirmed unchanged by the contextual review.

Same session, two more asks against the pre-existing `check_live_state_reconciliation` (broker-state-vs-local-DB check, unrelated to the add-on fix but raised in the same conversation): (a) retry a broker-fetch failure up to 3 total attempts, 3s apart, before giving up — previously a single failure silently skipped that position for the cycle; alert once retries are exhausted instead. (b) moved this check earlier in `active_signals.py`'s poll loop, right after `check_sl_order_fills`'s `open_positions` refresh, so it runs before SELL/BUY actions are considered that cycle (previously ran after exit_check/paper/dry-run sells).

**3-way paired review (Opus independent-cold + Fable independent-cold + Opus contextual, all launched in parallel) converged strongly**, catching real bugs in the first pass at every one of the above:
- **[HIGH, all 3]** The new reconciliation fetch-failure alert had no cooldown, unlike every sibling alert in the same file — a sustained broker outage (expired token, network down) would flood Slack every ~5min per position indefinitely (up to 11 messages/cycle on `soxl_ira`). Fixed: new per-account `_RECONCILE_FETCH_FAIL_ALERTED` cooldown (reuses `_RECONCILE_COOLDOWN_SECS`), plus the post itself wrapped in try/except (Opus independent-cold's separate catch: an unguarded post failure would abort reconciliation for every remaining position that cycle).
- **[HIGH, all 3]** The retry sleeps (up to 6s/position) now sat ahead of the time-critical pinned entry/exit scans this project has specifically protected before (2026-07-31 ambient/pinned race fix). Fixed: once an account exhausts retries once in a given poll cycle, every later position on that SAME account skips straight to the failure path with no further retry/sleep — bounds the added latency to O(#distinct accounts down), not O(#positions).
- **[MED/HIGH, all 3]** `check_addon_buying_power_drift`'s original once-per-day GLOBAL watermark advanced even when every account's fetch failed (contextual review's sharper point: `get_account_buying_power`'s own docstring flags the `buyingPower` field as unverified against a real response, so a `KeyError` there would silently kill the monitor for the rest of the day, every day, with zero retry and zero alert — the exact failure this check exists to catch, happening to the check itself). Fixed: rebuilt around a PER-ACCOUNT `checked` map instead of one global date string — an account only gets marked done for today after a successful compare (diverged or no_drift), and a diverged account whose Slack post doesn't confirm stays unmarked too (mirrors `check_intraday_risk_review`'s existing confirmed-post-before-advancing-watermark pattern). No separate retry loop needed — the daemon's own ~5min poll cadence naturally retries within the same day.
- **[LOW, 2 of 3]** `result="failed_closed"` was a mislabel (nothing fails closed, the account is skipped and retried) — renamed to `fetch_failed`. Hardcoded `mode="live"` replaced with `_coverage_mode(account)` (latent bug: a `dry_run` account hosting a live addon node would have logged as live).
- **[LOW, 2 of 3]** A comment claiming "same workaround already used by check_intraday_risk_review's siblings" was false (grep found no other `ticker=<account>` call site anywhere) — corrected.
- **[MED, contextual only]** `coverage_registry.py`'s new `addon_buying_power_check` notes falsely claimed real live events existed ("see the pre-existing 'passed'/'failed_closed' events") — verified against the live DB: zero `addon_%` coverage_events exist at all. Corrected; `failed_closed` added to that row's `bad_results` (was missing).
- **[MED, contextual only]** The new `addon_second_ticker_buy_allowed` event (item 4's fix) had no registry row at all, unlike its non-addon sibling — added.
- **[LOW, contextual only]** Item 2 was only half-fixed: `schwab_safety.check_order`'s top docstring (~line 875-880) still said a blocked second-ticker BUY was "cash permitting," not accounting for the add-on path now being buying-power-based — corrected. Also a dead `blocked_addon_leg` result string still cited in a comment (`signals_notify.py`, the `_CONCERNING_RESULT_SUBSTRINGS` comment) — corrected to `blocked_insufficient`.

All 3 reviewers independently confirmed the retry-counting math, the drift comparison sign, the `ADDON_BUYING_POWER_HEADROOM_MULT`-not-touched claim, and the poll-loop move's lack of stale-data risk (the function re-fetches every position fresh via `db.get_position_by_id` regardless of where it sits in the cycle) were all correct as originally written — only the failure-path/alerting/bookkeeping issues above were real. Full test suite: 701 passed pre-fix, re-verified scoped (56 tests across the 4 directly-touched test files) post-fix, all green. New test files/additions: `tests/test_addon_buying_power_drift.py` (10 tests, new), `tests/test_live_state_reconciliation.py` (+2 tests for the cooldown/skip-retry behavior), `tests/test_fake_broker_check_order_guards_phase2_scenario.py` (item 5's 3 replacement tests, already counted in the original fix).

## [live-trading] Superseded 2026-08-10, see resolved entry above — add-on buying-power reservation fix shipped with 5 real paired-review findings, not yet resolved
Fixed the confirmed "1-ticker-per-account artifact" in `schwab_safety.check_order`'s add-on-leg guard (was unconditionally blocking ANY add-on the instant another ticker had a resting BUY in the same account, with zero real buying-power check behind it — same bug shape as the RETL/LABD incident this session started from, already fixed for the general/non-addon case in commit `038908d`). Folded a reservation for other tickers' resting-order notional into the existing `addon_buying_power_check`, mirroring the sibling non-addon reservation pattern exactly. **Correction to note for next session**: an earlier claim in this same investigation ("blast radius is near-zero, no live addon_enabled node exists") was checked directly against the DB and found FALSE — 11 real `soxl_ira` live nodes (GDXU/SPY/SH/DPST/RETL/LABD/ERY/HIBL/USD/YANG/SOXL) have `addon_enabled=1` right now. This is live-reachable with real capital today, not theoretical.

Paired Opus review (independent-cold + contextual, both launched in parallel against the real diff) converged independently on the same 5 findings, no rebuttal round needed given the strength of that convergence:

## ✅ [backtest] Investigated 2026-08-09 (later) — "certain" fill-resolution's credited entry price is unobtainable by any real execution mechanism; SOXL example node's alpha drops ~10x once corrected
Full detail: `docs/research_log.md`'s 2026-08-09 (later) entry. Started from the user flagging SOXL's `best certain` candidate row (+13,799.9% headline alpha) as "ridiculous, like the 27000% number [from] v4" and asking for it to go "under a microscope." Compounding arithmetic verified exact (not a bug) via a full manual re-derivation and bar-by-bar trace of real trades against the real kernel logic (`backtester.py:984-1003`). Real flaw found: the Close-confirmed fill case credits the entry at the theoretical trigger price, which has already passed by the time Close proves the fill — not obtainable by any real order. Corrected simulation (Close-confirmed case priced at the real Close instead): **alpha vs SPY +1,270.3%** (down from +13,030.7%, ~10x), still real (no single-trade sign flip) but far more concentrated in one historical window (first-half return collapsed from +548.4%→+30.4%) than the uncorrected number implied. A new live-executable mechanism idea ("CertainEntryTrailingSell" — confirmed entry via bar-close proof, unchanged trailing-sell exit) was scoped in conversation but explicitly NOT built — real open design gaps found (new hourly polling infrastructure needed, undefined overnight/EOD exposure policy) mean it needs `docs/new_mechanism_promotion_standard.md`'s process before any live code, and this session stayed in research/backtest-validation territory throughout (dedicated `[Research]` session, confirmed with the user). `robust_alpha`'s own `MIN(possible,pessimistic,certain)` selection convention is NOT directly corrupted by this bug (certain is the inflated outlier, not the minimum, for this specific row) — but `candidate_full_review.py`'s new "best certain" candidate-selection type (which ranks directly by `alpha_certain_pct`) is directly exposed and should be reconsidered.

**CertainEntryTrailingSell closed 2026-08-16 — negative result once priced correctly.** The "+1,270.3% alpha" figure above still used best-possible-in-bar pricing for the confirmed entry, not a true bar-close-only execution price. Once actually adjusted to price the entry off bar-close (matching what a real live mechanism could obtain), the result went **negative** — user's own framing: "certain entry trailing sell died because we found out the certain entry uses the best possible price for the bar but when we adjusted to bar close it actually went negative." Dead end, not a deferred idea — no further design work planned. See `docs/research_log.md`'s 2026-08-16 entry.


User's explicit ask, several rounds of iteration: "for every criteria we've ever contemplated, and overlays, I want to see it in one place - one sheet. I'll filter it out myself over time" — one row per (ticker, candidate-selection-type), no hard filters (only indicative `_tranche` columns, "these are just indicative though. Some are harder stops than others"), scoped to the full `docs/watchlist_candidate_checklist.md` 14-item list rather than just tranche-ifying what already existed.

**What it computes per row**: 4 candidate-selection types (was 3 — added `best certain`, ranking by the `alpha_vs_spy_certain` resolution alone, since `pessimistic`/`certain` previously only ever acted as a downside floor on `robust_alpha`, never their own ranking axis; this surfaced a genuinely different, much safer SOXL node worst_neighbor +197.6% vs the standard pick's +5.6%); raw strategy CAGR (not just SPY-relative AnnExcess%); the three raw fill-resolution alphas (possible/pessimistic/certain) as separate columns; sector + K-1/UBTI tax status (only for tickers actually confirmed via a real source check, everything else honestly "not checked"); overlay (drought/addon) robustness (chronological split + single-trade-removal, reusing `candidate_overlay_robustness_check.py`'s logic inline); a real 5-fold walk-forward out-of-sample check (checklist item 13, reusing `walk_forward_check.py`'s own functions against THIS row's exact node params, not just the old v4/TrailingBoth-only `best_v4_node()` path); max/current drawdown (items 11/12, free — reuses walk-forward's own trade list); same-day-block sensitivity/stability (items 9/10, TrailingBoth-only, a 2nd real kernel run per row); 30d/90d macro trend (item 1) and a real yfinance stock-split check (item 6); and (added after review) trailing-sell 5-min resolution accuracy (item 3, the exit-side mirror of the existing entry-side fillacc columns). Every continuous/free-text column gets an indicative `_tranche` companion (years/trades/liquidity/CAGR/cliff/walk-forward/overlay/K-1/resolution-spread/drawdown/trend/split/same-day-block) for pivot-table use — liquidity tranches at the user's requested $50k/$100k/$500k/$1M boundaries, nothing ever silently dropped by a tranche.

**Paired review (Fable independent-cold + Opus contextual, both converged independently) found real bugs, all fixed same session**:
- **HIGH (both reviewers, Opus with concrete repro)**: the walk-forward input cache (`_INPUTS_CACHE`) was keyed `(ticker, strategy)` without `window` — a ticker with 2+ candidate rows at different windows (15+ tickers affected, e.g. GDXD) silently ran walk-forward/drawdown/same-day-block for later rows against the FIRST row's SMA/Std indicators. Fixed by adding `window` to the cache key; verified against Opus's own before/after numbers (GDXD "best possible": max_dd −57.63%→−47.19%, exactly matching their independently-computed "fresh cache" figure).
- **HIGH (both reviewers)**: node-param lookup by `WHERE robust_alpha=?` float equality could silently return no match after any `backtest_cache` recompute (blanking 8+ columns with no marker), or match a *different* node on a robust_alpha tie between two grid plateaus. Fixed by threading the real node dict through directly from `candidate_type_membership()` (extended to also return `label_to_node`, the exact objects `find_candidates()` itself would produce) instead of round-tripping through the DB — also eliminated a second, now-redundant DB query for the three fill-resolution alphas, since the node dict already carries them.
- **MEDIUM (Opus)**: same-day-block sensitivity (item 9) compared `possible`-only alpha, not robust alpha (`MIN(possible,pessimistic,certain)`) — contrary to the checklist's own explicit instruction. Fixed: the blocked re-run now uses `return_bounds=True` and both sides compare robust alpha.
- **MEDIUM (both reviewers)**: the item-10 stability split cut each variant (blocked/unblocked) at its own 70%-of-trade-COUNT index, landing at two different calendar dates since same-day-block removes trades non-uniformly in time — defeating the check's stated purpose. Also used the full-window SPY benchmark for both half-comparisons instead of each half's own period. Fixed: one shared calendar cut-time (the unblocked run's own 70th-percentile trade's entry time) applied to both variants, with per-half `period_spy_bh`, matching `train_test_split_check.py`'s own established convention.
- **MEDIUM (Opus)**: `alpha_retention_pct`'s sign inverted when the unblocked baseline was negative (a blocked variant that's *less bad* read as "low retention," backwards) and `sdb_tranche` could mislabel this `HIGH_RETENTION`. Fixed: the ratio is now only computed when the unblocked baseline is a real positive edge; raw before/after alpha values are always exposed in the CSV regardless, so the sign is visible even when the ratio is withheld.
- **MEDIUM (Opus)**: checklist item 3 (trailing-sell 5-min resolution) was scoped but never actually implemented. Added, reusing `verify_trailing_sell_resolution.py`'s `find_hourly_trailing_exits`/`replay_five_min` directly, gated on the same `--skip-5min` flag as the existing entry-side check.
- **LOW (Opus)**: `x_addon_pct`/`x_drought_pct` (already computed by the reused `build_rows_for_ticker`) were dropped from the CSV fieldnames — added back.
- **LOW (Opus)**: `--skip-walkforward`'s help text only mentioned disabling item 13, when it silently also disables items 9-12 (all computed inside the same function) — help text corrected.

**Pre-existing bug found running the real 82-ticker batch (not from the paired review, from actually running it)**: `verify_fill_resolution_accuracy.py::fill_accuracy_for_node` used `None` (not `np.nan`) for a missing resolution key — a column missing for EVERY real signal (e.g. no ticker ever producing a `certain` resolution) infers as `object` dtype, and pandas' `.abs()` raises `TypeError` on an object column containing `None`. Never hit before because no prior caller ran this across enough tickers to produce an all-missing column. Fixed at the source (`np.nan` instead of `None`); `candidate_summary_report.py`'s `fill_accuracy_summary` (the actual crash site) needed no change once the root cause was fixed.

Full suite not run (this is a reporting-layer script, no test file yet — a real gap, `tests/test_candidate_full_review.py` doesn't exist; flagged, not fixed, this session). ## ✅ [live-trading][security] Parked 2026-08-09 — max cumulative BUY notional per ticker per day: the concrete live gap it was meant to close is already closed elsewhere; residual justification is generic defense-in-depth only
Raised 2026-07-22 as a backstop against a repeat-buy/runaway bug (a bug causing 2+ real BUY orders to stack up for one ticker in a day, beyond one intended entry) — not about sizing a single legitimate order. Design had already converged (1.1x `starting_notional` normal case, ~1.05x same-day-sell-notional dynamic case) but was never built; user wanted to think about the multiplier further.

**Traced through step by step, 2026-08-09, before picking a number:**
1. **The original motivating scenario is already closed.** The item's own reasoning was "a market order fills almost instantly, so by the time a second buy attempt fires, the first is already `FILLED` (terminal), nothing stays resting for the open-orders guard to catch." But the 2026-08-02 existing-position BUY guard (`check_order` blocks any BUY when `get_open_position_for_account` already shows a position, unless `is_protective`) closes exactly this — regardless of resting-order status, re-sizing, or timing gaps between attempts. A sequential in-process retry bug is fully caught by this guard today.
2. **Considered whether a cross-thread race could still slip past it** (two near-simultaneous BUY attempts for the same ticker both passing `check_order`'s "no position yet" check before either's fill is locally recorded — `_position_lock` guards a *later* step, DB writes in `open_position()`/`close_position()`, not `check_order`'s own check-then-approve sequence). Traced the daemon's actual concurrency model: `active_signals.py` runs the main poll loop plus two other threads (`SocketModeHandler` for Slack interactive buttons, `schwab_stream.run_stream_forever` for fill-detection). Checked `schwab_stream.py` directly: it never calls `place_order`/`check_order`/`approve_and_record` — pure fill-reconciliation, can't race on placement. The Slack-handler thread was initially flagged as a possible racer, but for `AUTOMATION_ENABLED_TICKERS` the initial BUY placement happens synchronously inside the poll loop itself (`_attempt_automated_buy`/`_attempt_automated_market_buy`), not gated behind a Slack button click at all — **and the user confirmed 2026-08-09 the system has moved completely away from manual button-click confirmation**, closing this path for good, not just for already-automated tickers.
3. **Considered `starting_notional`'s own reliability as the cap's anchor** (a real, separate finding along the way): `signals_db.set_starting_notional()` exists but has zero callers anywhere in the codebase — the field is set once at node creation and never updates as the account compounds. A cap pegged to it would drift stale (too tight) as real capital grows, unless someone manually kept it in sync, which nothing prompts.
4. **Considered add-on's interaction** (also never accounted for in the original 2026-07-22 design, since add-on's real order-placement code wasn't built until 2026-08-1x): add-on legs are deliberately sized at ~100% of the already-deployed core position's notional and already bypass the ordinary cash check via a dedicated `is_addon_leg` exemption (uses buying power, not `availableFunds`). A same-day core entry + add-on could legitimately reach ~2x `starting_notional`, which a naive 1.1x cap would wrongly block as if it were the runaway-bug scenario.

**Conclusion**: with the concrete live gap already closed by the existing-position guard, the only remaining justification for building this is generic defense-in-depth against an unidentified future bug class — not the specific reproducible scenario it was originally scoped for. Given that weaker justification against the real complexity still needed to ship it correctly (an add-on carve-out, a compounding-drift answer for `starting_notional`), parked rather than built. Revisit only if a new concrete gap is found that the existing-position guard doesn't cover.

## ✅ [backtest] Resolved 2026-08-08 (later still) — sl_sweep_summary worst_neighbor persistence re-enabled, closing the CRITICAL/HIGH gaps that had it disabled; a 2nd paired review caught the first re-enable attempt itself broken
The 2026-08-08 (earlier) item left `identify_full_mesh_candidates`'s i3 (radius-3) cliff-safety persistence disabled (`DISABLED_2026_08_08 = True`) after a paired Opus review found: (1) CRITICAL — persisted rows carried no `window`/`z_score_threshold`/`fixed_sl`, so a row couldn't be mapped back to which sweep campaign produced it (JNUG/TrailingExit/stop_loss=1 had produced 3 indistinguishable rows from 3 different `fixed_sl` campaigns); (2) HIGH — the i3 neighbor query varied `trail_buy_pct` (via `_sl_axis_real_column`) instead of holding it fixed like `scripts/top_safe_nodes.py`'s own `CLIFF_RADIUS=3` convention does, measuring something materially different (~18x apart on a real SOXL node).

**First re-enable pass**: added `window`/`z_score_threshold`/`fixed_sl` columns (`ALTER TABLE`) and rewrote the i3 query to hold `trail_buy_pct`/`trail_sell_pct` exactly fixed while varying the literal `stop_loss` column, per `top_safe_nodes.py`'s mask (`scripts/top_safe_nodes.py:35-55`). Verified with a manual scratch-DB smoke test (TrailingBoth case only) before requesting a 2nd paired review, since this touches `run_optimization_sweep.py` (a CLAUDE.md-listed kernel module).

**2nd paired review (independent-cold + contextual, both converged independently with matching real-DB measurements) found the first re-enable itself broken**, not safe to land:
1. **CRITICAL** — the `trail_sell_pct` pin used `tpct_c if fourth_axis_col == 'trail_pct' else 0.0`, which is wrong for `TrailingExitZScoreBreakout`: its `sl_axis` IS `'trail_pct'` (real column `trail_sell_pct`), not its `fourth_axis` (which is `None` for that strategy) — so the pin was always `0.0`, a value matching zero real rows (30 distinct real values in cache, none `0.0`). The neighbor search silently came back empty, and `float(worst_i3) if worst_i3 is not None else 0.0` then persisted a fabricated **"safe" `0.0`** for every TrailingExit row — the exact strategy the original disable comment cited. Measured on real SOXL data: the diff's query returned `None`→persisted `0.0`; the correct pin returned `+490.7%`.
2. **HIGH** — the inline comment's "harmless no-op" claim about `{scope_sql}` was factually correct (`_campaign_scope_sql` does pin `stop_loss=fixed_sl` exactly for `uses_fixed_sl` strategies) but wrong about the consequence: it meant the i3 radius never actually searched neighboring `fixed_sl` campaigns, while `top_safe_nodes.py`'s own `CLIFF_RADIUS=3` is NOT campaign-scoped — it pools the whole ticker/strategy/version's `backtest_cache`, and since only ~4 distinct `fixed_sl` values typically exist, its ±3 window genuinely spans nearly all of them. Measured on real SOXL/v5/TrailingBoth data across 3 `fixed_sl` values: the diff's campaign-scoped i3 read up to **119x more optimistic** than the true `top_safe_nodes.py`-equivalent number (666.3% vs 5.6% at `fixed_sl=2`; 359.7% vs 41.2% at `fixed_sl=1`; 640.0% vs 263.2% at `fixed_sl=3`) — a more dangerous failure direction (false-safe) than the original 18x-pessimistic bug being fixed.

**Both fixed**: `trail_sell_pct` is now pinned from a literal `trail_sell_pct AS literal_trail_sell_pct` column fetch (matching the existing `trail_buy_pct` pattern) instead of re-derived from `tpct_c`/`fourth_axis_col`. The i3 query now only holds `entry_timing` fixed (dropping the `stop_loss` half of `{scope_sql}`), so it genuinely searches neighboring `fixed_sl` campaigns for every strategy, matching `top_safe_nodes.py`'s real scoping. An empty neighbor set now persists `NULL` (`worst_neighbor_i3 = float(worst_i3) if worst_i3 is not None else None`), matching `top_safe_nodes.py`'s own fail-closed `pd.notna(worst)` guard, instead of a fabricated `0.0`.

**Verification**: manual scratch-DB smoke tests (not a committed pytest file — matches this module's established zero-test convention, [[feedback_manual_review_over_regression_test]]) covering: TrailingBoth cross-campaign neighbor inclusion (`fixed_sl=1` campaign correctly pulled into `fixed_sl=2`'s neighborhood) and exclusion (out-of-radius `fixed_sl=6`, wrong-`trail_buy_pct` row both correctly excluded); TrailingExit's previously-always-`0.0` case now correctly finds its real same-`trail_sell_pct` neighbor (`490.7%`); a lone-node case confirming the anchor row always satisfies its own filter (matching `top_safe_nodes.py`'s identical behavior, so a genuinely empty neighbor set essentially never fires in practice — the `None` fallback is still correct defensive code). `DISABLED_2026_08_08` flag fully removed; module imports and parses clean.

**Residual, accepted difference (LOW, both reviews flagged, not fixed)**: `top_safe_nodes.best_safe_node()` ranks unscoped across ALL campaigns with a `min_alpha=200` floor and walks down ranks until a safe one is found — it can pick a different anchor node than this function's single campaign-scoped top-1. The two numbers are now comparable in NEIGHBORHOOD convention (same radius, same held-fixed axes) but can still legitimately describe different winning nodes. Also noted, not fixed (pre-existing, out of scope): the new `fixed_sl` column duplicates what `stop_loss` already stored for `uses_fixed_sl` strategies; `sl_sweep_summary`'s `UNIQUE` constraint still doesn't include the new columns and `run_timestamp` being part of it means `INSERT OR REPLACE` never actually replaces (rows accumulate per run).
