## ✅ [live-trading][coverage] Resolved 2026-08-08 (weekend) — canary scenario_expectations unified onto the Trade-Flow Accountability Grid; price-action auto-explain for benign "no trade" deviations; nightly canary restage tool built
Answers the 2026-07-30 open question ("should canary scenario_expectations tests appear on the Grid?") — yes, unified. Three pieces, built after discovering (from the 2026-08-08 capital-at-stake Slack redesign) that canary nodes now get zero real-time Slack visibility at all (`state='dry_run'` fails `has_capital_at_stake` by construction), making the Grid/EOD report the only place canary activity is visible anymore.

**1. Grid rows for all 7 canary letters** (`scripts/coverage_registry.py`): only 2 of 7 (`canary_pinned_entry`/C, `canary_market_buy_exit`/E) had `REGISTRY` rows before — added the other 5 (`canary_full_lifecycle`/A, `canary_early_sl`/B, `canary_overnight_carry`/D, `canary_time_exit`/F, `canary_bull_bear_pair`/G) using the existing `scenario_expectations` check mechanism, no new plumbing needed. `pages/14_Coverage.py` needed no changes (iterates `REGISTRY` generically).

**2. Price-action auto-explain** (`scripts/coverage_check.py`, `signals_db.record_deviation`): a `trade_lifecycle` "no activity at all" miss (no pending_buys row, no closed trade — distinct from a trade closing with the WRONG outcome, which stays a real unexplained ticket) is checked against real cached price data via a new `_entry_threshold_crossed()` — instantiates the node's actual strategy class and calls its real `check_signal()` against cached hourly bars for the target trading hours, exactly mirroring what the live daemon would have seen. If the entry threshold provably never crossed, the deviation is recorded and immediately auto-explained (`reason_by='system'`) instead of sitting as a ticket demanding human `--explain`. Returns `None` (never auto-explains) on any data gap/uncertainty — fails toward leaving the ticket for a human, never toward false confidence. `record_deviation` was changed to return the row id so the auto-explain call can target the exact row just written. Backfilled against 2026-08-04 through 08-07: unexplained count dropped from 21 to 5. Verified against a real case (IVV): z-score stayed +0.8 to +2.8 across 4 straight days against a -0.1 entry threshold — genuinely never close to crossing.

**3. `scripts/restage_canary_nodes.py`, new** — nightly-only tool (never wired into the intraday daemon poll loop, user's explicit call) that closes every canary node's stale open position, letting it re-enter organically on the next real signal (canary entry z-thresholds are ~0.1%, hair-trigger, so a fresh cross happens almost daily once free to re-enter). Purpose is regression safety, not testing-frequency: after any execution-code change, an old canary position that opened days earlier under prior logic doesn't prove the new code works — restaging clean every night means the next day's canary activity always tests *current* code. Scope deliberately canary-only (`version='canary'`) — refuses to touch anything whose open position isn't `is_dry_run_sim`. First real run (2026-08-08) found and closed 2 genuinely stuck positions (SPXU open since 2026-08-03 at entry $36.065, never armed since price never moved favorably; TWM similarly) — confirmed via real price data (SPXU's Close never exceeded entry+0.1% in 5 days) this wasn't a bug, just an unlucky entry that would have sat for a long time otherwise (its `max_hold_hours=48` is trading-hour bars, not calendar hours, so TIME wouldn't have force-exited it for another ~2 trading weeks).

**Session-wrap paired Opus review (independent-cold + contextual + rebuttal exchange) of the `signals_db.py` diff found and fixed 2 real HIGH bugs, both independently converged on by both reviewers:**
- **HIGH — the price-action auto-explain could silently overwrite a human-authored deviation reason.** `explain_deviation` had no `reason IS NULL`-equivalent guard, so a later rerun of `coverage_check.py` for a past date (a supported, real use case) could replace real testimony ("confirmed real bug, SL branch never fired") with the generic auto-verified string. Fixed: the auto-explain call site now checks the row's current `reason_by` fresh and skips entirely if it's already `'user'`. Verified with a direct regression test (record a deviation, human-explain it, rerun `run_check` for the same date, assert the human reason survives).
- **HIGH — restaging (original design: close + synthetically reopen at current price) undermined the very canary lifecycles it was meant to test.** Two compounding effects, both found independently by each reviewer then confirmed in rebuttal: (a) a synthesized reopen never exercises the real entry/bounce-fill/pending_buys mechanism, so a "met" result overstated coverage; (b) setting `entry_time` to the evening restage moment meant a next-day exit's entry/exit dates never both matched `check_date` in `get_closed_trades_for_ticker_on_date`'s same-day requirement — making a restaged lifecycle's REAL outcome (including a genuinely wrong exit reason) invisible to `coverage_check.py`, and then auto-explained away as "no signal" by the price-action checker — actively burying a real bug rather than flagging one. This also permanently blocked `canary_overnight_carry` (D expects a resting `pending_buys` row, impossible once a position is force-reopened at the same wl_id every night) and made `canary_full_lifecycle` (A) nearly impossible to satisfy (needs same-day entry AND exit). **Fixed by redesigning the tool to close-only, no reopen** — resolves all of the above at once (real dated entries, real pending_buys rows, no invisible outcomes) and matches this session's separately-established "prefer organic coverage over forced/synthetic test state" preference.
- **2 MEDIUM/LOW findings also fixed**: `_entry_threshold_crossed` only checked bar Close, missing that `entry_timing='open_check'` nodes (canary C/E: IWM/TWM/VOO) also evaluate the bar's Open live — now checks both when the node uses `open_check`. Also switched to reusing `signals_compute._load_cache` instead of a hand-rolled CSV load (removes a tz/sort-order assumption gap).
- **2 LOW items reviewed and accepted as documented gaps, not fixed**: `pages/4_Portfolio.py`'s realized-P&L aggregate has no `is_dry_run_sim` filter, so canary trades (RESTAGED closes included) already polluted it before this session — pre-existing, not a regression, worth fixing next time that page is touched. A `close_position` race (something else closes the position between listing and restaging) now at least logs a `coverage_event` instead of failing silently, per review request.
- Full regression: `tests/test_coverage_check.py` (56/56), `tests/test_fake_broker_overlay_truth_table_scenario.py` (5/5), `scripts/live_sim_harness.py` (7/7). Grid confirmed to have 64 unique REGISTRY rows, no id collisions from the 5 new canary rows.

**Scope note, real and explicit**: restaging LIVE nodes was raised and deliberately narrowed out — only the V5 go-live checklist's small, hand-chosen staged-test set (SH/GDXU/DPST) exists to confirm live-only mechanisms, and even those stay manually staged, never broadly/automatically reset, since real capital is involved. `docs/backlog_cache.md`'s `post_fill_topup` entry now carries a note on why: an earlier attempt to design live-node restaging didn't land, and the low-capital-notional approach was the pragmatic fallback — not a dead end, worth another pass if a small-scope live-restage design is picked back up later.

Also resolved same session (real state verification, no code): GDXU's post-reconciliation TIME exit confirmed firing as predicted (2026-08-07); `stage_live_test_order.py` audited and confirmed already closed (widened to all BUY types in a prior review); user enabled Schwab's native `soxl_ira` trade alerts directly.

## ✅ [live-trading][coverage] Resolved 2026-08-08 — Slack alerting redesigned around a "capital at stake" threshold (not just live/dry_run); real gaps found by paired Opus review, all fixed
User's real-world complaint: with ~189 watchlist nodes (paper/dry_run/live) and zero nodes currently carrying genuinely meaningful capital (even the 11 real `soxl_ira` live nodes are deliberately kept small, $500-$2,500, as a proving-ground tier before `roth`/`brokerage` open with real capital), routine Slack volume had become noise the user explicitly said they wouldn't validate in real time ("i'm not going to be validating much myself", "it's just going to pollute"). Landed on a precise, mechanical definition through a long back-and-forth: `signals_helpers.has_capital_at_stake(node)` = `state=='live'` AND the account has `trading_enabled=True` AND `starting_notional >= cfg.CAPITAL_AT_STAKE_THRESHOLD` ($10k default, env-configurable) — deliberately dollar-based, not a manual per-node tag, so it grows automatically once real accounts fund up. User explicitly rejected two initial carve-outs the assistant proposed for safety (showing any real open position regardless of size in the Reference Report; leaving the manual "place a real trailing-stop order" / SELL-confirmation prompts unmuted for small positions) — final rule is uniform, no exceptions, but with an explicit requirement that muted-but-real anomalies must still be captured for later review, not silently dropped ("you capture risk at eod... i need you to wake up and assess the anomaly and judge it's risk").

**Built**: `should_alert_live`/`has_capital_at_stake` (`signals_helpers.py`); dry_run + sub-threshold live nodes muted across `notify_buy_signal`, `notify_sell_signal`, `notify_trailing_activated` (`signals_notify.py`); `send_reference_report` reworked to filter both Open Positions and Buy Candidates to capital-at-stake nodes only; new `check_intraday_risk_review()` wired into `active_signals.py`'s poll loop (runs every cycle, gated to trading days + 9:15am-4:00pm ET, reviews `trading_incidents` + a conservative `coverage_events` scan for anything new, alerts only if something's there); `scripts/live_sanity_check.py` gained a durable `trading_incidents` write on an unexpectedly-accepted test order (previously Slack-only, could be missed if unwatched). Also unrelated cleanup same session: deleted a superseded dead function (`_has_open_buy_order_in_account`) from `schwab_safety.py`; `scripts/check_untracked_positions.py` refactored to expose `run_full_sweep()`, wired into the 7am readiness check (detect-only, per the "self-heal" scoping decision — never auto-correct); added a `(revisit ~YYYY-MM-DD)` backlog deferral-tag convention.

**Paired Opus review (independent-cold + contextual) found 4 HIGH + 3 MEDIUM + 2 LOW real bugs, all fixed same session**, both reviewers independently converging on the most severe one: the three reminder/nag loops (`check_buy_reminders`, `check_trailing_reminders`, `check_exit_reminders`) were never gated on the same threshold as the initial alert, so a muted signal came back as an *unbounded* 15-minute nag stream — the opposite of the stated goal. Also found: `send_reference_report`'s new empty-state early-return removed the kill-switch status display and the ONLY Start/Stop Engine Slack buttons in the codebase, silently, every single day (since zero nodes currently cross $10k) — user's own reaction: "oh i probably need the kill switch lol." A missing/reconfigured `watch_list` node (the documented EDC/UDOW precedent pattern) was treated as "not capital at stake" by 4 gate sites, failing toward silence for a position that might still be real money — fixed to fail toward alerting instead. `check_intraday_risk_review` initially reviewed a table (`trading_incidents`) nothing in the daemon actually writes to (only manual scripts do) — extended to also scan `coverage_events`, deliberately narrow (fail/reject/mismatch/tripped/orphaned/overspent substrings, explicitly excluding `blocked_*` since many blocked results are a guard working correctly). Also fixed: a misleading "no open positions" claim when a real sub-threshold position was open; the incident/event watermark advancing even when the Slack post failed (now only advances on confirmed delivery); a missing-state-file bootstrap that would have dumped every historical (including resolved) incident as "new" (now seeds to current max instead); non-atomic state-file writes; two stale comments/docstrings referencing removed code.

**Deliberately deferred, not built**: a judgment-based review layer (an LLM call from `active_signals.py` itself, or a dedicated background session, actually reasoning about ambiguous events rather than a fixed rule) — discussed at length, explicitly tabled ("yeah not yet"). A cloud `RemoteTrigger` routine was evaluated and rejected as the mechanism (isolated sandbox, no access to the real local DB; 1-hour minimum interval, not 15). `/loop` (a local, judgment-capable background session) was evaluated as viable but deprioritized in favor of the cheap deterministic daemon-side version first.

9 new/updated tests (`tests/test_intraday_risk_review.py`, `tests/test_reference_report_coverage.py`), `scripts/live_sim_harness.py`'s `scenario_pinned_entry_trailing_buy` updated to assert the new mute (was asserting the now-intentionally-suppressed BUY SIGNAL post) — 7/7 scenarios pass. Full suite: 631 passed (was 622).

## ✅ [live-trading][security] Resolved 2026-08-07 (evening) — LABD's real stop-loss fill went undetected 8+ hours (no fill-detection path polled the resting entry SL independent of exit_pending); RETL's genuine signal blocked by an overly blunt one-resting-BUY-per-account guard; both fixed and paired-reviewed
**LABD (soxl_ira)**: a 1-share, hair-trigger (fixed_sl=0.3%) position's real stop filled ~7 minutes after entry, but `check_own_sell_fills`/`check_auto_fills` only ever polled `trail_state.exit_pending.order_id` (which only exists once the daemon's own bar-close signal check has already computed an exit) — nothing polled `open_positions.sl_order_id` directly. The position stayed stuck open locally for 8+ hours; every retry against the now-terminal order 400'd, posting a false "UNPROTECTED — place a stop-loss manually" alert on an already-safely-closed position. Fixed via new `signals_notify.check_sl_order_fills`, polled every cycle *before* the bar-close exit scan, closing the first-cycle false-alert window too. `exit_reason` is derived from order identity (`sl_order_id == trail_state.exit_order_id`), not the `trailing` flag — an earlier draft keyed off `trailing` alone and would mislabel a genuine SL fill as TRAIL whenever arming was persisted but the real trailing-sell placement had failed (caught by a paired independent-cold + contextual Opus review, converged in rebuttal). Applied to the real stuck LABD row: closed correctly (entry $7.685 → exit $7.66, SL, -0.33% pnl). Same review also caught and fixed two adjacent gaps: a fresh trailing-sell placement never repointed `open_positions.sl_order_id` at all (only a REPLACE did), and an add-on leg's own protective stop had the identical unpolled-fill gap one level down (`check_addon_leg_reconciliation`) — both fixed the same session. 5 new fake_broker tests (`test_fake_broker_sl_order_fills_scenario.py`), plus updated coverage for the arm-time repoint fix.

**RETL (soxl_ira)**: blocked from buying because LABD already had a resting BUY in the same account — real numbers checked: soxl_ira had ~$9,884 left after LABD's $208 reservation, comfortably affordable for RETL's $800 order. The account-wide guard (`schwab_safety._has_open_buy_order_in_account`, now removed/commented) blocked unconditionally regardless of real headroom — directly working against `soxl_ira`'s deliberate design (11 tickers sharing one account, to maximize organic exercise of real order-placement code paths in production, not one-account-per-ticker). Replaced with a cash-aware check deferred into the existing cash-availability block: reserves the resting order's REAL quantity × live price (not the node's `starting_notional` — a contextual review found `starting_notional` diverges sharply from real resting-order size, e.g. LABD's real order needed $208 against a $500 config value), summed across ALL other resting tickers, not just the first (a cold review caught that the singular-lookup version silently under-reserved once 2+ resting BUYs became possible — real risk given `soxl_ira`'s 11 tickers). `is_addon_leg` BUYs kept strictly blocked, unaffected — different risk category, explicit policy. New `AccountLimits.margin_floor` field (default $0.0, no live effect yet) added alongside, for a future genuine full-margin account's real borrowing capacity once portfolio construction gives a real number. 6 new/updated fake_broker + unit tests, including a 3-ticker case proving the multi-order reservation fix.

**Deferred, same session (discussed at length, not built)**: whether the add-on guard's `account_type != "margin"` check (a known overloaded-flag mislabel — `soxl_ira` reads as real-margin-capable when it structurally can't borrow) should become cash-aware too. Real complication found mid-design: add-on doesn't inherently need to borrow (a sufficiently-cash-flush account can fund the doubled notional outright, in any account type), but a cash-aware version would need to account for the skim-and-reserve overlay's earmarked-but-not-yet-redeployed cash and multiple tickers triggering add-on near-concurrently (9-10 `soxl_ira` nodes have `addon_enabled=1`) — same shape as the RETL fix, one level up. User's call: defer — moderate balances, no skim active yet, and Schwab's own broker-level rejection is a safe backstop (a limited-margin account genuinely cannot overdraft) in the meantime. See `docs/backlog_cache.md`'s "2027 problem" entry (companion note added).

**Accountability Grid** (`scripts/coverage_registry.py`): fixed a stale `second_ticker_one_account` row (claimed "not reachable today" — it fired for real the same day), added `second_ticker_buy_allowed_when_cash_sufficient`, `sl_order_fills_independent_detection`, and `addon_leg_independent_sl_fill_detection` rows, flagged a `scenario_key` collision (`addon_exit_fill` now logged by two unrelated code paths). `CLAUDE.md`'s `session wrap` gained a new mandatory step (3c) requiring this Grid/truth-table/canary check going forward, so it's not something the user has to explicitly ask for again. Separately, `scripts/audit_live_test_candidates.py` (feeds `status_check.py`) fixed a real reporting bug found live in this same conversation: a canary/dry_run node's local `pending_buys` row (no real broker order ever placed) printed identically to a real resting order ("pending buy resting"), causing genuine confusion when checking a canary ticker (SDOW) against the real broker and finding nothing — now explicitly renders LIVE / 🧪 CANARY / PAPER-DRY_RUN, checked in that priority order.

Full suite: 622 passed throughout. `live_sim_harness.py`: 7/7. `signals_invariants.py`: clean. `verify_trailing_buy_resolution.py`/`verify_trailing_sell_resolution.py` (AGQ, SOXL): clean, no mismatches.

## ✅ [live-trading][security] Resolved 2026-08-06/07 — `watch_list.mode`+account-level `dry_run` collapsed into a single `state` column (`paper`/`dry_run`/`live`); real-order gate now `state=='live' AND account.trading_enabled`
Started as a per-node `dry_run` override scoped narrowly (see the superseded 2026-07-26 entry below), then the user pushed for the full collapse mid-session: `mode` ('research'/'live') and account-level `dry_run` are now one literal `watch_list.state` column, mutually exclusive/exhaustive. `schwab_safety.AccountLimits.dry_run` renamed `trading_enabled` (semantics inverted). Real formula: `real_order_allowed = (node.state=='live') AND (account.trading_enabled==True)` — account ceiling stays independently checked, never absorbed into node.state. Migration (`signals_db.ensure_tables()`): `ADD COLUMN state`, backfill from old `mode`+`dry_run`+`account.trading_enabled`, `DROP COLUMN mode`/`dry_run`. Position-lifecycle state (trigger-buy/arming/trailing-sell as a shared enum) was raised and explicitly deferred — user's call: the next genuinely new strategy paradigm should own its own state tracking internally, not a shared generic layer (multi-security strategies, dynamic universes don't fit a single position-state enum cleanly).

**Two full paired Opus reviews (independent-cold + contextual, rebuttal exchange) + one exhaustive third-agent sweep**, ~50 production files + ~30 scripts touched. Combined ~30 real findings fixed, most serious:
- Slack button metadata whitelist (`signals_blocks.py`) omitted `state` — tapping "Filled" for a `dry_run` node computed `node_dry_run=False` (fail-open), could have placed a real order for a node meant to simulate.
- All ~13 `node_dry_run=(node.get('state')=='dry_run')` call sites in `signals_notify.py` failed OPEN on any unexpected/missing state value — changed to `!= 'live'` (fail closed) everywhere.
- **CRITICAL, found by the exhaustive third-agent sweep, reproduced against a real DB copy**: a legacy column-ladder line in `ensure_tables()` (`if 'mode' not in wl_cols: ADD COLUMN mode...`) unconditionally resurrected the dropped `mode` column (defaulted `'live'` on every row) on the *second* `ensure_tables()` call after migration — i.e. the very next daemon restart. Fixed by gating on `'state' not in wl_cols` too. Re-verified: 3x `ensure_tables()` calls against a real DB copy, `mode` stays gone, `state` distribution stable (82 paper/43 dry_run/9 live). On reflection with the user: downgraded from "CRITICAL — breaks live trading" to "MEDIUM — data hygiene," since nothing in the current codebase actually reads `watch_list.mode` anymore (confirmed) — the real risk was a human misreading raw SQL later, plus the (not-currently-reachable) `watch_list_new` rebuild-migration crash if a future schema change hits it while zombie `mode` is present.
- `add_node`'s default (`state='live'`, unvalidated) survived a full 46-call-site audit — every real production call site relying on the default (the interactive `cmd_add` CLI, both Streamlit "Watch"/"Add to watchlist" buttons, `scripts/live_test.py`) genuinely wanted `'paper'`; default flipped, `add_node` now validates `state` against the 3 legal values. One test (`test_scan_buy_signals_relocks_after_real_same_day_close`) needed an explicit `state='live'` after the flip. Also found via a broader AST-based audit (not caught by either Opus review, which only grepped literal `mode="live"` strings): `scripts/build_v5_watchlist.py` passed `mode=MODE` (a variable) — 8 more real crash sites across `scripts/add_labu_backup_node.py`, `scripts/setup_2026_07_24_soxl_ira_live_test.py` (6x), `scripts/add_daily_track_paper_nodes.py`.
Migration applied to the real `cache/live/trading_live.db` (backed up first: `cache/live/trading_live.db.bak_pre_state_migration_20260806_230040`) after killing the daemon; before/after diffs run on 21 read-only scripts against the real DB, all clean (only the intended relabeling, confirmed via structural diffing, not byte-exact since live prices moved between runs). Daemon restarted clean, Morning Report rendering the new tri-state labels correctly (`(paper/ira)`/`(live/soxl_ira)`/`(dry_run/brokerage)`) end to end. Full suite 611/611 throughout.

## ✅ [live-trading][security] Resolved 2026-08-07 — GDXU (`soxl_ira`) sat as a real, untracked, unprotected broker position for a week; root-caused to 2 distinct silent-failure bugs, both fixed, position reconciled for real, and a ground-truth sweep tool built
Found while spot-checking `soxl_ira` after the state-refactor migration (user: "check filled order in soxl_ira" → "wait no...."): the real broker held 2 shares of GDXU (avg $80.18, then +35% unrealized) with **zero** local record — no `open_positions` row, no `trade_log` entry, nothing. `watchlist_status.py`/`status_check.py`/every existing invariant check was blind to it because none of them ever ask the broker "what do you actually hold" — all are DB-driven, checking local records against themselves or a committed baseline.

**Root cause, traced exactly via `coverage_events` + a prior session's own transcript (not guessed)**: a Claude Sonnet 5 assistant in an earlier session (2026-07-30 01:28 UTC) ran `scripts/stage_live_test_order.py` — the deliberate direct-broker-bypass tool for staging a real order outside a signal window — to place a real undersized `TRAILING BUY` on GDXU (`staged test role: gap_resize_and_topup`; deliberately undersized, 2sh/~$155 vs the node's $500 target, specifically to organically trigger `post_fill_topup`, a mechanism never proven live, only via fake_broker). The script's own node-lookup (`get_watch_list_node`) returned `None` (ambiguous match at the time); old code printed a warning and placed the real order anyway, skipping `pending_buys` row creation. **Confirmed via call-chain tracing**: `_reconcile_fill`/`post_fill_topup` is only ever reached through the fill-reconciliation flow, which requires a `pending_buys` row to find the node — so the top-up proof this test existed to produce never happened either, not just the tracking.

Second, independent bug: `signals_notify._reconcile_buy_fill` (the single entry point for a detected real BUY fill, called from 4 real fill-detection paths) had `if not pendings: return` — completely silent, no alert — distinct from an adjacent, already-correct branch that DOES alert loudly on a `wl_id` mismatch (wrong candidate vs. zero candidates were conflated). This is why nothing ever surfaced the orphaned fill for a week.

**Fixes**: (1) `stage_live_test_order.py` now fails CLOSED for a TRAILING BUY specifically — refuses to place the real order at all unless the node resolves (new `--wl-id` override to disambiguate), instead of warn-and-place-anyway. (2) `_reconcile_buy_fill`'s silent branch now checks `db.get_open_position(ticker)` first — an already-reconciled fill (position exists) stays silent as before (regression-tested, `test_reconcile_buy_fill_logs_coverage_event`), a genuinely untracked fill (no position, no pending row) now alerts loudly with a new `buy_fill_reconciled`/`no_pending_buys_row` coverage event. (3) The position itself reconciled for real: node 108 flipped to `state='live'` (required — a `paper`-state node's protective order would have simulated, not hit the broker), `open_position()` called with the REAL backdated entry (2026-07-30 09:30:44 ET, matching the broker's actual fill `closeTime`), then the real production arm-detection path (`signals_compute.check_sell_condition` → `notify_trailing_activated`) run against the real current price — confirmed directly against Schwab's own order book afterward (`TRAILING_STOP SELL 2 GDXU`, order id 1007505678467, resting). Rehearsed via a new fake_broker test (`tests/test_fake_broker_gdxu_reconciliation_scenario.py`, mirrors GDXU's exact config/situation) *before* touching the real broker, not after.
(4) New on-demand (explicitly NOT periodic — user's correction: "when I ask you for state, I expect state") ground-truth tool, `scripts/check_untracked_positions.py` + `schwab_client.get_all_real_positions(account)`: sweeps every real account's actual broker position list against local `open_positions`, flagging untracked positions, share-count mismatches, and stale local rows — the check that would have caught this the day it happened. Directly instantiates `docs/automation_principles.md` #1 ("Reconfirm real state before acting — never trust a local/cached record as ground truth"). Run clean against both linked accounts after the fix.
(5) Separately found in the same investigation: `scripts/seed_baseline_config.py`'s config-drift `FIELDS` tuple never tracked the 10 drought/addon/skim overlay columns — a silent overlay-config drift would render as a false "✓ matches committed baseline." Fixed (FIELDS expanded) + one-time backfill merged the new fields into all 24 existing `baseline_config` rows from each node's real current value; re-verified zero drift violations afterward.
**Paired Opus review (independent-cold + contextual, with rebuttal exchange) of this incremental fix set found the first pass's own fixes had real gaps — most seriously, the new orphan-fill alert was itself unreachable for the exact scenario it was built for** (every caller of `_reconcile_buy_fill` except `drain_fill_queue` iterates `pending_buys` and so can never observe a fully orphaned fill; `drain_fill_queue` itself short-circuited at `node_auto_fill_detection_enabled(None)==False` before ever calling it). 18 findings total, all CONFIRMED and fixed:
- `drain_fill_queue` gained a dedicated orphan-fill branch (confirms the fill via a real broker poll, alerts loudly, does NOT attempt to reconcile since there's no node to attribute it to) — the one path that sees a broker fill event independent of any local row.
- `_reconcile_buy_fill`'s "already reconciled" check (`db.get_open_position(ticker)`, ticker-only/all-accounts/dry-run-sim-inclusive) replaced with a new `db.get_real_open_position(ticker, account)` — a same-ticker synthetic canary position in a different account was silently suppressing the real alert.
- `stage_live_test_order.py`: `--wl-id` is now validated against `--ticker`/`--account` (an unvalidated override could misdirect a real order's tracking to a completely different ticker, and `check_gap_resize` would later place a real MARKET BUY against the wrong one); the fail-closed check now requires `node['state']=='live'` (a resolved `dry_run` node would place a real order that the daemon's own dry-run fill synthesis then re-orphans a second way); the check now covers any real BUY (`MARKET` included, not just `TRAILING` — the still-open `market_buy_placement` go-live item had zero coverage, same exposure, faster fill).
- The new failure event moved off the `buy_fill_reconciled` scenario_key (whose registry row has no `bad_results`) to a distinct `orphaned_fill_detected` key — the failure event was otherwise rendering as verified-live proof of the exact mechanism it proves failed, in the Accountability Grid/EOD readiness headline.
- `scripts/check_untracked_positions.py`: rewritten to distinguish algo-relevant tickers (ever on that account's `watch_list`) from hand-held non-algo holdings (informational only, not flagged — the original version rendered every real account permanently red); widened account scope to the union of `schwab_safety.ACCOUNTS` and any other linked account; fetch errors now count as findings, not silent "clean"; accounts for open real `addon_legs` before flagging a share-count MISMATCH; catches NULL-account local rows separately; sums rather than collapses duplicate ticker rows.
- `schwab_client.get_all_real_positions` now sums rather than overwrites duplicate symbol rows (defensive); new `get_all_real_short_positions` — a naked/accidental short was previously invisible to the sweep entirely (the most dangerous state a ground-truth check could miss).
- `scripts/seed_baseline_config.py` gained `--merge-new-fields` (adds any newly-tracked FIELDS key to an already-staged row from the node's current value, never overwriting an existing tracked value) — the committed script itself had no update path for the 24 rows this session's manual backfill already covered; also widened its default seeding scope from `state=='live'` to `state != 'paper'` so a future `dry_run` overlay node isn't silently skipped.
- 2 new fake_broker regression tests (`test_fake_broker_orphaned_fill_alert_scenario.py`) proving the orphan-fill alert fires for a genuinely untracked fill and stays silent for a normally-reconciled one.
Full suite 614/614 (611 + 3 new tests this round), `live_sim_harness.py` 7/7, `signals_invariants.py` clean throughout.

## [live-trading][coverage] Resolved 2026-08-1x — staged 17 isolated paper nodes covering the full drought/addon/skim regression matrix on SOXL plus 2 realistic AGQ candidate configs, after finding and closing a real truth-table gap (skim's equity math was silently core-only, never decided)
Extended the initial 4-node stage (below) after further discussion: SOXL now carries all 7 non-trivial combinations of `drought_overlay_enabled`/`addon_enabled`/`skim_enabled` (2^3 - 1; "all off" is just the real, already-running v5 node) as `version` tags `v5-overlay-test`/`-a`/`-da`/`-skim`/`-skim-d`/`-skim-a`/`-skim-da` (13 nodes total, live+daily-track pairs for every combo except skim-alone). AGQ carries only its 2 realistic candidate configs (addon alone; addon+skim) rather than the full matrix, since AGQ was rejected as a drought candidate (see `docs/research_log.md`'s 2026-08-07 entry) — 4 nodes total.

**Design decisions made explicit during the build-out, not assumed**:
- **One ticker (SOXL) for the exhaustive regression board, deliberately**: real per-mechanism ticker validation (drought only proven for SOXL; addon only real-executable in a margin account, and AGQ — the only margin node — was rejected for drought) doesn't block combined-config PAPER testing at all, since no real order code exists yet for any of these mechanisms (see entry below). Consolidating on one ticker was also judged to have a real diagnostic benefit over spreading across tickers: sibling nodes reacting to the identical price history give direct apples-to-apples comparisons when a shared event fires, the same value the live-track/daily-track pairing already provides, rather than incomparable independent draws.
- **Live-track/daily-track pairing skipped for the skim-alone combo only**: skim's own logic never makes a price-timing-sensitive decision (reacts to an already-closed trade's recorded P&L; its only live-price read, `_spy_price_at`, is a pure mark-to-market lookup, not a signal check) — so daily-track's Close-vs-tick comparison adds no diagnostic value there specifically. Every combo that ALSO includes drought or addon keeps the pairing, since those mechanisms have their own price-timing sensitivity independent of whether skim is also present — the pairing is inherited from drought/addon's own need, not removed by skim's absence of one.

`scripts/stage_overlay_test_nodes.py` rewritten to a data-driven `COMBOS` list (ticker, live-track source id, daily-track source id or `None` for live-only, version tag, overlay config dict) — idempotent (existing 4 nodes correctly no-op'd on rerun via `add_node`'s dedup check). `signals_invariants.py` clean after all 17 nodes existed.

## [live-trading][coverage] Resolved 2026-08-1x — staged 4 isolated paper nodes for drought(SOXL)/addon(AGQ) testing; found and closed a real truth-table gap: skim's equity math was silently core-only, never decided
Picked up the open "staged real-order testing" item from the 2026-08-09 overlay build (see entry below). Found on inspection: `paper_trading.py` never calls `schwab_client`/`schwab_safety` at all for any of the three mechanisms — there is currently no real-order code path for drought-entry or add-on-entry anywhere in the codebase, so "staged real-order testing" as worded in the backlog was premature; the actual next step is paper-testing the overlay logic against real live-cadence data first (see the new backlog_cache item for what real-order staging actually requires).

**Isolation decision**: rather than flipping `drought_overlay_enabled`/`addon_enabled` directly on SOXL's/AGQ's real v5 research nodes (id=92/163 live-track+daily-track, id=86/157 live-track+daily-track) — the only source of real v5 paper-trading track record for those tickers — created 4 new cloned nodes instead (`scripts/stage_overlay_test_nodes.py`, `version='v5-overlay-test'`, `mode='research'`): SOXL drought pair (id=167 live-track, id=168 daily-track, `drought_confirm_days=3, drought_vol_gate=0.4` — the corrected/validated config) and AGQ addon pair (id=169 live-track, id=170 daily-track, `addon_enabled=1`). Rationale: the 2026-08-09 HANDOFF-before-core-scan fix touches `_scan_pinned_entry`, the real core entry-scan path every live node flows through (gated per-node by `drought_overlay_enabled` before any action, confirmed by direct code read — `active_signals.py:974,1209,1245` — so an unrelated node like KORU takes zero drought-specific action), but the surrounding loop/state-refresh restructuring is still new, first-real-activation code shared by every node in the scan. Cloning is free in paper mode; isolating the blast radius from already-trusted data was judged worth it. `signals_invariants.py` clean after creation; schema itself confirmed freshly migrated onto the real `trading_live.db` this session (`ensure_tables()` had not run against the real live DB before — daemon restarted by the user specifically to pick it up).

**Real gap found and closed, not caught by any of the three 2026-08-09 paired Opus review rounds**: the existing "5 reachable states" truth table (`tests/test_overlay_paper_trading.py`) only enumerates `(core, drought, addon)` — skim is a 4th, independent node-level flag never included in that enumeration, and nothing stops a node from having `skim_enabled=1` alongside `drought_overlay_enabled=1`/`addon_enabled=1`. Direct code read confirmed `_paper_core_equity`/`_latest_core_trade_pnl_pct` (`paper_trading.py:1169-1202`) filter to `position_source='core'` in `paper_trade_log` only — drought trades (`position_source='drought_overlay'`) and addon legs (a wholly separate `paper_addon_legs` table) are invisible to skim's equity/`strategy_value` math. This was an accident of the query filter, not a decision, until this session made it explicit.

**User's decision**: core-only stays the design for now (skim isn't planned for near-term real use given small notional/trade volume). **Real, correctly-characterized worst case, walked through live in conversation**: asymmetric, not just "occasional bloat" — if drought/addon are profitable, core-only skim harmlessly under-captures (leaves some upside undeployed in the reserve). If drought/addon are *losing* money on a node, skim's equity reading has zero visibility into that drag — it could still fire and move money to reserve based on core's isolated gain while the node's true blended equity is flat or worse, and any human reading a skim alert/dashboard would see a rosier picture than reality. Accepted as low-severity (no correctness/double-count/safety exposure, a signal-accuracy question only, and not reachable today since no real node has more than one of these flags on).

Locked the current behavior in with 2 new tests (`test_skim_ignores_drought_overlay_pnl_by_design`, `test_skim_ignores_addon_leg_pnl_by_design`) rather than leaving it an unverified side effect of the filter — a future change to either query is now a deliberate, reviewed decision, not a silent behavior change. Also confirmed directly (not assumed): `check_paper_skim` has exactly one call site (`paper_trading.py:1463`), gated `if pos.get('position_source')=='core'` — drought/addon closes structurally cannot reach it at all today, so `skim_reserve_log`'s lack of a trigger-source column is a non-issue now but would need adding if this scope ever changes (see backlog_cache).

Full suite: 568 passed (was 565 at the 2026-08-09 build's close; `test_overlay_paper_trading.py` alone: 29 passed, was 27, +2 from today). `signals_invariants.py` clean.

## [live-trading][security] Built 2026-08-09 — drought overlay/margin add-on-at-arm/skim-and-reserve as generic `watch_list` features, paper-trading through live daemon wiring, put-hedge and staged real-order testing still open
Full design: `docs/design.md`'s 2026-08-07 "Live automation design" entry. This session executed the staged checklist end to end for two of the three mechanisms plus drought overlay (put-hedge explicitly excluded per user's call at session start): DB schema → DB functions → paper-trading logic → daily-track sync → nightly reconcile → Accountability Grid rows → truth-table tests → live daemon wiring. Three paired Opus reviews (independent-cold + contextual each) ran during the build — schema+DB+paper-trading-logic diff, the daemon-wiring diff, and a final session-wrap review of the complete cumulative diff — and found/fixed a combined 1 CRITICAL + 4 HIGH + many MEDIUM/LOW real bugs, all individually re-verified with new tests before moving on. 30 new tests added (`tests/test_overlay_paper_trading.py`), full suite 565 passed, `live_sim_harness.py` 7/7 both before and after the daemon wiring.

**Schema/DB (`signals_db.py`)**: new `watch_list` columns for all three mechanisms' config, including nullable per-node override columns for drought's SL/arm/trail (validated default: reuse the node's own core risk params — every independently-tuned variant tested in real research failed cliff-safety or out-of-sample, see `docs/research_log.md`'s 2026-08-05 entries — overrides added anyway for a possible future re-validated config, routed to the correct column per strategy: `TrailingBothZScoreBreakout` stores arm in `arm_sell_pct`, everything else in `take_profit`, mirroring `signals_db._tp_or_arm_pct`). `position_source` discriminator (`'core'`/`'drought_overlay'` only, CHECK-constrained) on `open_positions`/`trade_log`/`paper_positions`/`paper_trade_log` — margin add-on legs deliberately do NOT share these tables (a cold Opus review found that would break `get_open_position`/`top_up_position`/`set_broker_stop_price`/`get_held_tickers`/`schwab_safety.check_order`'s double-buy guard, all of which assume at most one row per ticker/wl_id); add-on legs live in new dedicated `addon_legs`/`paper_addon_legs` tables instead, linked via `parent_trade_log_id` (permanent) rather than only `parent_position_id` (deleted on close). New `skim_reserve_pool` (real pooled reserve position per account, composite `(account, reserve_ticker)` key with explicit `NOT NULL` — a plain `TEXT PRIMARY KEY` permits multiple NULL rows in SQLite), `skim_reserve_log` (append-only ledger history), `overlay_reconciliation_log` (mirrors `daily_track_reconciliation_log`'s shape, with a `UNIQUE(wl_id, mechanism, mode, check_date)` constraint that table is missing). Migration verified idempotent against both a fresh DB and a real copy of `trading_live.db` — **the real live DB itself was never migrated this session**, only copies; the schema lands automatically the next time anything calls `ensure_tables()` against it (next daemon restart).

**Paper-trading logic (`paper_trading.py`)**: `check_paper_drought_entry`/`check_paper_drought_handoff` (once-per-gap fire, vol-gated, daily-track-aware), `check_paper_addon_trigger`/`close_paper_addon_leg_if_open` (hooks the same `just_activated_trailing` event core already detects; lockstep close with the validated margin-cost haircut applied), `check_paper_skim` (real dollar-denominated strategy/reserve values marked to a real cached SPY price, not the reference's normalized equity-unit weights — economically equivalent, more directly useful downstream). `reconcile_overlay_nodes` replays each mechanism's own validated backtest function (`scripts/stacked_model/drought.py`/`add_on.py`/`skim_reserve.py`'s `skim_only`, deliberately not `manual_redeploy_overlay` — the reference executes real automated redeploys paper never does) against real cached data through today, pure observation, one row per node/mechanism/mode/night.

**Real bugs found and fixed across the three review rounds, most severe first**:
1. **[CRITICAL]** `check_paper_drought_handoff` checked `sig is None` instead of `sig['signal'] == 'BUY'` — `compute_buy_signal` returns a real dict (`signal='HOLD'`) on almost every poll, never `None` just because there's no signal; the bug would have closed every drought position on virtually every poll inside a signal window, permanently starving every gap of a second attempt (once-per-gap guard compounds it). Found the moment the function was actually wired into the daemon.
2. **[HIGH]** Drought entry re-entered unboundedly within one gap (the backtest makes exactly one trade per gap; the live version's confirmation check stayed true for the rest of the gap once crossed) — fixed via a `drought_gap_start`-keyed dedup against both open and closed paper trades.
3. **[HIGH]** The HANDOFF-before-core-scan ordering contract was violated by a third real core-entry path, `_scan_pinned_entry` — the actual primary entry mechanism for every real drought candidate (all `entry_timing='open_check'` + automation-enabled). Fixed by adding a HANDOFF call inside the pinned-bar loop too, plus refreshing the stale `open_position_keys` snapshot afterward (the later scans would otherwise still see a just-closed drought row as "already held").
4. **[HIGH]** Redeploy alert fired against a genuinely empty reserve — the reference's `w_spy > 0` guard was dropped entirely; an independent review's differential simulation against the reference over 500 random equity paths proved this ONE missing guard explained 100% of the divergence.
5. **[HIGH]** Skim amount formula diverged from the validated model in the wrong direction — recomputed off the full undiluted notional every time instead of a shrinking fraction of the already-reduced deployed sleeve, so later skims grew instead of shrinking (a 6th skim was 3x too large in one differential test). Fixed via a real `skim_strategy_value`/`skim_reserve_balance` dollar ledger.
6. **[MEDIUM]** The reserve was never actually modeled (no real shares against a real SPY price) — fixed via mark-to-market against real cached SPY data at every call.
7. **[MEDIUM]** Window gate for drought entry/handoff wasn't node-aware — ran for a `close`-timing node during the `open_check` window even though no core scan runs for it then, closing a position with nothing behind it. Fixed with a per-node gate matching each node's own `entry_timing`.
8. **[MEDIUM]** No `mode='live'` guard — a live node with the flag flipped on could have a paper drought position silently suppress its own real BUY alerts via the shared `open_position_keys`/`wl_id` space. Fixed on both entry and handoff.
9. **[MEDIUM]** `reconcile_overlay_nodes` had no per-node fault isolation — a malformed row on one node would abort reconciliation for every node still left to check that night (only the inner backtest replay was guarded). Fixed with per-node/per-mechanism try/except in the coordinator loop.
10. Smaller: vol-gate `None`-handling polarity inverted vs. the backtest (unknown reading should exclude entry, not allow it); `MARGIN_COST_FLAT_PCT` missing from add-on P&L; an unmemoized per-poll CSV re-read on the vol-gated path; `add_daily_track_paper_nodes.py` had no way to carry the new config columns to a clone (fixed with a direct post-`add_node` sync + a new `signals_invariants.py` check, `check_daily_track_overlay_config_matches_live_track`, for ongoing drift); `get_trades_and_bars`/`generate_drought_trades`/`generate_addon_trades` need `node['arm_pct']`/`node['z']` normalization a raw `watch_list` row doesn't have — found the moment `reconcile_overlay_nodes` actually ran against real cached data, not caught by any review (no test had exercised the real replay path yet at that point).

**Coverage/reconciliation infra**: 6 new Accountability Grid rows (`drought_entry`, `drought_handoff`, `addon_entry_fill`, `addon_exit_fill`, `skim_fire`, `skim_redeploy_alert`), all `wired-never-fired`/`event-asserted` (via the registry's `registry id '<id>'` test-marker convention) since nothing has fired against the real live DB yet. Truth-table tests cover the 5 real reachable `(core, drought, addon)` state combinations and the two races the design doc names by name (addon-vs-core same-bar exit desync — structurally impossible by construction, since the addon leg never independently evaluates any exit condition; HANDOFF-vs-core-entry same-poll race — resolved by the ordering contract).

**Not done this session**: put-hedge (explicit scope exclusion), staged real-order testing (needs organic real signals over time, not a same-session step), the edge-case hardening pass (this project's own history suggests one will be needed once staged testing starts producing real data), and actually running the schema migration against the real live DB (deferred to the next natural `ensure_tables()` call, per the project's standing convention that the agent doesn't mutate the live DB directly).

## ✅ [backtest][data] Resolved 2026-08-08 (late) — `prune_backtest_cache.py`'s take_profit/NULL bug fixed; 17 tickers' zeroed TrailingBoth v5 island data recovered from the pre-prune archive
Root cause (same class as the `top_safe_nodes.py`/`three_layer_summary.py` bug fixed 2026-08-07, and the same underlying `take_profit` overload flagged as a deferred schema item in `backlog_cache.md`): `_island_rowids_for_group`'s final `SELECT rowid ... WHERE take_profit IN (?)` filter used the raw `take_profit` column, which is always `NULL` for `TrailingBothZScoreBreakout` rows (that strategy stores its real arm value in `arm_sell_pct` instead). SQL's `x IN (NULL)` never matches, even against `NULL` rows, so the 2026-08-02 prune silently dropped the entire strategy for every ticker whose `TrailingBoth`/`v5` data hadn't been reswept after the prune ran (17 of 18 v4-universe tickers — TQQQ survived only because it happened to be reswept the next day). Confirmed via the same `docs/session_cache.md` 2026-08-06 (very late) entry that first found this, live-DB counts, and a fresh count against the archive before touching anything.
**Fix**: `scripts/prune_backtest_cache.py` now uses `TP_COL_SQL = "COALESCE(take_profit, arm_sell_pct)"` everywhere the old code referenced `take_profit` directly (winner selection, nearest-value search, final keep-rowid query) — same pattern already proven in `top_safe_nodes.py`.
**Recovery**: confirmed all 17 tickers' data fully intact in the permanent pre-prune archive (`cache/research/permanent_archive/trading_universe_pre_prune_20260801.db`, opened read-only) before writing anything — 698K-1.02M rows/ticker, ~14M rows total for the full grid. **Per explicit user decision, recovered island-only (not the full grid)**, matching how the rest of the live DB is already pruned: reused the fixed `_groups`/`_island_rowids_for_group` functions directly against the archive connection, collected 736,111 island rows across 17 tickers (31K-63K rows/ticker, 6 groups/ticker), and `INSERT OR IGNORE`'d them into the live DB (safe no-op on any accidental overlap, since `backtest_cache`'s real PK covers the full node key). Live DB backed up first (`trading_universe.db.pre_recovery_20260805_223249.bak`, 3.2GB) before any write.

## [live-trading][backtest] Resolved 2026-08-05 — piece 4: `scripts/paper_vs_backtest_reconcile.py` rebuilt to be `wl_id`-scoped and to report daily-track results from `daily_track_reconciliation_log` instead of re-deriving its own comparison
The original script (2026-08-04 very late) matched paper trades to a backtest replay by ticker and
entry date, recomputing its own win-rate/compounded-return comparison from `paper_trade_log` +
`get_trades_and_bars`. Two gaps once daily-track landed the same day: (1) ticker-only matching would
silently conflate live-track and daily-track paper trades for the same ticker now that both exist
as separate `watch_list` nodes; (2) daily-track already gets a much richer, purpose-built nightly
reconciliation (`paper_trading.reconcile_daily_track_nodes`, entry-miss and exit-wick
Close-vs-Open/trailing-peak counterfactuals, TIME-forced exclusion) written to
`daily_track_reconciliation_log` — recomputing a second, simpler comparison risked drifting from
that judgment rather than reporting it.

build). The script now runs two separate reports — `report_live_track` (unchanged comparison logic,
just wl_id-scoped, since nothing else computes this for live-track) and `report_daily_track` (reads
`db.get_daily_track_reconciliation_log(wl_id)`, filters to the date window, prints per-node action
counts via `Counter`, and lists individual rows for a `FLAGGED_ACTIONS` set — `entry_miss_unexplained`,

(shared by `drought_overlay_test.py`/`drought_buy_hold_test.py` too) was resolving a ticker's
live-track node via `MIN(id) ... WHERE mode='research' GROUP BY ticker`, which only happened to
avoid picking up the new daily-track clones because they were created later with higher ids —
tightened to `AND paper_role IS NULL` explicitly rather than relying on that incidental ordering.

Smoke-tested (`--tickers SOXL AGQ`): live-track report correctly shows real backtest/paper trade
counts and flags; daily-track report correctly shows "no reconciliation log entries in window" for
both (expected — the nightly reconcile job hasn't run yet against the just-created nodes). Full
