## [live-trading][security] Resolved 2026-08-02 — both gaps deferred from the TP/TRAIL alert-wording fix closed: broker_stop_price clearing, and Skip no longer abandons a real resting order
Both found by the same Opus review that caught the alert-wording fixes; deliberately deferred at the
time (touches `_attempt_automated_sell`/`_attempt_automated_exit_sell`, which carry ~15 documented
regressions in their own comments — judged too risky to modify further without dedicated scoping).
**(1) `broker_stop_price` staleness — found already resolved on investigation, backlog was stale.**
Turned out to have been fixed the same day (2026-08-01, commit `9b2f22f`) by the session-wrap Opus
review's own HIGH finding — `set_broker_stop_price_by_position` now accepts `None` and is called at
both replace sites (`signals_notify.py:171`, `:343`) right after a real replace succeeds. This backlog
item just hadn't been updated to reflect that; no code change needed here, only doc cleanup.
**(2) `handle_sell_skipped` (`signals_handlers.py`) now cancels a real resting FRESH exit order before
dropping local tracking**, instead of just popping `exit_pending` (and its `order_id`) with nothing left
polling it. **The first version of this fix (committed to working tree, never landed) unconditionally
cancelled whatever order `exit_pending.order_id` pointed at — a paired independent+contextual Opus
review (2026-08-02) confirmed this was itself a HIGH real-money regression**: for a genuine TRAIL breach
(not hold-time-forced), `_attempt_automated_exit_sell` reuses the SAME order placed at the earlier arm
event (`signals_notify.py:251-252`) — the position's ONLY live protection, since arming already replaced
the stop-loss with it (confirmed by reading `_attempt_automated_exit_sell`/`notify_trailing_activated`
directly, not just taking the review's word for it). Cancelling it on Skip would leave the position with
zero broker protection while the alert simultaneously says "no action needed." The review also caught:
`exit_order_id` left stale after a cancel (next bar's forced-exit attempt would try to replace an
already-dead order and fail — the exact pre-existing risk `_attempt_automated_exit_sell`'s own comments
already flagged, reached through this new door); a confirmed `FILLED` status mishandled two ways (via a
race during the cancel call, and via the order already being FILLED before Skip was even tapped) with
`exit_pending` dropped either way, silently disarming `check_own_sell_fills`' polling reconciliation; and
`exit_pending` popped unconditionally even on a failed/unconfirmed cancel, recreating the exact "live
order with nothing polling it" bug the fix was meant to close, just on the unhappy path.

**Rewritten, correctly scoped:** cancellation now only applies to a genuinely FRESH exit order (TP/SL/
TIME, or a hold-time-forced TRAIL replace) — a standing arm-time trailing-sell (genuine TRAIL breach) is
left untouched, Skip only clears that alert's own reminder tracking. `exit_pending` is only dropped on a
confirmed `CANCELED`; a confirmed/discovered `FILLED` leaves it in place so `check_own_sell_fills`'
existing polling reconciles the real close with the real fill price instead of this handler guessing; an
unconfirmed/failed cancel also leaves it in place. A successful hold-time-forced cancel additionally
clears `exit_order_id`/`hold_time_replaced` so the next forced-exit attempt doesn't retry a dead order.
`pos` is re-fetched immediately before the write (the stale-snapshot clobber class this region has been
bitten by repeatedly — `_exit_order_resting`'s broker round-trip can take seconds). New
`tests/test_fake_broker_sell_skipped_scenario.py` (4 scenarios, zero prior coverage existed for this
handler) pins all four branches, including the TRAIL-protection-must-not-cancel case as the primary
regression guard. Full suite: 499 passed, no regressions.

**User's expectation, 2026-08-02**: this whole Skip/Exited manual-confirmation flow may be redone as
part of a broader Slack-interface rework once v5 moves toward no manual step at all (see the
`manual_buy_confirmation_account` entry above) — landed anyway since it's a live real-money gap today
and the redesign isn't scheduled.

## ✅ [live-trading][coverage] Resolved 2026-08-01 (evening) — GDXU TRAIL-exit alert wording bug closed, 2 review rounds
Original finding (2026-07-28): `_build_sell_blocks`'s TP/TRAIL branches hardcoded "Cancel Stop Loss
order — Sell All (Market)" regardless of whether an SL order actually rested — for a genuinely armed
position (SL already replaced by a resting trailing-sell, per `_attempt_automated_sell`), this reads
as an instruction to cancel an order that doesn't exist. Confirmed still real: `notify_sell_signal`
was rewritten 2026-07-31/08-01 to attempt an automated exit for every SELL reason before ever posting
a manual alert, falling through to `_build_sell_blocks` only when a short (~15s) fill-confirm poll
doesn't return a result — the *normal* case for a resting trailing-stop, not evidence of a problem.
The other sub-issue from the original finding (`_current_price()`'s overnight staleness guard) was
already fixed 2026-07-31 (widened to a straight age check) — confirmed via code read, no action needed.
**Fix (round 1)**: `_build_sell_blocks`/`_exit_pending_blocks` branch on whether an automated exit
order is confirmed resting instead of always showing the manual-cancel instruction.
**Opus review round 1 found 3 real gaps, all fixed**:
1. **HIGH**: the first version trusted a stored `order_id`'s mere presence as proof of a resting
   order — indistinguishable from a REJECTED/CANCELED one (real failure mode, see LABD's rejected
   stop, 2026-07-31), and the reassuring text removed the only warning that case had. Fixed: new
   `schwab_client.get_order_status(account, order_id)` (single non-retrying real status check,
   deliberately not reusing `_confirm_order_status`'s 4x0.5s retry loop built for right-after-
   placement use) + `signals_notify._exit_order_resting(pos, reason, order_id)`, a tri-state
   (True/False/None) check that fails toward the cautious message on both False and None.
2. **MEDIUM**: TIME reason was left on the old "Change Stop Loss → Market Close" text, contradicting
   its own now-reason-agnostic 15-min reminder. Fixed after confirming `_attempt_automated_exit_sell`
   really does route TIME through the identical market-sell path as TP (traced end to end).
3. **MEDIUM**: the TRAIL fix's first version missed its own target case (`exit_order_id` legitimately
   None on a real automated placement success) via a `trail_state['order_placed']` fallback.
Also escalated `_exit_pending_blocks`'s wording after `reminder_num >= 3` even when confirmed resting
("should have filled by now, worth a look") — the original 2026-07-28 design intent (distinguish
"routine still-waiting" from "should have filled by now"), not just wording.
**Opus review round 2 (verification pass on the round-1 fixes) found 2 more real gaps, both fixed**:
1. `_exit_order_resting` gated on `schwab_client._ORDER_TERMINAL_BAD_STATUSES` (3 statuses: REJECTED/
   CANCELED/EXPIRED, built for a different question) instead of `schwab_safety._OPEN_ORDER_STATUSES_
   EXCLUDED` (5 statuses, the set the resting-order duplicate guard already uses for "is this
   genuinely still open") — would have reported "confirmed resting" for an order that had actually
   FILLED or been REPLACED. Fixed by switching to the correct 5-status set.
2. The `trail_state['order_placed']` fallback for TRAIL was itself unsafe — `order_placed` is ALSO set
   by `signals_handlers.handle_trail_order_placed`, a manual Slack button tap with no broker
   verification, and there's no stored provenance distinguishing which path set it. Trusting it would
   have reintroduced the exact "trust an unverified flag instead of the broker" pattern this whole fix
   exists to eliminate, through a different door. **Removed rather than patched under time pressure**
   — the narrow sub-case it targeted (unextractable order id on a real automated TRAIL placement)
   reverts to the pre-2026-08-01 cautious text; not a new regression, same as before this session.
**Deferred, not fixed this session** (see the paired backlog entry): `broker_stop_price` never cleared
after a replace (now more load-bearing since `stop_status()` reads it directly); `handle_sell_skipped`
abandons tracking of a real resting order without cancelling it. Both touch
`_attempt_automated_sell`/`_attempt_automated_exit_sell`, judged too risky to modify further in the
same session given their documented regression history.
19 new tests (`tests/test_exit_order_resting.py`, `tests/test_sell_blocks_automated_exit_wording.py`).
Full suite: 493 passed (was 479). `signals_invariants.py`: clean.

## [live-trading][coverage] Partially resolved 2026-08-01 — the 07-27 canary_* duplicate-row concern was already inert; cleaned up

coverage system to real node_id identity"). The original 6 rows (seeded 2026-07-24) had `mode=None`;
the migration re-seeded the same `(scenario_key, node_id, ticker)` combos with `mode='live'` explicitly
set. Since `add_scenario_expectation`'s dedup key is `(scenario_key, node_id, ticker, mode)`, the
differing `mode` meant "not a match" — new rows got inserted instead of updating the old ones in place.
**Verified NOT a live bug**: the old `mode=None` rows were already `active=0` (mechanism unclear — no
current code sets `active=0` for this table, likely a manual DB edit during the same 07-25 session, not

`coverage_check.py` and `pages/14_Coverage.py` explicitly filter `WHERE active=1` too — confirmed via
source read, not inference. So the duplicates never double-counted or affected `coverage_check.py`'s
output. Cleaned up anyway: backed up `cache/live/trading_live.db` first (daemon confirmed running but
this table sees no concurrent writes), deleted the 7 `active=0` rows directly. Full suite (coverage/
scenario-tagged subset): 126 passed, unaffected (isolated test DBs).
**Still open**: whether `canary_early_sl`/`canary_full_lifecycle`/`canary_market_buy_exit`/

## [live-trading][security] Resolved 2026-08-01 (evening) — real incident: an ad hoc test call posted a real Slack message; SIM_MODE flipped to a fail-safe default
While testing the reconciliation_mismatch fix above, `signals_notify.build_eod_scenario_review('2026-07-31')`
was called directly in a Python one-liner without setting `SIM_MODE=1` first — it returned a real
`(channel, ts)` pair, confirming a real, unprefixed message posted to the live Slack channel (content:
a coverage/readiness report, not a trade action — no order was placed). Root cause: `signals_config.
SIM_MODE` defaulted OFF (`os.environ.get("SIM_MODE") == "1"`), an opt-in-safety design that fails open —
any ad hoc script/test invocation that forgets to export it posts for real.
**Fix, user-directed**: flipped the default to fail-safe (`os.environ.get("SIM_MODE", "1") != "0"` — ON
unless explicitly set to `"0"`), matching the fail-closed pattern already used everywhere else in this
codebase (kill switch, oversell guard, node circuit breaker). Since `SIM_MODE`/`INTERACTIVE`/the Bolt
app singleton are computed at `signals_config` import time, the real daemon can't set this itself after
importing — `active_signals.py`'s own entrypoint now runs `os.environ.setdefault('SIM_MODE', '0')`
as literally its first executable line (before `import sys`, well before `signals_config` is reachable
via any import chain), so the existing real launch command (`python active_signals.py run` / bare
`python active_signals.py`) needs no change at all and no env var to remember.
**Defense in depth**: new `signals_invariants.check_sim_mode_off_for_real_daemon()` — deliberately NOT
added to `CHECKS`/`run_all()`, since that function also runs standalone via the pre-commit checklist
(`.venv/bin/python signals_invariants.py`), where `SIM_MODE=1` is the correct, expected default and
would false-positive on every routine pre-commit run. Instead called directly, once, from
`run_loop()`'s own startup (non-blocking, alerted not fatal, matching the existing invariants-check
pattern immediately below it) — catches the one real remaining failure mode, `SIM_MODE=1` already
exported in the shell before launch (`setdefault` respects an existing value by design and won't
override it), which would otherwise silently turn the real daemon into a no-op simulator: every alert
misleadingly prefixed 🧪 SIM MODE, every interactive button (Executed/Filled/Order Placed/Exited/
Skipped) disabled.
Verified all 4 real scenarios directly: ad hoc script alone → SIM ON; `active_signals` imported → SIM
OFF; `SIM_MODE=1` pre-exported then `active_signals` imported → stays ON (setdefault correctly
respects it); `signals_invariants.py` run standalone → no false-positive SIM_MODE violation.
**Not fixed / open question**: whether to post a Slack follow-up in the live channel clarifying the
earlier accidental EOD-report post was a test artifact — deferred to the user's call, not urgent (no
trade action, just a coverage report).

## ✅ [live-trading][security] Resolved 2026-08-01 (session-wrap review) — final whole-diff Opus review of all 5 session pieces together found 2 real cross-piece bugs, both fixed
Required by `session wrap` (CLAUDE.md): once individual pieces are reviewed and fixed, the FULL combined
diff still needs one end-to-end pass, since a fix in one piece can be undermined by another piece added
later in the same session. Findings:
1. **HIGH — piece 1 (SL alert `stop_status`) activated a dead code path that was never given the
   staleness handling it needed.** `broker_stop_price` had zero production writers before this session
   (confirmed: the legacy `set_broker_stop_price` was dead code) — so `_build_sell_blocks`/
   `_exit_pending_blocks`'s `'known'`/`if bsp:` branches were dead in production too. Making the field
   live (piece 1's whole point) meant it also needed to be *cleared* wherever the real stop it describes
   gets replaced — which happens routinely: `_attempt_automated_sell`'s arm-time SL→trailing-sell
   replace, and `_attempt_automated_exit_sell`'s TP/SL/TIME market-sell replace. Left uncleared,
   `stop_status()` reported `'known'` off a dead price — a real SL alert firing after either replace
   would have falsely said "broker stop on file, no action needed" for a position actually protected
   only by an unconfirmed resting order, a behavior *regression* from the pre-diff cautious "check
   account" text. Fixed: `db.set_broker_stop_price_by_position` now accepts `None` to clear; wired into
   both replace sites (`signals_notify.py`, the arm-time success path and the TP/SL/TIME replace
   success path, gated on `resting_order_id == pos.get('sl_order_id')` so only a genuine SL replace
   clears it, not a trailing-sell-to-trailing-sell no-op). 2 new regression tests
   (`tests/test_broker_stop_price_cleared_on_replace.py`, via `fake_broker`) prove the field actually
   clears after both real replace paths, not just that the code compiles.
2. **MEDIUM — piece 4's `os.environ.setdefault('SIM_MODE', '0')` sat at module-import scope**, so any
   `import active_signals` (the file's own documented library-reuse pattern — 11+ scripts do exactly
   this) silently disabled the new fail-safe default, reproducing the exact incident the change existed
   to prevent, just through the library-import path instead of a bare script. Verified empirically
   before and after the fix. Fixed: gated behind `if __name__ == '__main__':` (Python sets `__name__`
   before any of a module's top-level code runs, imports included, so this is safe to check at the very
   top of the file, before any imports) — only a real direct invocation (`python active_signals.py
   [run|list|add|remove|positions]`) now opts back into real posting; a library import stays SIM-ON by
   default. Re-verified both directions empirically (library import → stays True; direct execution via
   `runpy.run_path(..., run_name='__main__')`, the same mechanism as `python active_signals.py` → False).
Also checked and confirmed clean (no fix needed): piece 5's `is_protective` exemption doesn't interact
badly with the trading-day gate (separate, unconditional, unaffected) or with SIM_MODE/dry-run (the
window gate is side/flag-driven, doesn't branch on either); `tests/conftest.py`'s new
`cfg.INTERACTIVE = True` forcing doesn't mask any of piece 2's tests (every consumer reads `cfg.
INTERACTIVE` via the same patched module object, and piece 2's own tests explicitly override it back to
False per-test where needed); piece 3's `other_by_key` grouping composes correctly with the rest.
2 cosmetic-only findings (a stale docstring claim in a test file contradicting its own sibling test, a
redundant no-op patch loop in conftest) — not fixed, zero behavior impact, noted for whoever touches
that code next.
Full suite: 495 passed (was 466 at session start). `signals_invariants.py`: clean.
`live_sim_harness.py`: 7/7. `verify_trailing_buy_resolution.py`/`verify_trailing_sell_resolution.py
--tickers AGQ,SOXL`: both clean, matching expected drift.

## ✅ [live-trading][security] Resolved 2026-08-01 — real live-trading bug found via the Accountability Grid, not a diff review: post-fill top-up BUYs blocked 100% of the time outside signal windows
Found by running `scripts/coverage_registry.py` directly to answer "what's still uncovered" — showed
`top_up` as `live-attempt-failed`: fired for real 3 times, failed every single time
(`db_update_failed_after_real_order`, `failed_unexpectedly`, `blocked`, `overspent_no_corrective_sell`).
Traced the real events (`db.get_coverage_events(scenario_key='top_up')`): 2 of 3 were rejected for
`"BUY outside signal windows"` at 18:57 and 00:19 — hours after any signal window, exactly when a
delayed trailing-buy fill would land.
**Root cause**: `schwab_safety.check_order`'s signal-window gate (`schwab_safety.py:950`) only exempted
`is_gap_correction`, not `is_protective`. The post-fill top-up BUY (`signals_notify._reconcile_fill`,
`is_protective=True`) passes `is_gap_correction` through from its triggering fill — but that only
covers the ONE narrow case where the fill itself came from `check_gap_resize`. The general case (any
normal trailing-buy fill landing outside the narrow windows, which is routine — a resting order can
fill hours after the signal fired) was still gated. The code's own docstring shows the author was aware
of the narrow case but missed the general one. A top-up isn't a fresh signal-driven entry — it's
completing an already-approved one, same reasoning already applied to `is_gap_correction`.
**Fix**: `check_order`'s window-gate condition widened to `not is_gap_correction and not is_protective`.
Checked every real `is_protective=True` BUY-side call site (only one exists — the top-up itself; the
other two are SELL-side, where the window gate never applied anyway) to confirm no unintended scope
widening. Regression test added (`tests/test_schwab_safety.py::test_protective_buy_bypasses_signal_
window_gate`) confirming a non-protective BUY still gets blocked outside the window while a protective
one doesn't.
**Why the test suite never caught this**: nobody had ever written a test for `is_protective` against
the signal-window gate specifically — only the daily-cap exemption
(`test_protective_top_up_bypasses_exhausted_daily_cap`) was tested. The bug was invisible to "suite is
green" because the specific combination (top-up + outside-window) was never exercised. Found instead by
checking real broker outcomes via the Accountability Grid, not by reading the diff or trusting test
coverage — the exact reason the Grid was built.
Full suite: 494 passed (subsequently 495 after the session-wrap review's 2 more tests).

## ✅ [backtest] Resolved 2026-08-03 — paired-ticker/idle-capital strategy paradigm refuted with real cross-checked evidence; framework abandoned
Full writeup: `docs/research_log.md`'s 2026-08-03 "Idle-capital/joint-capital pairing framework, refuted" entry. Summary: what started as a real strategy idea (use a ticker's matched leveraged inverse to trade during idle capital windows) went through several framings across the session — static hold (rejected, leveraged-decay blowup), secondary-trade/idle-window-fill (initially looked promising, AGQ/ZSL 1.56x), then concurrent/additive (raised as the "real" version, but killed as underpowered to test before building — 3 real pairs vs a random-pair control isn't a meaningful sample). The idle-window-fill framing was then tested properly at scale: all 90 directional pairs among the 10 real v5 watchlist tickers (no inverse relationship needed) showed the same mean~1.0, huge-variance (0.27x-3.45x) noise pattern as the "special" inverse pairs — confirming the multiplier reflects trade-timing-overlap luck and small-denominator artifacts, not a real structural edge, inverse-pair or otherwise. Where enough real history existed to test time-consistency (SOXL/AGQ, 5 equal periods), the result was small but genuinely consistent — and negative (a drag, not a benefit). SOXS's headline 1.85x number was traced to an n=2 real-period sample that didn't even agree with itself (2.10x then 0.74x). **Practical conclusion**: run v5 nodes independently, as the live watchlist already does — no coordination mechanism between tickers showed a reliable payoff. The individual nodes' own backtested edges are unaffected; only the *combination* mechanism was refuted.

## ✅ [backtest] Resolved 2026-08-03 — SOXS added to real v5 backtest_cache via the committed sweep queue; TrailingExitZScoreBreakout fixed_sl=2 is the cliff-safe winner
User ran `VERSION=v5 TICKERS="SOXS" FIXED_SLS="1 2 3" STRATEGIES="TrailingBothZScoreBreakout TrailingExitZScoreBreakout" ./scripts/run_sweep_queue.sh` to completion (910,940 `TrailingBoth` rows, 66,620 `TrailingExit` rows). Full pairing/robustness follow-up in `docs/research_log.md`'s 2026-08-03 entries.

Flipped all 3 nodes `mode='live'`, set `starting_notional` to the planned figures, logged via `watch_list_audit`, DB backed up first. GDXU (also research-mode in the same account) deliberately left alone — still under the active GDXU/AGQ wash-sale hold (clears 2026-08-05/06).

**Caught by `signals_invariants.py` before it could bite live**: the resized `starting_notional` values ($1,000-$2,500) exceeded `soxl_ira`'s real `notional_cap` of $800 (a stale figure from 2026-07-24, set "conservatively low pending a real balance check" — that balance check never happened until this session). Every entry/top-up attempt for the 3 newly-resized nodes would have been structurally blocked by the account's own per-order safety ceiling, silently defeating the whole point of the resize. Raised `notional_cap` 800→3,000. Independent Opus review (isolated worktree) confirmed the fix is correct and found two real follow-on points, both left open rather than fixed this session (user's call, "let's see what happens"): (1) real order sizing compounds off `_last_sale_recovery` (last closed trade's proceeds), not the static `starting_notional` — so after HIBL/YANG's first winning trade (~+22%+), the effective order ceiling could re-approach $3,000 and re-trigger the same block, and `signals_invariants.py`'s current check (`starting_notional > notional_cap` only) won't catch that recurrence since it doesn't look at compounded proceeds; (2) no aggregate cross-node exposure guard exists anywhere in `schwab_safety.py` — 9 live nodes now share `soxl_ira` with nominal-sum exposure ($10,200) exceeding the ~$9k real balance, a pre-existing gap (documented 2026-08-02 resting-order balance blind spot) now more relevant at the higher per-order cap. `live_sim_harness.py`: 7/7 scenarios pass. `signals_invariants.py`: all invariants hold post-fix.

## ✅ [backtest] Resolved 2026-08-08 — paired Opus review of the v5-stacked framework found 1 CRITICAL + 3 HIGH + several MEDIUM/LOW real bugs, all fixed; one prior claim in this doc's history corrected
Full writeup: `docs/research_log.md`'s 2026-08-08 entry (research narrative — hypothesis/method/result for each finding, not duplicated here). Summary: user-requested paired Opus review (contextual + independent/cold) of yesterday's v5-stacked framework, outside the mechanical trigger since these are research scripts not `signals_*.py`/kernel — user wanted it anyway given real capital decisions ride on the numbers. Both reviews converged, no rebuttal conflict. Fixed: add-on's compounding math (was mathematically wrong, not just approximate — corrected the earlier 2026-08-07 claim in this log that 100%-margin sizing made the multiplicative stacking exact; AGQ's number was inflated ~1.43x), add-on account-eligibility gating (AGQ only, real margin account; SOXL/KORU reported but flagged not-executable per the user's explicit "report it as not safe" instruction), a CRITICAL skim-reserve redeploy-trigger bug (fired on noise, never required a real decline first), put-hedge's liquidity gate (checked the wrong strike, was warning-only not a real gate), real spread cost + correct capital-denominator in hedge pricing (found live mid-session by the user asking about a real SOXL put purchase), a scale-mismatch bug in the crash-stress script's spread cost (today's real dollar spread wrongly applied to synthetic 2008-era $2-5 prices, producing a spurious -98% wipeout), max-drawdown calc missing the starting peak, `top_safe_nodes.py`'s incomplete entry_timing fix (same neighbor-search bug pattern as the 2026-08-07 trail_buy_pct fix, plus an unreproducible output dict), drought's neighbor-search allowing thin single-window cells to corrupt safety verdicts, a widened `CONFIRM_DAYS_GRID` that had been silently missing confirm_days=3 (the value SOXL's marquee finding uses), a no-data-counts-as-positive bug in the 18-ticker drought scan, a fail-open default on an empty neighbor set in `three_layer_summary.py`, and (the most consequential correction) **`v5_stacked_backtest.py` was using SOXL's plain unvalidated drought default (confirm_days=10) instead of the real validated confirm_days=3/vol_gate=0.4 signal** — corrected core+drought from 1587.0% to 3461.5%. Verified afterward: SOXL's marquee drought finding survives the neighbor-bug fix completely unchanged (none of its neighbors were thin cells); KORU's drought overlay stays correctly rejected; SOXL's crash-stress put-hedge benefit holds up across all 4 historical crashes after every pricing correction. Real open design questions surfaced and deliberately deferred (not bugs): when to hedge (vol-gated trigger proposed, not built — "additive, skip for now, notionals will be low next year"), daily overnight-only put hedge vs. hold-through-trade (still genuinely undecided, a real backlog item already), put roll-past-20-days (low priority), and the two runner scripts' different IV-proxy defaults (not a bug — both legitimate for their own context, no fix needed).

## ✅ [backtest][coverage] Resolved 2026-08-1x — `trade_log`/`paper_trade_log` `wl_id=NULL` backfill: extended the existing `ensure_tables()` migration to cover both tables, added an `added_at` tie-break for the live-track/daily-track ambiguity it exposed
Root cause (unchanged from the original finding): `log_trade_entry`'s `wl_id` write only landed in commit `fb699cf` (2026-08-09) — `open_positions`/`paper_positions`' own `wl_id` write is much older (2026-07-26) — so historical trade_log/paper_trade_log rows never got backfilled the way the 2026-07-24 `account` backfill precedent did for other columns. Fixed by extending `signals_db.ensure_tables()`'s existing idempotent `(ticker, strategy, version, window, account)`-match migration (already run for `open_positions`/`paper_positions`) to also cover `trade_log`/`paper_trade_log` — same code path, not a new script. This surfaced a real ambiguity the original migration never had to handle: 35 of 36 `paper_trade_log` NULL rows matched *two* watch_list candidates (a live-track/daily-track pair sharing every match column by construction, per the 2026-08-05 daily-track design) even though every one of these trades predates the 2026-08-05 daily-track node creation. Fixed by adding an `added_at`-based tie-break — when a match is ambiguous, drop any candidate whose `watch_list.added_at` is after the trade's `entry_time` (that node didn't exist yet, so it can't be the source). Verified against a copy of the real `trading_live.db` before touching the live one: `paper_trade_log` NULL wl_id 36→1 (the 1 remaining is a genuinely pre-account-column legacy row, 0 candidates), `trade_log` NULL wl_id 60→16 (remaining rows are legacy v3.x/deleted-node trades — EDC, GDXD/LABU `soxl_test`, JNUG `v4`/`canary` — same "acceptable, leave NULL" behavior as the original open_positions/paper_positions precedent). Applied to the real `cache/live/trading_live.db` after backup (`trading_live.db.bak_pre_wlid_backfill_20260806_114323`), daemon running throughout (additive UPDATE on historical closed-trade rows only, no interaction with in-flight state) — row counts unchanged, `PRAGMA integrity_check` clean. Full suite: 589 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (`test_automated_exit_sell_replace_updates_stale_sl_order_id`'s `webbrowser.Error`, confirmed environmental).

## ✅ [backtest] Resolved 2026-08-09 (later still) — `certain` fill-resolution kernel fix (two real bugs) applied and verified; recompute + tooling gap tabled by user's explicit call
Full investigation narrative: `docs/research_log.md`'s 2026-08-09 (later still) entry. Two real, independent bugs in `_simulate_trail_both`'s certain branch (`backtester.py`), both fixed: (1) Close-crediting bug (already documented in the prior 2026-08-09 entry above) — a Close-confirmed fill credited the theoretical trigger price, not the real Close, crediting a price already passed and unobtainable; (2) frozen-trigger case — a bar whose own Low doesn't move the running low has its trigger frozen for the entire bar regardless of intrabar ordering, so a High-touch on such a bar is exactly as certain as an Open-gap; the old code only ever checked Close-confirmation and needlessly deferred these (56 of 141 total `possible` fills on SOXL's own node, 40%, were this exact case). Fix added directly to `_simulate_trail_both`'s certain branch, plus a new standalone lean kernel `_simulate_certain_only`/`run_backtest_certain_only` (no possible/pessimistic bookkeeping) for a cheaper future recompute — verified byte-identical to the corrected bundled kernel (0 mismatches, multiple tickers). A hand-written Python mirror built earlier in the same session for ad hoc analysis was found to have missed the frozen-trigger fix and silently diverged from the real kernel across ~80 tickers' worth of conclusions — all discarded, redone against the real verified kernel. Per-ticker impact of the full fix: NOT uniform (2x to 11x drop from the old buggy value depending on ticker). **Correction (found during the session-wrap paired review below): an earlier note claimed "KORU flips to a real loss" — that was from the since-discarded incomplete mirror; the real kernel-verified value is +64.6%, still clearly positive, no sign flip.** **User's explicit call: table the full `backtest_cache` certain-column recompute (~5M rows) and the broader "possible-only tooling" architectural gap (candidate overlay/reporting pipeline never had a real certain/pessimistic trade-generation path, only a scalar `robust_alpha` MIN() input) — `possible` stays the working default, both because it's already the empirically stronger/more-frequently-winning resolution (same-node possible-vs-corrected-certain check: possible wins 45/81 tickers, certain 26/81, and by a much larger margin when it wins) and because the kernel fix's practical payoff didn't justify the compute/tooling cost right now.** Kernel fix left in place (real bug, harmless to leave fixed) even though nothing currently depends on it.

**Paired independent+contextual Opus review run at session wrap per this project's kernel-change convention — found a real CONFIRMED HIGH issue, not just a clean bill of health.** Both reviewers independently flagged, then reconciled via a rebuttal exchange, that the Close-crediting fix isn't actually a proven no-guess price: it's provably always ≥ the old buggy code's credit (one-directional, not a mixed correction), with no proven relationship to the true resting-order fill. A direct isolation test confirmed this — not the frozen-trigger fix — is the dominant driver of the reported 2x-11x drop: frozen-trigger-only (keeping the old Close-credit) actually IMPROVES every ticker checked over the original buggy baseline (SOXL +3099.5%, KORU +914.6%, AGQ +1523.5%, HIBL +1381.4%, GDXD +926.1%); adding the Close-crediting fix on top is what pulls all of them down (SOXL +1439.7%, KORU +64.6%, AGQ +1061.7%, HIBL +687.4%, GDXD +340.4%). Both reviewers proposed `min(buy_trigger_prior, high)` as a genuinely tight, provable bound instead of `cp`, confirmed mathematically valid by both — but flagged as a real semantic shift (would make `certain` a pessimistic-price bound, contradicting its own docstring's "certain can end up better than possible" claim, which only actually holds for the frozen-trigger case). **Not fixed this session** — left open pending a real decision on which definition of "certain" (provable fill vs. provable price) is wanted, rather than picking one at session wrap under time pressure. Also confirmed by both reviewers: `scripts/export_trades.py::simulate_trail_both_signal_tracked` and `scripts/verify_fill_resolution_accuracy.py` still run the pre-fix certain logic and are now silently stale (the latter is the tool whose "possible is 94% accurate" finding justified the possible-as-default decision above — it should be fixed before being trusted again); no pinned regression test exists for the frozen-trigger case or for `_simulate_certain_only`'s parity with the bundled kernel (only a one-off manual verification this session); `_simulate_trail_both`'s docstring was not updated to reflect either fix. Full detail: `docs/research_log.md`'s 2026-08-09 (later still) entry.

## ✅ [backtest] Resolved 2026-08-09 (later still) — `candidate_full_review.py` gained 3 CAGR-stacking columns (`core_addon_cagr_pct`/`core_drought_cagr_pct`/`core_both_cagr_pct`), each overlay gated on its own robustness verdict; `drought_ie_*`'s vol-gate REAL_SELECTION verdict now actually overrides the plain drought number instead of sitting disconnected
Real gap found and fixed: `drought_included_excluded_check`'s vol-gate verdict (`REAL_SELECTION`/`DISCRIMINATES_BUT_UNPROFITABLE`/`NO_REAL_SELECTION`) was purely diagnostic — confirming whether the entry-time intraday-vol filter does real differential selection — but never fed back into the reported `drought_compounded_pct`/CAGR numbers at all, even when confirmed to genuinely work. Now: when `drought_ie_verdict=REAL_SELECTION` for a row, its vol-gated included-only compounded return replaces the plain (ungated) drought factor in the new CAGR-stacking columns, since a confirmed-real filter is strictly better evidence than the ungated overlay. Multiplicative stacking confirmed correct via manual verification (two ~1.5-1.6x-robust overlays multiply to ~2.3-2.7x, not ~3-4x as naive addition would suggest — real math, not a bug, see `docs/research_log.md` if this needs re-deriving). Non-robust overlays (FRAGILE verdicts) contribute a factor of 1 (no effect), so a fragile add-on/drought can't silently inflate the combined number. Also fixed same session: `--csv`/`--xlsx` outputs were silently overwriting the same filename on every run (no history) — now always timestamped (`_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS` suffix) via new `_timestamped_name()` helper, matching this project's "never delete/overwrite, versioning exists for coexistence" convention.

## 2026-08-15 — ✅ built end-of-year tax forecast script (brokerage-only): `tax_realized_loss_baseline` table + `k1_tax.brokerage_tax_forecast()` netting/reserve math + `scripts/evening_status.py` part2 wiring
Closes the "build end-of-year tax forecast script" backlog item's realized-loss-baseline-netting + reserve-recommendation piece specifically (the 2026-08-15 model worked out in `docs/backlog_cache.md`) — NOT the separate, still-open "K-1 tax forecast tool needs real data" item (`k1_tax.py`/`k1_tax_forecast.py` themselves are still populated with synthetic/manually-logged data, untouched by this build beyond reusing their `RateConfig`/`load_rate_config`/`blended_rate()`/`get_payments()`).

**Scope, confirmed via a peer session before building**: `brokerage` account only — no distribution-tracking or scope for `ira`/`roth`/`soxl_ira`, deliberately narrow.

**Built**:
- `signals_db.py` `ensure_tables()`: new `tax_realized_loss_baseline` table (`id, account, tax_year, amount, character CHECK IN ('short_term','long_term'), note, created_at`), seeded once (idempotent, checked by `account/tax_year/character` before insert) with the real `account='brokerage', tax_year=2026, amount=240000, character='short_term'` baseline the user gave.
- `signals_db.add_tax_realized_loss_baseline()` / `get_tax_realized_loss_baseline()` (sums multiple rows of the same character, if any — supports a future correction/carryforward row without overwriting).
- `signals_db.get_realized_pnl_by_ticker(account, tickers, year)` — real dollar P&L per ticker from `trade_log`, `(exit_price - entry_price) * shares`, scoped to `exit_time`'s calendar year, excluding `is_dry_run_sim=1` and never touching `paper_trade_log` — same convention as `scripts/annual_pnl_report.py`.
- `k1_tax.py`: `SECTION_1256_TICKERS = frozenset({"AGQ"})` (real, documented fact — AGQ is the one Section-1256 K-1 PTP in `brokerage` today; JNUG/ETHU are standard '40-Act ETFs, 100% ordinary short-term) and `brokerage_tax_forecast(year, realized_gains_by_ticker, baseline, rates=None, estimate_already_paid=0.0) -> BrokerageTaxForecast`. Reuses `RateConfig`/`load_rate_config()` entirely — no rate values hardcoded here. Netting: combined short-term pool = ordinary-ST tickers' gains + 40%-short-term slice of every Section-1256 ticker's gain, netted TOGETHER against the short-term baseline; the 60%-long-term slice is only reduced by a long-term-character baseline (0 today, since the real baseline is 100% short-term — confirmed by a dedicated test). `Liability = lt_gain_net*lt_rate + st_pool_net*st_rate`; `Reserve = max(0, Liability - estimate_already_paid)`. `recommend_full_sweep` signals True once both baseline characters are exhausted AND liability remains — informational/report text only, no automated action (this project's detection-only pattern).
- `scripts/evening_status.py`: new `_brokerage_tax_forecast_section()`, called near the top of `part2()` (before the node loop, not the Slack EOD message). Sources live `brokerage` tickers dynamically from `watch_list` (`account='brokerage' AND state='live'`) rather than hardcoding — confirmed against real DB before building: AGQ (id=203), ETHU (id=201), JNUG (id=205), matching the spec exactly. `estimate_already_paid` defaults to `sum(k1_tax.get_payments(year))` — reuses k1_tax's own real payment-tracking as the source of truth rather than inventing a new one, falls through to 0 naturally when nothing's logged. Header text and module docstring both state the calibration framing explicitly: reserve-sizing estimator, ~5-10% expected error, not filing-accuracy, CPA/K-1 confirms the real number.

**Verified against real data**: ran `scripts/evening_status.py 2` against the live `cache/live/trading_live.db` — `brokerage` has zero closed trades in any of AGQ/ETHU/JNUG this year (all three real `live` nodes are flat), so the real output today is `Liability=$0, Reserve=$0, baseline_remaining=$240,000` — correct given no realized gains exist yet to net against.

**Netting math confirmed by hand** (see `tests/test_tax_realized_loss_baseline.py`, 15 tests, all passing): example AGQ +$100k, JNUG +$50k, ETHU -$10k, baseline $240k short-term → `lt_gain_gross=$60,000` (100k*0.6, untouched by the ST baseline), `st_pool_gross=$80,000` (40k+50k-10k), fully absorbed by the $240k baseline → `st_pool_net=$0`, `liability = $60,000 * 0.38576 = $23,145.60` (default `RateConfig` blended LT rate). A second case (AGQ $200k/JNUG $150k/ETHU $100k) pushes the ST pool to $330k, clearing the baseline outright → `st_pool_net=$90,000`, `baseline_exhausted=True`, `recommend_full_sweep=True`, `liability = 120,000*0.38576 + 90,000*0.55576`. Both hand-computed and asserted in the pinned tests.

**Test coverage**: `tests/test_tax_realized_loss_baseline.py`, 15 tests — table seeding/idempotency, `get_realized_pnl_by_ticker`'s dollar-math/dry-run-sim exclusion/account+year scoping, and 8 tests pinning `brokerage_tax_forecast`'s netting math directly (baseline-absorbs-ST-pool, baseline-exhausted-triggers-sweep-signal, reserve-subtracts-paid, reserve-floors-at-zero, no-activity case, long-term-baseline-only-touches-LT-slice, no-Section-1256-activity classification). Full suite run after the change (no regressions found — see session notes for the exact pass count).

## ✅ 2026-08-16 — Built: per-`(account, ticker)` lock around the retry-and-confirm order-placement sequence
Closes the item spec'd 2026-08-15 (peer session, "planner") — closing the retry-dedup wrong-sibling-order-id gap (see the "Open, found 2026-08-16" item above, still open on its own terms — this lock is a concurrency-root mitigation of it, not a replacement for the matching-predicate fix) at its concurrency root instead of matching-predicate cleverness.

**Built** (`schwab_client.py`):
- `_retry_locks` dict + `_retry_locks_meta_lock` + `_get_retry_lock(account, ticker)` (~`schwab_client.py:107-122`) — returns a shared `threading.Lock` per `(account, ticker)`, created on first use; the meta-lock only guards the dict's own get-or-create moment, never held while a caller blocks on the returned lock.
- `_submit_order_with_retry` (`schwab_client.py:341-366`) split into a thin wrapper that acquires `_get_retry_lock(account, ticker)` (or `contextlib.nullcontext()` if either is missing) around the unchanged original body, now `_submit_order_with_retry_locked` (`schwab_client.py:369-410`).
- `_submit_replace_with_retry` (`schwab_client.py:413-...`) split identically into a wrapper + `_submit_replace_with_retry_locked`, same lock key.
- Whole placement+confirm sequence is locked (baseline-snapshot through the final broker-state check), not just the matching step — that's what actually removes the ambiguity rather than narrowing it. Mirrors the existing `open_position()`/`close_position()` lock pattern in `signals_db.py` (2026-07-22, same poll-loop-vs-handler-thread race shape) — a plain in-process `Lock` is enough since this is a single-process, multi-thread daemon.

**Proof**: new test `tests/test_fake_broker_retry_flapping_scenario.py::test_per_account_ticker_lock_serializes_concurrent_retry_loops` — fires 5 real `threading.Thread`s all calling `schwab_client._submit_order_with_retry` directly for the same `(account='soxl_ira', ticker=TICKER)`, with `fake_broker.place_order` wrapped to record max concurrent callers (0.05s artificial delay inside the critical section makes real overlap observable rather than relying on a race that might not manifest without it) — asserts `max_concurrent == 1`. Also asserts `_get_retry_lock('soxl_ira', TICKER)` returns the same `Lock` object across calls, and a different object for `_get_retry_lock('ira', TICKER)` (distinct keys don't share a lock). One real bug caught while getting this test green: the wrapper's `slow_place_order` originally called `fake_broker.place_order(...)` from inside itself after monkeypatching that same attribute onto itself, i.e. infinite self-recursion (surfaced as `max_concurrent=991`, not true thread concurrency) — fixed by capturing `original_place_order = fake_broker.place_order` before patching and calling that instead.

**Verified**: `tests/test_fake_broker_retry_flapping_scenario.py` 7/7 passing (6 pre-existing + the new one); `tests/test_schwab_client.py` 7/7 passing (no regression from the wrapper-split refactor); full sweep of every test file importing `schwab_client` (33 files) run clean.

## ✅ 2026-08-15 — trading_incidents id=9 (record_deviation/coverage_check auto-explain persistence bug), fixed in 2 paired-review rounds, 7 production rows repaired
Real incident: the evening coverage report showed 4 canary scenarios auto-explained in console output ("price never crossed entry threshold") but a direct DB query confirmed the underlying `coverage_deviations` rows were still `reason=None` — the explanation was computed and printed but never persisted.

**Round 1 root cause**: `signals_db.record_deviation` (the daily-check upsert) unconditionally reset `reason`/`reason_by`/`reason_ts` back to NULL whenever an existing row had `reason_by='system'` — but that value is written by two call sites with opposite meaning: `clear_deviation_if_resolved`'s `'Auto-resolved: ...'` (evidence about a PRIOR resolution, should reset on a new deviation) and `coverage_check.py`'s own price-action auto-explain `'Auto-verified: ...'` (evidence about THIS observation, should not be blindly reset). A same-day rerun whose own auto-explain condition no longer held would reset a good explanation and never re-set it, stranding the row. Fixed by scoping the reset to the `'Auto-resolved:'` prefix specifically.

**Round 1 mistake, caught by paired review (both independent-cold and contextual reviewers converged independently)**: the round-1 fix over-corrected into ALWAYS preserving a stale `'Auto-verified:'` reason on any rerun — masking a later pass that finds a genuinely new problem (a trade closing with the wrong `exit_reason`, or the entry threshold now confirmed crossed) behind the stale "nothing to see" note, silently hiding a real deviation from `get_deviations(unexplained_only=True)` and the daily report. Confirmed empirically by both reviewers on isolated DBs.

**Round 2 fix (per both reviewers' identical recommendation)**: kept `record_deviation`'s narrow reset scope, but moved the "is this stale reason still valid" judgment into `coverage_check.py` itself — the only place with visibility into the actual `no_activity`/`crossed` facts. New `signals_db.clear_system_reason(deviation_id, prefix)` resets one row but only if `reason_by='system' AND reason LIKE prefix+'%'`, a double guard enforced in SQL (not just caller logic) so it can never touch a human-authored reason — verified adversarially by the confirmation review (20 attack combinations, all human rows survived). `coverage_check.py`'s `SELECT reason, reason_by` moved above the `no_activity` branch so the clear-when-stale logic also covers the `no_activity=False` "wrong outcome" case, which the original code never checked against a stale prior reason at all. `AUTO_RESOLVED_REASON_PREFIX`/`AUTO_VERIFIED_REASON_PREFIX` added as shared constants (signals_db.py and coverage_check.py respectively, the former also imported by coverage_registry.py's 2 read-side `LIKE` queries) so the write/read sides can't desync on a future text edit.

**Tests**: 2 regression tests in `tests/test_coverage_check_price_action.py` (`..._survives_a_rerun_that_still_qualifies`, `..._clears_when_rerun_finds_a_real_problem`), both mutation-verified for real (temporarily reverting each half of the fix makes the corresponding test fail, reproducing the exact real symptom — confirmed by actually reverting and rerunning, not just claimed). Full suite: 107/107 (`test_coverage_check_price_action.py` + `test_coverage_check.py` + `test_coverage_report_summary.py`).

**Production repair**: all 7 stranded rows (`coverage_deviations` ids 154, 155, 156, 161, 163, 164, 165, all `check_date=2026-08-14`) repaired via a real `scripts/coverage_check.py --date 2026-08-14` rerun — confirmed 0 unexplained afterward, all 7 carry a genuine per-ticker `'Auto-verified:'` reason. `trading_incidents` id=9 resolved via `signals_db.resolve_incident()` with the full 2-round history recorded.

**Fixed 2026-08-17**: `already_human_explained`'s check only recognized `reason_by=='user'`, missing `reason_by='streamlit'` (written by `pages/14_Coverage.py`'s inline Explain action) — a Streamlit-entered human reason could be silently overwritten by the auto-explain. See this file's top ✅ entry for the fix.

## [live-trading][security] Accepted risk 2026-08-17 (evening) — HANDOFF `exit_pending` reminder-loop gap: user's call, no fix planned ✅ (residual risk accepted, not fixed)
Found 2026-08-16 (paired review of the `check_drought_handoff` `current_price` fix). `signals_notify.check_drought_handoff`'s `exit_pending` write (Case B, ~line 2476) omits `target_price`/`last_reminder_at`, unlike the other 2 `exit_pending` producers in the file — so a HANDOFF-triggered drought-position close that doesn't confirm filled within the initial poll window (`_GAP_FILL_POLL_ATTEMPTS`) gets exactly one Slack message ("drought HANDOFF exit order placed, waiting for fill confirmation") and then no further reminder nags, unlike every other pending-exit type.

Under normal operation this is harmless: `check_own_sell_fills` runs every poll cycle, unconditionally, and once it holds the real `order_id` there's no ambiguity — it closes the position and posts a confirmation the moment Schwab confirms the fill. The gap only matters if the poll loop itself isn't running or succeeding (daemon down, a Schwab API outage) — the exact scenario that produced 2 real incidents the same evening this was discussed (SOXS automated-buy failure, RETL SL-placement failure + 3-day fill-detection gap, both incidents #10/#11 in `trading_incidents`). In that scenario, HANDOFF goes silent with no signal anything's stuck, unlike the normal trailing-exit reminder loop which would keep nagging and make the stall visible.

**Why not fixed**: naively adding the missing `target_price`/`last_reminder_at` fields to match the other 2 producers would introduce a NEW live bug — `_exit_pending_blocks`'s `reason_labels` dict has no `'HANDOFF'` key and is dereferenced unconditionally, so a HANDOFF reminder render would raise a KeyError. A real fix needs a design decision first (should HANDOFF nag at all, what should the message say), not a quick patch.

**User's call, 2026-08-17 (evening)**: "I'll survive" — accepting the residual risk as-is rather than prioritizing the design decision + fix. Revisit only if a HANDOFF exit actually gets stuck unconfirmed for real (would surface via the broader "no proactive alert for a real position with no expected protective state" gap already flagged in the pending_buys.order_id KEY item, docs/backlog_cache.md) — not on a schedule.

## [live-trading][security] Resolved 2026-08-17 (evening) — one-brokerage-account-per-ticker blast-radius containment: directional call revised, node-level shared-capital mechanism confirmed unnecessary ✅
**History**: original 2026-08-09 call was strict 1-ticker-per-margin-account containment against a rogue algo draining shared cash/buying power, with node-level shared-capital self-policing explicitly deferred (reasoning: initial rollout was small/bounded enough not to need it). **Superseded 2026-08-17**: user confirmed the design has fundamentally changed — multi-ticker sharing on a real margin account is now the accepted design. Confirmed live at the time: `brokerage` (`cash_settlement_type='margin'`, `margin_capable=True`, `trading_enabled=True`) runs 3 real `state='live'` tickers (AGQ wl=203, ETHU wl=201, JNUG wl=205, $6,000 each, $18,000 total real capital) sharing one account's cash/buying-power pool.

**Real question raised**: does the deferred node-level shared-capital safeguard need to be built now that the "small bounded scope" reasoning no longer applies? **Answer, worked through with the user: no — the system is already doubly self-policing, structurally, with no dedicated mechanism needed.**

1. **Sizing is always conservatively bounded per-node.** Every BUY's target notional comes from `signals_helpers._last_sale_recovery(node)` — that ticker's OWN compounded last-sale proceeds, or its own `starting_notional_override`. A node never requests "however much the account has available," only its own modest, pre-determined amount. Two tickers racing near-simultaneously are each asking for their own bounded slice, not competing for an unbounded pool.
2. **The real-time buying-power check is the final ground-truth backstop regardless.** `schwab_client.get_leveraged_buying_power` (checked via `schwab_safety.check_order` on every real order, core or add-on) fetches Schwab's live account balance fresh on every call — no local caching — and its own docstring confirms `buyingPower` already nets out capital committed to resting orders in real time. So even a same-moment cross-ticker race can't overspend: worst case is a blocked order (missed trade) when true capacity has already been consumed by a sibling, never an actual overcommit. A theoretical rounding-level overshoot on the sizing side (layer 1) would still be caught by this check (layer 2).
3. **Broker-side enforcement is a further backstop.** Schwab itself enforces margin limits at execution — a genuine overcommit that somehow slipped past both local checks would still be rejected broker-side, not silently filled.

No dedicated node-level shared-capital mechanism needed. Closed as "no gap, verified by design," not "deferred/not built" — the original 2026-08-09 framing (deferred pending small scope) is now moot since the actual mechanism (bounded sizing + real-time capacity check) was already sufficient all along, independent of ticket count/scope.
